`watermark_unknown` (where the link stands against the boundary; `boundary_omitted` is `watermark_ahead`
with the asked answer off the page, judged on the page's own window), what the link holds now — or what sharing would publish
while unshared — (`new_turns` after the watermark not included, `published_turns` on the page,
`earlier_turns` older ones the page leaves out, `image_count`), and what sharing or updating publishes
(`update_image_count`, `update_new_image_count` on turns the link does not show yet,
`update_earlier_turns`). It is counted with the dialog's existing algorithm (an image count is each
turn's anchors' and citations' images, deduplicated per turn — an upper bound on what the page shows)
over the same window the public page serves: every set involved is a prefix of the conversation's
completed jobs in the canonical `(created_at, id)` order, sized in one SQL aggregate bounded to the
conversation by `idx_global_jobs_conversation`, and the page's window of each prefix (at most two) is
read backwards along that index under a `LIMIT`. The watermark resolves as the public read resolves it
(a keyset on that job, or the `created_at <=` interval when it is gone). A boundary or watermark that
does not resolve is reported, never refused; a library the sharer can no longer read on any counted
turn is the share's own 404, so no number is ever given for a page that would 404 (the same rule
the dialog met before the endpoint existed: the conversation read it paged through refuses such a
conversation too, so the dialog reads exactly as it did). The dialog gives no number — only the sentence
naming both attached images and personal-memory excerpts "(本次未能统计数量)" — when the endpoint fails or
answers malformed, when the asked answer no longer resolves, when the link's watermark cannot be placed
(`watermark_unknown`), or when the personal-memory disclosure cannot be fetched; otherwise it shows the
endpoint's numbers. One deliberate difference from the old in-browser count, for conversations of any
length: a watermark job past its retention stamp is placed where the public page places it (the page
still anchors on its row), so the scope copy reads "behind"/"at" instead of "unknown".
`backend/tests/fixtures/share_counts_golden.json` holds the browser's algorithm and the endpoint to the
same expected numbers.

Images reuse the notebook-scoped token-HMAC alias channel (an alias reverses only against the assets
the public page actually disclosed) under the same `MINERU_RETURN_IMAGES` deployment switch, plus one
global-only gate: the asset's own library must be inside the set this open already re-checked, or the
image 404s — a snapshot spans several libraries, so "the frozen snapshot is the grant" can only hold
per library.

The projection is the notebook-scoped allowlist verbatim (`conversation_public_view`): the public page
shows **no library names**, no addressable id (`notebook_id`/`source_id`/`element_id`/`asset_id`/
`job_id`…), none of the `skipped_notebooks`/`degraded_notebook_ids`/`resolved_notebook_ids` receipts,
and no `reasoning_trace` or `intent`. Turn/reference/snippet/caption bounds are
[the same table](#public-conversation-share-guardrails) — both links share this one projection and one
set of constants. A legacy turn (its answer stored under `response`) still projects; the
`asked_at`/`answered_at`/`evidence_level` it lacks take the projection's existing degradation branch.

Input reuses `ASK_QUESTION_MAX_CHARS=4000` and `CONVERSATION_TITLE_MAX_CHARS=200`; global identifiers
and client request identifiers allow 200 characters. List pagination defaults to 50, capped at 100.
`GLOBAL_ASK_CANDIDATE_LIMIT` defaults to 64 (minimum 1), bounding merged evidence across all notebooks
without cutting the participant list. Candidates must meet `GLOBAL_ASK_MIN_RELEVANCE` (default 0.25,
range 0–1) and `GLOBAL_ASK_RELATIVE_RELEVANCE` times their notebook's best score (default 0.6,
range 0–1). Each notebook with qualified evidence reserves one distinct passage; remaining slots follow
local reciprocal rank weighted by confidence relative to that notebook's best score. Identical text is
deduplicated across notebooks. Raw scores from different retrieval lanes are not compared for global rank.
When the shared `chunk` engine takes its `mix` branch, its final rerank + token cut additionally shares
`min(CHUNK_MMR_K, ceil(CHUNK_MMR_K × CHUNK_FEDERATION_ACTIVE_RESERVE))` seats (4 at the defaults) across the
participating notebooks in the order of each notebook's best qualified passage — the split the exact seats use —
after the graph and exact seats. Seats are dealt one at a time round-robin in that order, so the strongest notebook
takes a seat too, and with more participating notebooks than seats (4 seats at the defaults against up to 8
participants) the notebooks ranked after the last seat get none; within those limits a notebook with qualified
passages keeps a seat the strong notebook's hits would otherwise have taken. The same per-library split holds the
reasoning engine's passage prefix (single-shot synthesis and deep-report drafting, see "Notebooks without a
knowledge graph" below); it is inert with a single participating notebook or a ratio of 0.
Model context is assembled by the shared engine under its existing budgets; global Ask builds no second
context packer of its own.
Unknown model citation markers trigger the shared answer retry rather than retaining unbound claims.
`GLOBAL_ASK_HISTORY_TURNS` defaults to 10 (minimum 0), controlling completed prior turns.
`GLOBAL_ASK_MAX_NOTEBOOKS` defaults to 8 and accepts 1–8: 8 is a product ceiling, not a deployment knob, so a
larger value fails configuration validation and a larger resolved scope is rejected, never silently
truncated. The rejection is actionable rather than a bare limit statement: an `all` scope that resolved past
the ceiling asks for a selection of 8 or fewer, because a caller that never sent a scope — an MCP client
above all — cannot narrow one. The browser keeps this from happening: when a user can read more than 8
notebooks it pre-selects the 8 with the most sources and leaves the selection editable up to 8, and
otherwise selects all of them. `GLOBAL_ASK_MAX_CONCURRENT` defaults to 4 (minimum 1)
per process, including admissions in progress; a full service rejects new work for retry and contributes to
the PostgreSQL pool budget warning. Shutdown cancels workers and waits at most
`GLOBAL_ASK_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 5, greater than 0).
`GLOBAL_ASK_RETRIEVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 30, greater than 0) is the phase budget of ONE federated
retrieval call rather than an absolute instant for the whole job: a `reasoning` run gets a fresh budget per
retrieval round, and the model calls between rounds do not consume it.
`GLOBAL_ASK_NOTEBOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 5, greater than 0) is the per-notebook budget, and it starts
when that notebook actually issues its database query — queueing and waiting for an execution slot do not
count, so a notebook that never issued a query is never described as having timed out.
Participating notebooks retrieve concurrently, bounded by `GLOBAL_ASK_RETRIEVAL_CONCURRENCY`
(default 4, range 1–8) across the whole process, so the retrieval phase is no longer the sum of its
libraries. That bound is one process-level shared executor, and the fair share is divided by the number of
IN-FLIGHT FEDERATED CALLS (slots divided by in-flight calls, recomputed on every top-up): a `reasoning` job
federates several times at once, so dividing by jobs would hand it the whole pool and leave its own remaining
legs queued until the phase expired. Receipt order and evidence selection follow the resolved participant
order, never completion order, so the same question over the same notebooks yields the same answer.
There are exactly four skip reason codes: `timeout` (the per-notebook budget expired or the database
cancelled the statement), `saturated` (no connection could be leased in the remaining budget, so the query
never ran), `queue_deadline` (the phase budget expired while the notebook was still queued, having issued no
query at all) and `unavailable` (everything else).
SQL execution and connection-pool acquisition use remaining deadlines. Database transport failures can
outlast the server-side SQL timeout; this is not a hard wall-clock guarantee under broken network I/O.
Native ANN calls cannot be forcibly
interrupted; overdue results are discarded before hydration/synthesis. Shared query rewriting and one query
embedding run before this phase under existing model-service timeouts; these are not whole-answer deadlines.
The cold-load guard treats every participant alike, the first library included: a LARGE notebook's leg may
only borrow an already-warm scale index and never cold-loads a shared index, ANN handle or whole-library
vector matrix, so one cross-notebook question cannot evict the warm indexes the single-notebook path depends
on. Authority is unchanged throughout: hydrated candidates outside the frozen list are still removed before
scoring.
Where semantic recall is unavailable, bounded lexical recall plus candidate-only vector scoring applies,
including its cross-language limitation. `skipped_notebooks` contains
`{notebook_id, reason}` receipts in both jobs
and answers; MCP exposes both lists in `coverage`. Model original-text projection reuses
`CHUNK_ANSWER_BUDGET_CHARS` rather than introducing a second truncation setting. Oversized chunks are
omitted whole, so evidence budgets do not promise a citation or context slot for every notebook.
`CHUNK_FEDERATION_ENABLED=0` is the federation's rollback switch. It does not return global Ask to a
single-library short circuit: the run degrades to a ONE-LEG federation that searches the first library only —
visibly worse, but still an answer with receipts.

The MCP `ask` tool reaches this engine when its `notebooks` argument names 2-8 notebooks (or its
`conversation_id` starts with `gconv-`); it requires only the `ask` tier and runs the whole job inside
one synchronous call (see "Ask over MCP" below for the routing, clarification and paging contract).
`mode` is `reasoning` (default) or `chunk`; the former `retrieval_effort` argument is gone. A
`reasoning` call runs the understanding pass once in-call, auto-confirms a clear question, and for
an ambiguous one creates nothing durable and returns
`{"status": "needs_clarification", "intent_token", "intent", "understanding_ms", "next_step"}`
instead of a job. Reasoning-trace steps page independently through `trace_offset` into a nested
`trace: {steps, offset, next_offset, total}` (each step keeps kind/summary/duration plus a capped,
explicitly flagged slice of its detail). `next_answer_offset`, `next_citation_offset` and
`next_coverage_offset` continue independent answer, citation and coverage pagination. Coverage
retains complete counts; skipped/degraded notebook lists continue together using `coverage_offset`.
A partially failed answer reports its citation-check summary at `coverage.citation_check`, each
failed citation carries `verification`, and no anchor output is added; `read_reference` answers a
flagged citation with a tool error carrying the same sentence the HTTP drill-down uses, and the
citation's stored `quoted_span` is what the answer read.
Citation metadata can be visibly compressed under the shared MCP budget;
`read_reference` exposes `next_offset` for the complete original text. Answer pages, identifiers and
continuation cursors must not be silently truncated. Results include `/ask?conversation_id=...`.
`list_notebooks` accepts `offset`/`query` and returns `total`/`next_offset`; discovery searches the complete
live allowlist rather than treating its first page as the global universe.

## Product Flow

The outer page is a notebook collection/library (KG-native pipeline):

1. Click `＋ 新建` — the app creates an `Untitled notebook` and enters it immediately (no dialog).
2. Upload PDF, Markdown, DOCX, PPTX, CSV, XLSX, or legacy binary XLS sources (multipart). The authenticated system configuration returns one sanitized parser-capability registry that drives upload validation and the supported-format hints in the import UI; endpoints, paths, credentials, and raw errors never leave the server. The routing pipeline itself (ordered self-hosted MinerU → MinerU public cloud → built-in fallback, execution boundary, availability) is deliberately not surfaced to users — they only see which formats are supported. Selection remains automatic, and a configured self-hosted path is never silently replaced by public cloud.
3. Backend (async background job): structured Markdown parse → chunking + embeddings — chunk-native Q&A is ready as soon as the source finishes processing.
4. **KG extraction is conditional** (see [KG extraction trigger](#kg-extraction-trigger)): on ingest it runs only when the notebook already has a KG, or when `KG_AUTO_EXTRACT=true`. `KG_JOB_CONCURRENCY` controls concurrent source jobs; every extraction model call is admitted by the system model scheduler for the service bound to the `kg_extract` workload, so the service's TOML `max_concurrency` remains the only model-capacity limit. The new source is then incrementally fused into the unified KG.
5. Knowledge objects are stored in `knowledge_objects` + `knowledge_relations` with element-level evidence bindings.
6. Hybrid retrieval (bi-gram keyword + float32 matrix semantic) feeds KG-native Q&A: answers contain sentence-level `[k_i]` citations, support multi-turn conversations, and expand via 1-hop KG neighbours.
7. Unified KG aggregates concepts across documents; pending cross-document merges can be confirmed or rejected.

Inside a notebook:

- Header: the editable notebook title stays compact by itself; the notebook description is shown in the Ask welcome state when no conversation is active, and toolbar actions keep their labels intact across desktop widths.
- Left column: user-imported source files with live parse-status (green = `extracted` only; others shown in amber while processing) plus per-source anomaly badges graded by consequence (red for integrity problems such as a parse failure, amber for retrieval-only problems such as partially unanalyzed content; neutral pending states like 待补全 appear only in the source detail view), detail previews, delete actions, and retrieval-scope checkboxes shared by Ask and new Deep Reports. Source detail fetches and renders a bounded 40-element page (the API caps a request at 100), loads earlier/later pages on demand, and resolves a citation target to its containing page, so opening a large document does not hydrate or mount every element. Pages follow the document's reading order at any size (`created_at`, then the element index -- a document past 9 999 elements included; see [Operations](./operations.md#sources-past-9-999-elements-derived-data-built-out-of-order)). The element list is a **reading view**, not a record dump: elements flow as one document without per-element cards; a slim divider (`第 N 页` / `幻灯片 N` / `工作表 X`, derived from element metadata) is inserted only where consecutive elements change page, slide, or sheet; heading elements render as real headings (h3–h5 by parser level); the parser's `location_label` (`PDF p.1 block 3`, `DOCX paragraph 12`, …) is never shown — it remains the citation coordinate for Ask/report evidence and citation jumps still scroll to and flash the target element. A type tag appears only for element types whose body shape does not speak for itself (speaker notes, image captions, knowhow cells); paragraphs, headings, tables, formulas, images, code, list items, slide text and table rows carry no tag, and table rows show their row number (`第 N 行`, `表 T 第 N 行` for DOCX tables) instead. Rules live in `frontend/app/source-element-display.ts`. Every user-facing source count uses this visible imported-source set and excludes hidden `memory` / `knowhow` projection sources. Network source search is disabled for now.
- Main column: four tabs — **问答** (Ask), **知识库** (Knowledge), **记忆** (Memory), and **深度报告** (Deep Report). Ask provides grounded Q&A with clickable `[k_i]` sentence citations, two built-in retrieval modes, multi-turn conversations, a live expandable reasoning trace, and feedback. Hovering a question or answer reveals its time below the bubble/card; clicking pins it until the next outside click. Questions use the persisted browser-submission instant, while answers use the authoritative answer-write instant returned as `AskResponse.answered_at` (legacy payloads are projected from `answers.created_at`). Browser-local formatting shows time only today, weekday plus time elsewhere in the current Monday-based week, date plus time outside that week (never both weekday and date), omits the year within the current year, and includes it for other years. Conversation history uses a single-row `历史 N` entry in the Ask header plus an expandable manager; the adjacent `+` starts a new session directly. It is ordered and timestamped by sub-second latest activity, and a submitted first turn appears immediately and remains reopenable while the model answer is still running—even if the user switches sessions before `started` arrives. Terminal history summaries refresh for the active notebook independently of which session owns the answer panel; same-notebook refresh callers converge on the newest request. The composer and mode controls remain disabled while the selected notebook/session's latest detail is loading. Knowledge browses and governs dynamic object types. Memory shows only the current user's private records bound to this notebook. Deep Report exposes the two-stage report lifecycle, outline review, progress, export, cancellation, and deletion. In Ask, `Enter` submits, `Shift+Enter` keeps a newline, and while a model response is running the input/mode controls are locked while the send button becomes an interrupt control. **There is one stop style, shared by the notebook Ask and Global Ask** (the rule, the discriminator and the notice copy live only in `frontend/app/stopped-turn.tsx`): stopping **before any process output** — during question understanding, while the submission has not returned, or while the trace holds only the `intent`/`start` preamble steps — returns the question to the input and leaves no record in the transcript; stopping **after retrieval/reasoning output is on screen** keeps that turn in the transcript (question, the trace so far, and the 「已停止回答」 notice), does not return the question, offers 「编辑问题」 to put it back into the input, and **the next submission replaces the record**. The notebook Ask's stopped record lives only in page memory (the backend persists nothing visible for a cancelled question) and is gone after a reload; Global Ask's stopped job is durable, is still the conversation's newest turn after a reload, and is still replaced by the next submission. Both surfaces give the same transient notices when a stop lands before any process output — 「已取消问题理解」, 「已返回修改问题」, 「已中断回答」 (the notebook Ask through the page toast, Global Ask through a self-clearing status line above its composer); a stop after process output gets no extra notice, because the record left in the transcript says it. A transport disconnect stops delivery to that client only; navigation, refresh, or transport loss leaves the detached Ask job running and it may persist its final answer. Clicking interrupt is a distinct cancellation action: the client calls `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask/jobs/{job_id}/cancel`, which sets the backend cancellation event so the worker/LLM path stops and does not save a cancelled final answer. If clicked before the first `started` event is readable, the client restores the draft immediately but keeps that run's transport only long enough to obtain its job id, cancels that job, then aborts it. The workspace remains two columns and has no fixed Studio sidebar.
- Knowledge Graph opens as a full-screen overlay: object-level KG nodes (Concept / Claim / Formula / Procedure) with type-specific shapes, edge relationship labels, multi-select type filters, and a type-grouped side panel that focuses the canvas on selection. Opening it from an Ask knowledge-object citation deep-links to the exact node: if the node is outside the bounded high-degree core, the client overlays its bounded one-hop neighborhood from the citation's real source notebook, including a mounted base notebook; graph-BFS anchors retain that owner id. Browser reads remain authorized by the active notebook, while the backend validates or resolves the object only within its effective participant set and internally proxies mounted-base neighborhood/detail/context reads; mounting a public base never grants direct notebook membership. Raw cited Concept ids are resolved by the neighbors endpoint to a canonical `focus_id` through a single-id cluster lookup, while their raw object id is retained for context reads instead of querying the synthetic graph id from `knowledge_objects`. If a large notebook has no folded viz artifact, the endpoint explicitly reports that location is unavailable instead of entering the full cluster-map fallback, and the client leaves no impossible pending focus. That is no longer a brief "still building" window: a serving process refuses to build a large notebook's viz artifact at all — neither on the request thread nor on a background daemon, because either way it materializes every object, every relation and the whole cluster map inside the API process. The artifact is published only by a scale index build: a manual one, or the off-peak one a concept rebuild queues — which happens only when that notebook still qualifies for automatic indexing (the feature is enabled, no build is already running or queued, the notebook is too large to copy, and its index is missing, merely suggested, or stale), and a concept rebuild re-arms that evaluation so a second rebuild in the same server process is not silently skipped. A concept rebuild leaves the previous folded graph serving as stale until such a build publishes, and a stale graph is served from the warm cache rather than re-read from disk on every request. `GET .../unified-kg` therefore answers a large notebook with no artifact as `viz_building: false` plus `viz_unavailable: true` (the backend makes the two mutually exclusive, so the client never ranks them), and the graph canvas renders a fourth state — 「库规模较大，图谱预览将在下一次索引构建后可用」 — instead of the misleading 「没有匹配的节点」. The citation-focus notice points at that same index build rather than promising a retry. The side panel renders source excerpts as structured evidence cards so long titles, locations, formulas, and mixed Chinese/English text stay inside the panel; excerpts whose source element type is `formula` use the shared block KaTeX renderer instead of showing raw commands.
- A **KG quality analysis** panel (batch 1 of 4; see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-kg-analysis-view-design.md`) opens from a `图谱分析` button inside the Knowledge Graph view header, next to `图谱 Schema`. Its report reads require only notebook read access. The body of the panel is a **findings list** (see `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-kg-analysis-findings-design_zh.md`) in four zones. **待处理** (to handle) is ordered by severity (high/medium/low — used for ordering and colour only, never summed into a score), then impact, then the finding's key; each finding names its rule in interface words (疑似内容错配 / 疑似重复导入 / 疑似解析残缺 / 疑似没合并的同名概念 / 没建立关联的内容), what it points at (a source, two sources, a concept group or the whole library), the numbers its criterion used with representative names, how many knowledge objects it affects, and the suggested action. **需要开发处理** (needs development) lists only defects measured on this library that only a code fix can remove — today, concept groups that differ only by spaces/hyphens and were not merged — stating the symptom and its size, with no button; once the running code fixes such a defect but the library's published result still predates the fix (`dev_items[].status` = `fixed_pending_update`), the item says "已修复，更新分析后生效" (still no button — `更新分析` sits in the header). **诊断数据** (diagnostics) holds every earlier statistics block, collapsed by default, with per-metric freshness unchanged; its `先看结论` block no longer has the "source review" card (replaced by 疑似内容错配, together with the extra source-profile request it made), and its topic-structure signal now reports the main content (the largest connected piece of related knowledge objects): what share of knowledge objects it holds and how many topics it contains, plus how many islands exist and how many sources they come from. **已通过** (passed) has one line per rule and keeps "checked, nothing found" (✓, with how much was checked), "could not check" (–, with the reason; not a pass — a rule that could not run completely and listed nothing is also –) and "marked as normal" (undoable) apart; concept groups the user already judged to be different also appear there. The header states which generation the report was built at, whether it matches the current graph, and how many findings disappeared / persist / are new since the last build, with the names of the ones that disappeared (or that this build is not compared, when the rule version changed or a rule could not run completely, followed by the counts of each rule that is still comparable). When the report is behind the data each finding carries "基于变更 #N"; a finding already acted on but not yet re-analysed carries "已处理，更新后核验" with the reason the read side recognised (source deleted, being parsed or re-parsed, merge confirmed, relink has run) and stays listed. Editors get action entries beside each finding, all of which go through the existing entry points and backend permissions: `打开来源核对` opens the source detail on top of the panel (the panel stays open, and focus returns to the button when the detail closes); `删除来源…` opens the existing delete confirmation unchanged, with "不可撤销，先打开来源核对" beside the button (for a duplicate import only beside the copy suggested for deletion, keeping the one with more objects); `重新解析…` first shows a confirmation saying the model will be called again and the source's current knowledge items replaced, then uses the same batch reparse as the health check (never offered for promotion sources), and the panel follows that source by id until that run ends (off the source list's current page too) and refetches the findings and the overview as it moves; from the confirmation until the follow judges that run over, `重新解析…` on every finding that references the source, and `重新解析` in the source detail, are disabled with "已提交重新解析，等待完成" written in place (stale terminal reads while the job is still queued do not release them; the follow ending — the run finished, the source deleted, the poll timed out, the notebook switched or the panel closed — does), so the reparse cannot be submitted twice; `去待确认合并` closes the panel and locates the group in the knowledge-graph view's pending merges (or says the queue does not hold the group yet); `补上关联` runs the existing background job and writes "新增 N 条关联，还剩 M 个没有关联的知识条目" as a notice at the top of the to-handle zone (by then the finding has either moved or lost its button), and when it already ran and nothing new arrived since, the finding leaves the to-handle list for the diagnostics zone with no button: "补上关联已经跑过，剩下 M 个没有可自动补上的关联；集中在某几个来源的，见疑似解析残缺" (not listed or counted under passed); `标为正常` moves a finding to the passed zone. While a background task runs the matching buttons are disabled with the reason beside them, and the panel refetches the findings once an action completes. Read-only members and mirrored libraries see the same findings and evidence without any action button or `标为正常`. The `生成分析` / `更新分析` button sits in the header. It reuses `POST /notebooks/{id}/unified-kg/rebuild`, the existing confirmation and per-notebook single-flight background job, and `job_id`-matched completion polling; it does not re-extract sources, and the report refreshes automatically when the job finishes. It is disabled with "已与当前图谱一致，无需更新" when the report matches the current graph, disabled with an explanation when only an unknowable merge generation remains (an ordinary update cannot change it), and enabled with "合并规则已更新，需要更新一次" when the merge result was built under older merge rules (the empty version record left by deleting the knowledge graph does not count). A library that has not produced findings since the upgrade shows a grey "升级后还没生成", not a red alarm. `GET /notebooks/{id}/kg-analysis` returns object-type composition, merge-convergence rates broken down **per object type** (concept/claim/formula/procedure computed separately — mixing them dilutes the true concept convergence rate roughly 3x), the topic-community list, and cross-community edges for an overview map. Each board in that list carries a `board_key` beside its `id`: the `id` is reminted every time a partition is published, while `board_key` is the board's identity across rebuilds -- carried forward when a new board and an old one are each other's best match and share at least half of their combined members (Jaccard >= 1/2), freshly minted otherwise. Rebuilds warm-start from the published partition, so a board stays where it is unless the graph itself moves it; a forced rebuild is still a warm start (see `docs/operations.md` for the one-time re-partition and `recluster_kg --cold-partition`). `GET /notebooks/{id}/kg-analysis/sources` paginates per-source profiles, ordered by how sparsely (default) or densely each source connects to the notebook's mainstream communities. Like every other user-facing source count, source profiles cover only the visible imported-source set: objects belonging to hidden `memory` / `knowhow` projection sources are excluded when the profiles are precomputed, so those internal titles never reach the report and never distort the sparse-connection ranking. Orphan references (a `source_id` whose source row no longer exists) are deliberately *kept* and flagged `source_missing` — that is a diagnostic signal, not a hidden source. Both endpoints only read three precompute product tables (`kg_community_edges`, `kg_source_profiles`, `kg_analysis_artifacts`) that `POST /unified-kg/rebuild` writes wholesale in the **same** transaction that publishes the community graph itself, so a report can never pair recast boards with the previous ledger; they never scan the full object/edge/cluster tables online. Every reported number carries the generations it was built at and how far behind the live graph it is, per metric rather than as one page-level staleness banner. There are **two independent generation lines**: `kg_mutation_seq` (object/relation writes) and `cluster_mutation_seq` (merge results). Cluster writes deliberately leave `kg_mutation_seq` untouched, so the four artifacts computed from `concept_clusters` (size histogram, largest clusters, cross-community edges, source profiles) also carry `built_at_cluster_seq`/`cluster_seq_behind` and go stale on a merge-only write; `relation_provenance` reads only the relation table, carries no cluster stamp, and is deliberately not invalidated by a merge — recomputing it would mean a needless full relation scan. The two board-dependent artifacts (cross-community edges, source profiles) stamp the merge generation **their board partition was built on**: an integer when the same round rebuilt the partition, and an explicit `null` when the round only backfilled the ledger (the partition is then whatever the library already had, and nothing records which merge generation that was). `stale` is therefore tri-state — `true` when a line is definitely behind, `false` when both are aligned, and `null` when the merge generation is unknowable; `null` is not `false`, and the panel shows it as its own caveat instead of "up to date". The product ledger has its own freshness gate over both lines, independent of the community layer's, so a library that already has communities backfills the ledger on its next ordinary rebuild instead of requiring a forced one. The topic-board list itself is judged by the **same** tri-state rule, not a second one: its KG line is `community_seq`, and its merge line reads the very stamp described above — that stamp *is* the record of which merge generation the partition was built on, and the two board-dependent ledger rows are voided in the same transaction that remints board ids, so a present row always describes the current partition. A merge-only write therefore makes the board list report "merge generation unknowable" exactly when the two artifacts drawn from that partition report it, instead of claiming "up to date" just because `kg_mutation_seq` happened not to move. The action refreshes derived analysis state only. The view gives findings with evidence and suggestions, but it carries out no remedy itself: it only takes the user to the existing entry points — deleting or reparsing a source, confirming a merge, relinking — each with its own confirmation and backend permission; its one write of its own is "mark as normal" (a dismissal).
- **Findings list (backend contract; design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-kg-analysis-findings-design_zh.md`).** The same precompute that builds the topic boards also computes a rule-based list of findings, each with the numbers its rule used and at most five sample names, and publishes it in the boards' own transaction as a sixth ledger kind, `findings` (required; dependent on the merge result but not on the board partition, so a board recast does not void it and the backfill path stamps an integer merge generation), plus the detail table `kg_analysis_findings`. Rules (`rules_version` 1): **F1 off-topic source** — a source with at least 10 concept canonicals of which fewer than 5% also occur in another source that is not its duplicate partner (severity high; suggests deleting the source; two duplicated wrong files become one row); **F2 duplicate import** — concept-canonical Jaccard ≥ 0.45 between two sources, concepts present in more than 30 sources left out (medium; suggests deleting the copy with fewer objects, equal counts keep the earlier import); **F3 parse damage** — any of: fragmented names (at least 10% and at least 5 of a source's concept canonical names contain a run of ≥ 4 single-character tokens), low relations (relations per object below 0.5 × the library median, judged only for sources with at least 20 objects), isolated objects (share above max(3 × the library median, 10%) and at least 20) (medium; suggests reparsing; an F3 source is not also reported as F1); **F4 unmerged same-name concepts** — canonicals whose names collide once every separator is removed, in at least two spellings that differ beyond whitespace/hyphen/underscore, not rejected or deferred by a stored merge decision (decisions match by every member's seeds in both merge seed spaces — the old v1 rule and the current v2 rule, a `~v1:<seed>` the decision recompute kept reading as that v1 seed — hidden members included; a merged knowledge object kept on its old seed is not an F4 subject itself) (low; suggests the pending-merge review); **F5 isolated content** — usable objects whose canonical has no non-self-loop relation, one row per library (low; suggests relinking). The narrow half of same-name groups (spellings that differ only in whitespace/hyphen/underscore — the seed-normalisation defect S1) is a count with up to three examples in a "needs development" item, never a row; each `dev_items[]` entry carries `status`: `fixed_pending_update` (fixed, applied by the next "update analysis") while the library's published merge is still in the old seed space (`unified_kg_state.concept_seed_version` below the code's), else `open`. Caps are explicit and never silent: at most `MAX_PERSISTED_FINDINGS=500` rows per rule (the ledger records `total` / `persisted` / `truncated` per rule), at most `KG_FINDINGS_ROWS_MAX=5000` detail rows per library (the write entry fails hard above it), and F2 candidate-pair generations capped by `KG_FINDINGS_MAX_CANDIDATE_PAIRS` (recorded as truncated). Display and sample names come only from visible sources' own objects, so a canonical name taken from a knowhow object never reaches the report. Each build inherits `first_seen_*` from the previous detail and records a comparison (resolved / persisting / new, with up to 20 resolved names) unless the rules version changed or either side truncated or could not run a rule. The findings payload also carries the connected-component structure (giant-component object share, island components and the sources they come from); the two partition numbers (boards inside the giant component, boards that are exactly one component) are in the board-dependent `community_edges` payload. A findings row built by other rules is stale (`rules_version` is its third freshness line), so a rules change makes "update analysis" recompute. Every ledger payload carries a `ledger_contract` stamp; when every present row predates it, a missing `findings` row reads as `upgrade_pending` (grey: not generated since the upgrade) instead of `unexpected`, and the next ordinary rebuild backfills it. Relinking records a durable `relink_attempted` mark at the `kg_mutation_seq` it finished on, also when it linked nothing; when something other than the relink itself moved the knowledge graph during the run (the maintenance slot does not hold back ordinary ingestion), the mark records the generation the run started on instead, so content the run never read keeps relinking available; F5 leaves the open list while that mark is at the current generation (running it again cannot link more). "Mark as normal" is the user's decision and rebuilds do not clear it: a publication removes a dismissal only when its subject no longer exists (the source of an F1/F3 finding, or either source of an F2 pair, was deleted); F4/F5 dismissals are never removed at publication, and nothing is removed for a rule that was skipped or truncated in that build — so a dismissal survives a knowledge-graph delete awaiting re-extraction or a source being reparsed, and the same finding reads as dismissed again after the next update. Dismissals otherwise go only when undone or when the notebook is deleted. The overview's `merge_code` `{stored, current, matches}` compares the merge code version stored at the last merge with the running code; `matches` is `null` when nothing was merged yet (for example after deleting the knowledge graph), which never reads as "merge rules updated".
- The Analysis menu itself contains only the promotion queue (admin), publish / unpublish public knowledge base (admin), and edge-review queue. Dashboard and the full-screen Knowledge Graph are separate top-toolbar actions; 「图谱 Schema」 is entered from the Knowledge Graph view header rather than a separate top-toolbar action. Editors also get **删除知识图谱** in the Knowledge Graph view's 「图谱处理」 group: after a confirmation it deletes the notebook's source-derived graph in the background while keeping sources and their parsed content, keeps the other graph-processing actions disabled while it runs, and reports the outcome next to the button (contract in the KG delete bullet under the KG maintenance endpoints). Administrators manage the global object-type baseline. Notebook owners can inspect the effective baseline, copy-on-write an inherited definition, disable it only in that notebook, or add a notebook-only type; deleting an override restores the global definition. Read-only members see the same effective definitions without write controls. An administrator can switch to the global-baseline view, whose changes affect only notebooks that have not overridden the same type. The panel is laid out in three parts so that "which types exist" and "change one" stay separate: a **scope** row on top (current notebook / global baseline, switchable by admins only) decides which registry is on screen and where a write lands; the **type list** on the left groups rows into pending proposals / active / disabled and shows each type's identifier, display name, field count, and provenance badge (inherited / override / notebook-owned / built-in), with `新增类型` and `从当前笔记本归纳候选类型` docked at the bottom of that column (a proposal does not shadow the inherited type of the same name, so the two occupy separate, separately selectable rows); the **selected type's definition** on the right is read-only until `编辑` swaps it for the form, and a proposal shows its rationale plus approve/reject there. Edit drafts are kept per object type, so switching to another type and back does not lose typing, and the list row carries an unsaved-changes dot. Writes are driven by a receipt: the panel only returns to the read view or clears the create form once the backend write succeeded and the list was reloaded; without a receipt it keeps the input and explains why next to the button. No retired content-generation or derived-rule actions are exposed. The existing notebook analytics view includes separate Memory and Knowhow content-asset cards: Memory metrics are restricted to the signed-in user and current notebook (including for admins), while Knowhow metrics follow notebook read access. The cards show counts, health/recency summaries, and links only; they navigate to the existing Memory and Knowhow pages/editors rather than duplicating a browser or editor.

Knowledge object types have a single source of truth for their display name: the backend `OBJECT_TYPE_LABELS` in `app/domain/extraction_profiles.py` (`app/services/extraction_profiles.py` is a re-export shim), delivered to the client as `KnowledgeTypeCount.label` by `GET /notebooks/{id}/knowledge-types`. Every call site that can reach that API label — the Knowledge browser's type tabs and object entries — renders it directly, so user-defined object types (for example the column names projected from knowhow tables) also show their proper Chinese name. Call sites that only hold an `object_type` string — the citation popover and the knowledge-graph canvas/side panel — fall back to the small built-in front-end table `KG_TYPE_LABELS` in `frontend/app/kg-type-model.ts`; `kg-type-mark.tsx` consumes and re-exports that model for shared rendering. The table is character-for-character identical to the backend constant; `scripts/check_object_type_labels_contract.py` runs inside `scripts/check.sh` as a hard gate that fails the build when the two copies drift. An unknown or custom type is displayed verbatim as its `object_type`, never Title-Cased into invented English. Because both tables are keyed by user-controlled strings, look them up with `Object.hasOwn(...)` rather than bare indexing: `constructor` and `__proto__` resolve through the prototype chain and yield inherited functions/objects instead of a miss.

User-visible labels and displayable backend `user_error(...)` messages follow the [UI vocabulary](./ui-vocabulary.md). Internal identifiers and persisted defaults remain unchanged. Unknown enum values use a neutral label; user-authored object types/field names may be echoed deliberately. Guard implementation and verification belong to [development](./development.md), not the product contract.

Reparse preserves the source row and original file: it replaces source elements/chunks and their embeddings, and removes extraction runs plus source-derived knowledge before rebuilding. Delete performs the same source-derived cleanup, then deletes the source row (cascading source-owned records) and the local file.

Before a newly parsed or reparsed source publishes elements, chunks, embeddings, or source-derived knowledge, ingestion removes high-confidence running-header/footer artifacts. A normalized nonblank `heading`, `paragraph`, or built-in PDF `page_text` must occur on at least 3 represented pages and on at least half of all represented pages, either as the page's first/last textual element or with a parser-explicit `header`, `footer`, `page_header`, or `page_footer` block type; only occurrences after the first are suppressed. Non-boundary copies, tables, formulas, images, code, same-page repetitions, and lower-coverage repetitions remain untouched. Historical rows and external-parser output receive an independent retrieval-time defense: chunks and direct source elements collapse by `(source_id, NFKC + whitespace-folded + case-folded text)` before candidate/result caps, cross-query accumulation, reflection summaries, and final Ask/Report context budgets. The highest-scoring representative wins in ranked paths; exact-section context keeps the first document-order representative. Matching text from different sources is never collapsed because it represents independent provenance. This two-layer rule prevents duplicates from consuming upstream retrieval slots or downstream synthesis slots; it does not silently rewrite or globally deduplicate authored source data.

Visible imported-source counts deliberately differ from physical bookkeeping: hidden Memory/Knowhow projection sources do not appear in the source rail or user-facing counts, but `size.sources`, copy thresholds, storage accounting, and background scheduling retain physical-row semantics. Likewise, `has_unindexed_content` keeps the scale-index update decision true when derived content changed even if the visible imported-source delta is zero.

Scale-index scheduling exposes immediate and off-peak operations. When no build is already running, `when=now` atomically supersedes an older idle entry for the same notebook before claiming the immediate build; a later idle request is preserved, and a worker-start failure restores the displaced entry. Scheduler ticks claim queued notebooks independently, leaving busy follow-ups queued and isolating per-item launch failures. `AskResponse.index_required` remains an answer-time diagnostic snapshot, while the Ask UI observes live `ScaleIndexStatus.exists`; an `index_done` event refreshes the active notebook even after bounded foreground polling stops, so a published index removes that warning from historical answers without rewriting them.

When a notebook's `ScaleIndexStatus.state` is `"queued"`, the status response discloses why the wait is happening rather than a bare "queued" flag: `queue_position` (1-based) and `queue_length` describe standing in the off-peak queue, `queued_at` gives the UTC ISO timestamp the entry was **first** enqueued (re-queuing updates the mode but keeps the original timestamp, so it stays anchored to the same instant as the insertion-order position), `offpeak_in_window` reports whether the server is already inside an idle window, `offpeak_next_start_at` gives the UTC ISO timestamp of the next window when it is not, and `last_build_ms` (0 = unknown) carries the previous build's wall-clock duration so the UI can set expectations. All six fields are optional so older backends degrade gracefully to the pre-existing generic queued copy. A queued notebook that already has a published index also still carries `last_built_at`, so the dashboard card can keep showing "last built X ago" while it waits. `queue_position` is first-enqueue order (derived server-side by sorting on the first-enqueue timestamp, so a worker-start-failure restore cannot silently move it), not wait order — once the off-peak window opens, `_process_idle_queue` starts every queued notebook's build concurrently, so it is not a promise of turn-taking. The frontend composes the disclosed fields into one sentence in the browser's local timezone (`frontend/app/scale-index.ts::queuedScheduleHint`), which reports queue length (when ≥ 2) rather than position for that reason; numeric tiers and internal terminology are never surfaced verbatim. The pending-actions bell also now passes through the underlying `"queued"` state for `type:"index"` items (previously rewritten to `"building"`) and shows a distinct "queued, will build during an idle window" label without a progress percentage.

The notebook workspace hides the global collection top bar and keeps an engineering-console visual treatment. Markdown shown in Ask, reports, Memory, and Knowhow treats a whole-line one-line `$$...$$` as display math even when it is adjacent to prose; wide display equations scroll inside their own content block. Source-detail, knowledge-object, and Knowledge Graph evidence formula views remove full-value Markdown math delimiters before direct KaTeX rendering and show the original text if parsing still fails, so malformed formula input never becomes a blank visualization. Across the three surfaces that render **model-produced text** (Ask answers and Memory cards, deep reports, the public report page) a **single `~` is a literal, not strikethrough**: GFM strikethrough must be written as the spec's `~~text~~`. This is not a style preference — with single tildes pairing, Chinese technical answers routinely put two of them in one paragraph (ranges such as `7~5nm`, `80~90%`, `2~3 周`; approximations such as `~3GHz`), and everything between them is struck through. The Knowhow cell preview deliberately still pairs single tildes: its Markdown-normalization guard reasons from that behavior.

### Reasoning trace details

In the expanded trace, each step's supplementary detail wraps within a bounded column and shows at most two lines by default. Only text that overflows those lines gets a “查看完整内容” control; “收起” restores the preview. Full text is preserved, and the expanded detail scrolls within a bounded height rather than stretching the page. Step duration remains visible beside the detail. Narrow screens place detail and duration below the summary. Overflow is re-evaluated when the container resizes or the detail changes. This presentation rule applies to the shared trace panel, including live and historical Ask traces; it does not change stored trace data or the separate full plugin-argument disclosure.

### Source-selected retrieval scope

The source sidebar starts with every visible imported source selected and offers per-row checkboxes plus `全选` / `清空`. The same current selection is sent to corpus-blind Ask intent preview, Ask execution, and new Deep Report creation. It constrains active-notebook chunks, source elements, KG evidence and relations, graph expansion output, PPR output, and report retrieval; a narrowed scope also excludes hidden Memory/Knowhow projection evidence because those internal sources have no user-facing checkbox. Inside that hidden half the two kinds are scoped differently: Knowhow projections are notebook-wide and reach every member's ceiling, while a Memory projection is private to the user who created it and enters only that user's ceiling, filtered in the read itself. Every entry point freezes a ceiling — a request that omits the scope gets the default one described below — so no Ask, intent precheck, MCP ask or Deep Report retrieves another member's Memory projections through its elements, knowledge-graph objects, relations or graph walks. The ceiling also governs the **second read of knowledge evidence**: when a KG hit enters the answer prompt, its definition, quoted snippet and citation locator are not reused from the recalled evidence but re-queried by object id from the original evidence list, and that re-read passes the same source ceiling whenever the ceiling **binds** the object's library on the run — the ceiling denies everything, the run is a global one or the library carries its own frozen per-library ceiling, the user narrowed the selection, the library's sources changed after the selection was frozen, or the library holds a hidden source the asker may not read (another member's Memory). Otherwise — every source ticked, nothing changed since the freeze, nothing hidden the asker cannot read — the ceiling could not exclude anything, so the re-read runs without it and returns exactly what an unscoped run gets. The verdict is taken once per run and library, at the first re-read of that library, and costs at most one read of its visible sources and three reads bounded by its Memory/Knowhow count. An object may therefore be recalled on an in-scope source while the sentence it contributes and the source its citation points at are always in-scope ones (an occurrence counts only when both the source it names and the source its element actually lives in are in scope); an object left with no in-scope occurrence is dropped whole rather than rendered as a name with no quote behind it. The definition obeys the same ceiling: a concept cluster's fused description is used only when it can be shown that no member of the cluster has an evidence source outside the ceiling or was created from a source outside it (strict — the description is a model fusion of every member and cannot be attributed to any one source; a member whose evidence names no source at all counts as outside). The proof reads at most 2,000 member rows of the cluster in one statement (`NODE_CONTEXT_CLUSTER_MEMBER_PROBE`); a cluster with more members cannot be verified within that budget, so under a binding ceiling its fused description is not used and the definition falls back as for a mixed cluster. The cost of the check does not grow with the cluster (measured on PostgreSQL: 5–9 ms median from 1,000 to 200,000 members, against ~0.5 ms without a ceiling). Without a verified description the first in-ceiling `defines` evidence is used (definers are scanned in relation-id order, at most eight; rejected `defines` relations and deprecated or merged-away definers are skipped before that count, with or without a ceiling, so they neither supply text nor use up the eight), and failing that the quoted snippet. A definer with no evidence contributes only its name, which cannot be attributed to any source, so that fallback is not used under a ceiling. Each procedure step is attributed before it is shown — to the source of the element it cites, or, when that element no longer exists or the step cites none, to the source the object was created from — and a step whose source is out of scope is dropped whole, name included; an in-scope step keeps its name and quoted text. Legacy sibling-procedure steps keep only siblings created from an in-scope source (or recorded with none) that have an evidence item whose element actually lives in an in-scope source, the step text taken from each sibling's first such item; an item that names an in-scope source but points at an element of another one does not count. For an object without a section path the siblings are read in pages of 500 until 500 in-scope siblings are found or 5,000 procedure rows have been read (`NODE_CONTEXT_LEGACY_SIBLING_SCAN`); the object's own step is taken first, so reaching that bound can only leave out other siblings, never the object's own step. Without a ceiling this path keeps its historical arbitrary sample of 500 rows. The object's own section path is the heading path of the source it was created from and is returned only when that source is in scope; its name is kept. The object context endpoint reads the same object context with the **viewer's** readable sources as the ceiling (see `GET .../objects/{object_id}/context`). Mounted reference libraries are separate participants and remain in scope. A participant library other than the active notebook contributes under its own ceiling — **that library's currently visible sources** — so its hidden Memory/Knowhow projections are structurally excluded from the cross-library passage channel rather than filtered out afterwards; the requesting user is usually not a member of a reference library, and that hidden half is scoped to members. Unchecking a reference library removes it from the participant set before any query is issued, so it contributes nothing to any channel.

`AskIntentPreviewRequest`, `AskRequest`, and `ReportCreate` accept an optional top-level `source_scope` object: `{ "mode": "include" | "exclude", "source_ids": string[] }`. `include` admits only listed visible sources from the active notebook; `exclude` admits every visible active-notebook source except those listed. Omitting the field does not mean an unbounded run: every entry point — HTTP `/ask` and `/ask/stream`, the intent precheck, MCP `ask`, extension answer engines and every Deep Report phase — freezes the asker's **default ceiling** instead, through one installation point: the notebook's visible sources plus the asker's own hidden sources (Knowhow projections, and the asker's own Memory projections unless the Memory channel is closed), each mounted library frozen to its visible sources. It binds like an all-selected freeze but is not a user choice: it never narrows the run, no receipt is shown, and a report persists `understanding.source_scope` as null. A deep report created without a scope runs its intent, planning and generation phases under the creator's default ceiling; a persisted selection is re-frozen and used as-is in every phase; an automatic confirmation that refreshes either dimension re-installs the refreshed one inside the ceiling. If the ceiling cannot be read the question or phase fails rather than running without one; a Stop pressed while it is being read cancels it. `exclude` with an empty list is the frontend's compact representation of all currently visible imported sources. At the API boundary, every explicit scope is validated and frozen into an explicit include-list. The server also computes `narrowed` against the current visible-source count and overwrites any submitted value: freezing an all-selected snapshot must not be confused with actually excluding a source. Therefore an all-selected run—including a one-source notebook—keeps conversation history and normal graph/reasoning channels; KG candidate generation also keeps its notebook ANN + lexical union and applies the frozen ceiling while hydrating evidence. Only a genuinely smaller set, a frozen-universe drift, or a producer-supplied explicit allow-list enters the source-restricted KG lexical lane. In that lane `source_index_backfilled=false` is interpreted as “historical completeness unverified”, never “no source rows”: the lexical query evaluates authoritative evidence before `LIMIT`, while `true` uses `knowledge_object_sources` as the fast predicate. New notebooks initialize the empty reverse index as complete and online KG writes maintain it in their existing transactions; offline `backfill-source-index` remains the certification/performance path for historical or imported notebooks. The server privately snapshots the current hidden Memory/Knowhow participant ids for that all-selected run, while a narrowed run excludes them; those ids are neither exposed nor persisted in the public scope object. Both modes retain the frozen snapshot in source-partitioned candidate generation and result checks, so concurrent uploads cannot widen an in-flight run. The snapshot is materialized into an allow-list and pushed below a producer's `LIMIT` whenever it can exclude something — it is *not* enough to *assume* an all-selected snapshot equals the live universe, because that snapshot is neither the producer's universe nor a live set: its hidden half is read for the requesting user while an unfiltered producer reads every member's (only the generated-question scan and its hydration re-derive that owner predicate for themselves), and the equality holds only for the instant it was checked. So it is *proven* instead, once per run and library (the `ceiling_binds` verdict): the run is not narrowed, no Memory was withheld, the live universe still has the frozen fingerprint, and the library holds no hidden source the asker may not read (another member's Memory). Only then do producers of the scope's own notebook read without the list — exactly what an unscoped run reads — and every such read is verified: a row from a source outside the freeze (one that finished after the verdict) flips the verdict for the rest of the run and that call is re-run bound, so it can neither reach the answer nor take a Top-K slot. Narrowed and drifted runs, notebooks holding another member's Memory and every mounted library keep the list, bound as one parameter. A producer-supplied explicit allow-list is likewise *intersected* with the frozen list rather than passed through, because producers enumerate the universe live. What an all-selected snapshot does change is **routing**, not filtering: because it did not narrow anything, the producers that must choose a lane — the lexical corpus-language gate above all — treat it as unrestricted and keep the fast path an unscoped run takes, while still applying the list in SQL. That gate's exemption for source-restricted runs assumes their source predicate bounds the scan; an all-selected predicate spans the whole notebook, so the exemption would reinstate exactly the unbounded probe set the gate exists to prevent. A frozen-universe drift makes the run genuinely bounded again and returns it to the restricted lane. If the current visible-source universe no longer equals an all-selected snapshot, unsafe whole-graph channels are disabled before I/O. That check re-reads the live universe on every call — never cached — as one row: an md5 fingerprint of each half (the visible sources; the asker's hidden sources) in id order, compared with the freeze's own fingerprint. A notebook that is ingesting sources while a question runs can therefore lose the whole-graph, PPR and relation channels for that question (exact lookup keeps running with the ceiling in its probe); this now applies to MCP asks and reports as it always did in the browser. A question whose Memory channel is closed (an agent token without `memory:read`) keeps those channels: the asker's own Memory, withheld from the ceiling, is not drift, and each channel keeps it out by the ceiling itself (see **Retrieval legs under the run's source ceiling** below). At the result boundary a ceiling that **binds** drops a relation or object hit that carries no evidence; a ceiling pushed down (all selected, no drift, nothing hidden the asker cannot read — an own notebook frozen empty included) leaves the boundary exactly as an unscoped run has it: evidence-less hits are kept and the Knowhow cell-object semantic recall runs when the question asks for Knowhow types. That is a change for the browser's all-selected run, which used to drop those hits and skip that recall; it now matches an unscoped MCP or API run. The backend rejects foreign, hidden, or stale source ids with 422. If the effective local scope is empty and no checked reference library holds evidence retrieval can reach, it rejects Ask/intent/report creation with 409 (see the **409 "empty scope"** paragraph below); the browser disables the Ask composer and new-report controls when no library is checked at all, while still allowing existing reports to be viewed. A report persists the resolved public scope in its understanding contract, revalidates it before intent confirmation and generation, and rehydrates the private participant snapshot for planning and drafting.

**A frozen scope never turns off chunk vector recall.** The frozen source list is a **filter**, not a **lane selector**. Whether a library has a chunk ANN (scale index) is a property of the **library**, unrelated to how many sources this request checked, so the chunk lane's degradation test is one and the same guard for scoped and unscoped requests: only a large library (`copyable=false`) or a whole-notebook chunk count above `CHUNK_BRUTEFORCE_MAX_CHUNKS` falls back to bounded FTS lexical candidates. A **small** library with no ANN index still serves a scoped request from the brute-force vector lane **bounded by the allowed sources**: chunk text rows are read for the selected sources only, while the vectors come from the same version-keyed whole-notebook matrix cache an unscoped request uses and are then **masked down to the allowed chunks before scoring**. A scoped request therefore materializes nothing an unscoped one would not, so the "do not materialize everything for a small library" concern does not apply on that path; the masking is what keeps it a filter — both the candidate list and the returned similarity/diversity matrix rows stay a strict subset of the allowed chunks, and excluded content never reaches Top-K selection nor MMR's diversity comparison. The accepted cost is one subset copy per request (an all-selected freeze copies the whole matrix). The `chunk_bruteforce_skipped(large_library_no_ann)` operational event therefore appears only for large/over-threshold libraries, and its `n_chunks` is always the real whole-notebook count, read through the same seq-gated count memo the notebook-open path uses (not a per-allowed-source count, not a candidate count, and never a placeholder). The federated chunk lane's borrow-only leg reports itself as a **different reason** on that same event, `peek_no_warm_ann`, because a large reference library whose index is built and healthy still degrades to bounded FTS whenever that index is not currently resident; there `n_chunks` is a diagnostic value only, since the degradation was decided by the lane rather than by the count. Reading "the list is not `None`" as "this query is bounded, lexical alone will do" was a production defect: every UI-issued question carries a frozen list (an all-selected freeze carries one too), so every library without an index lost chunk semantic recall entirely on the UI path, and a Chinese question against an English corpus returned nothing on the first round. The **routing** question — the `source_restricted` verdict the lexical corpus-language gate reads — is still decided solely by genuine narrowing or post-freeze drift, never inferred from "the list is not `None`".

Retrieval scope has **two independent dimensions**, both shared by Ask intent preview/execution and new Deep Report creation, and both defaulting to fully selected: one checkbox per visible imported source of the active notebook (`source_scope`), and one checkbox per *whole* mounted reference library (`base_scope` — never expanded into the sources inside it). `AskIntentPreviewRequest`, `AskRequest`, and `ReportCreate` accept an optional top-level `base_scope` object alongside `source_scope`: `{ "mode": "include" | "exclude", "notebook_ids": string[] }`. `include` admits only the listed mounted libraries; `exclude` admits every mounted library except those listed; omitting the field lets every mounted library take part, **each through its visible sources only** — a mounted library's Knowhow and Memory projections belong to its own members, so in a single-notebook question they no longer contribute (asking inside that library still uses them). These per-library ceilings are frozen when the question starts and are total: a library mounted after that takes no part. If a mounted library's source list cannot be read in time when a question starts (5 s per library, 10 s for all mounted libraries together), that library takes no part in the answer — it is never searched without its limits — and the answer says which reference library was left out (`AskResponse.skipped_libraries`: `[{notebook_id, name, included: false}]`, name as a snapshot, absent when none; MCP `ask` counts it in `coverage.skipped` and lists it under `coverage.skipped_notebooks`). Asking again normally includes it. `notebook_ids` may name only libraries currently mounted on the active notebook (422 otherwise), and — exactly like `source_scope` — the API boundary freezes every submitted scope, including `exclude` with an empty list, into an explicit include snapshot and recomputes `narrowed` server-side, ignoring any client-supplied value. Freezing matters most for reports: the resolved scope is persisted in the understanding contract and re-applied at intent confirmation and at generation, so a library mounted after report creation cannot silently join it.

The two dimensions are **orthogonal**. `source_scope` narrowing gates the *active notebook's own* channels (PPR, private Memory, weak-support relations, the report corpus profile); unchecking a reference library must never switch any of those off, or a user who declined to borrow one library would pay for it with the current notebook's retrieval quality. Exact-section lookup is not switched off by narrowing, in chunk or reasoning mode: the run's source ceiling is pushed into its probe, so only in-ceiling sections can occupy the probe window or a section slot. Cross-library channels each consult the library dimension for themselves: typed collection enumeration and the collection map, federated candidate retrieval, community expansion, graph traversal, `follow_chain`, evidence assembly, and the KG availability gate. The last of those is a *judgement*, not a result filter — with the active notebook carrying no graph of its own and the only graph-bearing library unchecked, availability must answer "no graph", or `kg_required` never flips and the graph path runs a round over a KG this run may not read; it resolves participants through the same `resolve_participants` seam candidate retrieval uses, gated on the frozen selection rather than on whether that selection narrowed anything. Conversation history is the one gate that consults both dimensions, because a prior answer can quote content from a library the user has just unchecked.

Library-level narrowing is applied at **one** boundary — the participant list, filtered once and read by the plan, the walk, the denominator, and the closing fingerprint — because enumeration requires rows and counts to come from a single predicate; filtering rows while the denominator still summed every mounted library would report a walk that in fact finished as `concurrent_change`. `enumeration_active()` is unaffected: the tool stays available and only its scope shrinks. The leak surface includes the query terms themselves: community expansion takes sibling *entity names* out of a library and those names reach the visible trace, the used-query ledger, and the reflection prompt, so narrowing happens where the names are read, not where the hits come back. The source dimension is applied at the same exit: under a library's frozen source ceiling (every mounted library, and every library of a global question, is frozen to its visible sources) a sibling is kept only when an in-ceiling source supports it, and it is named by a member the ceiling admits — one whose own source is inside the ceiling, or that has no source of its own (an object promoted into a public library) — using the stored merged name when such a member carries it, otherwise the first such member's non-empty name in member-id order, never a spelling that only an out-of-ceiling member carries (a Knowhow or Memory projection, or a member pruned since the library was last merged); a sibling with no admitted member is dropped, and the co-mention read fetches twice the sibling quota so that a dropped sibling does not take a place. The focal entity is resolved under the same rule: its stored name counts only when an admitted member carries that spelling, so a spelling only an out-of-ceiling member carries resolves to no focal entity (the ordinary "focal unresolved" outcome). Without a ceiling the stored names are used unchanged. `resolve_participants` / `mount_sql.py` are untouched — that predicate is shared with permission checks (cross-library source detail proxying, citation resolution, asset reads), and a per-request retrieval checkbox has no business narrowing an authorization set.

Two second-order costs are registered and accepted. Graph traversal is filtered *after* traversal and PPR still diffuses over every participant's graph, because the federated graph is memoised process-wide under a scope-blind key: an excluded library's nodes still occupy diffusion budget and can act as transit hops, but none of their content reaches the rendered prompt or becomes citable, and PPR's passage slots go only to in-ceiling passages (next paragraph). The whole-graph size guard likewise stays scope-blind, so unchecking a very large library does not turn that guard back off — deliberately, because the graphs it guards are still built over every mounted library; narrowing the guard alone would admit exactly the build it exists to refuse.

**Retrieval legs under the run's source ceiling.** PPR (concept-walk) slots go only to in-ceiling passages: the ranking still spans every participant's graph (the graph cache is keyed by the participant set, never by the run's source selection), but each library's frozen source ceiling is applied before the `ppr_top_chunks` cut, so a mounted library's Knowhow rows and sources uploaded after the run froze its ceiling never take a slot, and the walk still returns `ppr_top_chunks` passages when enough in-ceiling candidates exist (a navigation page is passed over like a
refused candidate and spends no slot). An all-selected run whose sources did not change hydrates exactly as before. Reaching past refused candidates is bounded: a library the run admits nothing of leaves the PPR ranking itself, and every other refused candidate is passed over within at most 8 hydration windows of 900 candidates beyond the over-ranked prefix; passages ranked deeper are not found by PPR on that run, which returns fewer passages and records `ppr_ceiling_walk_exhausted`.

In a single-notebook run, a derived chain is dropped whole when either of its hops has no evidence left inside the run's source ceiling, so another member's private Memory can no longer supply a citable chain quote. Weak-support relation hints show a relation only when its target is still supported inside the ceiling and its sample relation itself comes from an in-ceiling source; a hint whose sample relation comes from an out-of-ceiling source is dropped even if another supporting source is in range. Of these knowledge-graph hints, only the weak-support hint sends a source list to the database, and only when the run's verdict (taken once per retrieval run) says the ceiling binds and the library no longer matches the freeze, the Memory channel is closed (the asker's own Memory is withheld, so "not another member's Memory" would admit it), or the run carries per-library ceilings; another member's Memory alone is excluded by owner, not by list. When the verdict says the ceiling cannot exclude anything, the hint reads without a list and checks only the source of each sample relation it shows; the first one outside the ceiling switches the rest of the run to the bounded read.

The `chunk` mode mix overlay's 1-hop graph walk drops every node that no in-ceiling source of its own library supports — the current notebook included — so another member's Memory-derived node, and the asker's own when Memory reading is withheld, never reaches the prompt; a relation whose evidence lies wholly outside the ceiling is not rendered as a chain step. When the ceiling cannot exclude anything (all selected, nothing changed, no other member's Memory, Memory reading not withheld), the walk is used as read after its evidence is verified against the ceiling taken before the read; a node or edge found outside the ceiling makes the rest of the run bind. The rendered overlay block is checked once more on the same verdict: when the ceiling binds, a node supported only by out-of-ceiling sources is removed together with every chain line that names it, and a surviving node whose incoming edge came from a removed node loses its evidence quote; when it does not bind, the block is used as is and only the sources its nodes list are checked, the first one outside the ceiling making the run bind.

When a run's source ceiling binds a library (the user narrowed it, its sources changed after the freeze, or it holds another member's personal memory the asker may not read), the relation lines of the answer context count only in-ceiling sources: the "×N sources" suffix is the number of distinct in-ceiling sources of the relation between the two objects shown, without merging duplicate objects of the same concept, and a relation supported only by out-of-ceiling sources is not shown. Without a binding ceiling the suffix keeps the notebook-wide merged support count.

Per-notebook retrieval caches shared by every asker — keyword tokens and the relation vector matrix — hold only content no Memory source derives; Memory-derived relations are cached apart with their source and masked per request by the asker's ceiling, and an object whose evidence the ceiling trimmed is scored from the evidence that asker may see. A plugin engine's element hit whose source is outside the frozen universe is dropped.

The **409 "empty scope"** judgement is now the conjunction of both dimensions — "which libraries did this request check", not "which libraries are mounted" — and applies at all three Ask entry points and at report create, confirm, and generate. A dimension the request did not *narrow* answers from the notebook's real evidence universe; a request that scoped neither dimension is left to the existing `ask_available` gate. The local evidence universe is **not** the visible-source count: Knowhow cells, that user's confirmed Memory and the local graph carry no visible source row, so `NotebookSummary` exposes `local_evidence_available` next to `ask_available` (computed by the catalog from the three local availability predicates it already evaluates, at zero extra queries) and the emptiness test ORs it with the source count, so the signal can only widen the answer, never narrow it. A genuine narrowing still wins: clearing every local source is empty even when local evidence exists. The reference-library dimension is judged by **evidence**, not by how many libraries are checked (user ruling 2026-10-28, applied to Ask and to reports alike): a checked library counts only if it has a usable knowledge graph, or visible-source text the federated passage lane will search -- the reference-library half of `ask_available` (`NotebookSummaryQuery._base_evidence_available`), narrowed to the checked set. The lane's `CHUNK_FEDERATION_ENABLED` switch and `CHUNK_FEDERATION_MAX_PARTICIPANTS` bound apply to the checked libraries in `MOUNT_ORDER`, exactly as the retrieval seat applies them (it filters by the checked set first and bounds second), so a library past the bound among the checked ones counts for nothing, while checking it alone brings it inside. So clearing every local source and checking only a library with no usable graph and no reachable text (unparsed, empty, deprecated-graph only, past the bound, or with the lane off) is refused with the same 409 and the same 「当前检索范围为空」 wording, at all three Ask entry points, at report create, confirm and generate, and in the follow-up scope (`fell_back_to_all`). Cost: a request whose local dimension is non-empty -- nearly all of them -- never evaluates the library half; when the library dimension is not narrowed (nothing submitted, or every mount checked) the answer the notebook summary already computed for `ask_available` is reused; only an empty local dimension with a genuinely narrowed library selection runs the probe, at most the same two `EXISTS` statements `ask_available` uses (the graph half restricted to the checked libraries carrying `base_kg_notebook_ids`).

`AskResponse.retrieval_scope` is a read-only receipt: `{ local: { selected, total }, bases: [{ notebook_id, name, included }] }`. Library names are a snapshot taken while the run was authorized, never re-derived from current mounts, so a reopened answer still names a library that has since been unmounted. Retrieval never reads it back. It is absent — and the payload therefore byte-identical to every historical answer — when the request narrowed neither dimension, because the browser submits both scopes on every request.
