When a question names something exactly lookup-able, retrieval therefore runs one extra zero-model channel first — exact substring match to locate the section, then fetch that section (and its subsections) whole — and merges the result into whichever candidate branch runs. The gate is deliberately narrower than the lexical layer's identifier extraction: `_`- or `.`-joined names (`set_db`, `config.yaml`) always qualify, while a purely hyphen-joined word must carry a digit, so model/version names (`GPT-4`, `v1-2`) qualify and ordinary English compounds (`state-of-the-art`, `real-time`, `end-to-end`) do not. Those words are why: they appear in almost every analytical question — a deep report's per-section question contains one nearly every time — and each would buy a real probe whose hit promotes a whole chapter into the evidence budget. They stay in lexical recall, where one extra OR-ed term is free. Hits are then folded onto the command they belong to before section slots are handed out, so one command's Arguments/Examples sub-sections cannot consume the budget a second named command needs. Those chunks score keyword-only — coverage of the *name* that addressed the section, not relevance to the whole question, so both callers report the same number for the same evidence — carry ordinary `lexical` provenance, and hold `EXACT_SECTION_RESERVE` seats in the final mix selection so the reranker cannot truncate the parameter table back off. Every query is bounded (`EXACT_LOOKUP_MAX_IDENTIFIERS` / `EXACT_LOOKUP_FTS_K` / `EXACT_LOOKUP_MAX_SECTIONS` / `EXACT_LOOKUP_MAX_CHUNKS_PER_SECTION`), and a question with no such name issues no additional queries at all, so those asks are unaffected. Scoped to the active notebook; mounted reference libraries are deliberately out of scope (a global ask instead runs it once per participant, see Global Ask). **Heading breadcrumbs are a Markdown-parsing property**, so "fetch the whole section" is only available for sources parsed that way; MinerU-parsed PDF/DOCX sources carry no breadcrumbs, and there the channel falls back to returning exactly the chunks that matched, which still recovers the parameter table an ordinary ranking would have dropped. The `reasoning` engine has two guarantees of its own for the same exact channel, and does not share `EXACT_SECTION_RESERVE`: after single-shot synthesis sorts by relevance, `REASONING_EXACT_RESERVE` (default 4) stably promotes up to that many exact-channel chunks to the front of the synthesis context — reordering only, never expanding the budget; in per-section synthesis, exact hits not bound to any section (same cap) enter **every** surviving section as copies without the seat marker (each copy goes into its own "Exact-lookup passages" block, assembled after that section's own bound chunk and element blocks and admitted only from what budget they leave, so it can never displace the evidence the model itself bound), so a passage the user named explicitly does not disappear just because the outline happened to bind its evidence elsewhere.

**PPR over the cross-document KG (used by `reasoning`'s retrieve step).** Seeds via `federated_retrieve` (KG entities + their source chunks; relation-index hits are not fused in, whatever `RELATION_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED` says) become the personalization vector for HippoRAG-style **Personalized PageRank** (`GRAPH_PPR_ENABLED`, on by default), which propagates relevance across documents through the shared knowledge graph; the top-ranked chunks feed a grounded answer whose `[k]` anchors point at chunk citations. Turning `GRAPH_PPR_ENABLED` off simply removes this channel from the mix — reasoning's reflect loop records a `skip` trace step and `chunk`'s mix branch treats it as an empty candidate list; neither falls back to a BFS walk.

**`reasoning` — intent-first agentic deep retrieval.** The official UI first calls `/ask/intent/stream` (`/ask/intent` remains JSON compatibility). Clear intent auto-continues with the user's original wording as the authoritative first retrieval seed and the model normalization as a supplement; after an ambiguity review, the user-confirmed wording is authoritative. This corpus-blind preflight may use up to the latest five user questions, never corpus-derived assistant answers, but it does not create a durable conversation/job. It reads no corpus text; the one corpus fact it reads is which languages (zh/en codes) the whole-question keywords should be in (see the first-round lexical arm below), which reads no source scope and triggers no ceiling read. Clear requests auto-confirm; blocking ambiguity opens an inline review. `/ask` and `/ask/stream` accept the reviewed `intent` alongside the original `question`; the backend deterministically freezes it and builds one authoritative internal research question used by Memory retrieval, PPR, evidence retrieval, and answer synthesis. Its approved retrieval directions directly seed the initial subqueries, bypassing the old second planning pass; reflection can add evidence-driven queries but cannot replace the contract. Directions beyond the effort's first-round width are not discarded: a deterministic coverage pass executes them in contract order after the PPR/exact seed passes and before the reflect loop, taking at most half of the shared reasoning-step budget, and each executed direction produces a normal `retrieve` trace step. A per-run registry maps every reviewed direction to a unique short label (widening the truncation window, then a numeric suffix, for directions whose default labels collide) since the model only ever sees and resubmits the label, never the seed's full contract text; an `add_subquery` submission matched against that registry either executes an uncovered direction's own contract text (recorded under the direction's identity, not the bare label) or is deduplicated against one already covered — by the coverage pass or an earlier `add_subquery` — instead of being re-run. Every later reflection prompt is fed the current uncovered set so the model can spend its own budget on them first, and a single `skip` step naming whatever directions remain uncovered is recorded once the reflect loop ends — reflecting the run's final coverage rather than the moment the coverage pass ran out of budget — and is omitted entirely if reflection ends up covering them all. The response persists the confirmed `intent`, exposes the internal `retrieval_query`, and starts the engine trace with `intent` before retrieval while the saved user turn remains the original wording. The trace covers the whole run, not just retrieval: question understanding happens before a durable job exists, so the UI synthesizes its own leading steps (understanding in flight → understood or awaiting clarification → confirmed) ahead of the backend's, instead of giving that phase a separate status line outside the trace. Its client-measured wall clock comes back as the optional, bounded `intent.understanding_ms` (never an input to retrieval) and becomes the persisted `intent` step's `duration_ms`. The engine streams `intent` before Memory retrieval and records a `memory` step when private memories were recalled; that step reports recall rather than attribution — attribution is carried by the answer's `[k]` citations — and a zero-hit lookup is recorded as a timed `skip` so its candidate query and embedding call stay in the total. It records a `synthesis` step after answer generation — usually the longest single slice of a run, and therefore neither invisible nor excluded from the trace total — whose citation count comes from bound anchors rather than retrieved-evidence cards. Direct compatibility callers that omit `intent` retain the old clear-question path, but deterministic unresolved/generic ambiguity fails closed. That 422's message enumerates what needs to be added as numbered items (①, ②, …) joined into one line (e.g. "你提到的对象具体是什么？请给出名称或简要背景。"), at most 8 items with each capped at 500 characters, and never echoes the user's own wording. A clear question costs zero extra model calls and zero extra reads on that old path — byte-identical to today's behavior. Only when the deterministic gate finds an unresolved referent or generic ambiguity does it run, in order: reading the latest five user-only turns (never assistant answers, corpus-blind) of the session the request's `conversation_id` names, scoped to this caller's own notebook (not owned by this user, no `conversation_id`, or no history — the same 422 as today); rewriting the follow-up into a standalone question through the existing `query_rewrite` workload (unconfigured, failed, or empty — the same 422 as today); and re-running the identical deterministic gate against the rewritten sentence — still ambiguous fails the same 422, whose message is always built from the original wording (the rewrite itself never reaches the error text, and is never echoed either), while a clean pass makes the rewritten sentence the internal `retrieval_query` and `intent.resolved_question` — `intent.objective`, the turn saved/shown in the conversation, and `result_scope`/completeness requirements are all still judged from the original wording, so a rewrite that drops an "all of them" never silently downgrades it to ranked. The `intent` trace step's `duration_ms` trusts the client's `understanding_ms` when `intent` was supplied, records the server-side rewrite time when it ran without `intent`, and is otherwise empty — no new trace step is added, and `AskRequest` gains no field. MCP's `ask` does not go through this path: it already runs a model understanding step with the conversation's history (the last five user questions) inside the call and returns a clarification handle (see the MCP section above), resolving follow-ups there instead, independent of this rewrite mechanism. The remaining loop delegates to `ReasoningRetriever`: retrieve (using the PPR propagation described above), reflect on sufficiency, and expand the graph or add subqueries until answerable, with live `reasoning_trace` over the NDJSON stream (`/ask/stream`). For explicit derivation questions it may call `follow_chain`: two bounded adjacency samples reuse the existing source/target indexes, then deterministically check types, status, review, evidence, and `validity_scope`. The two stored relations remain citable premises; `A→C` is only a query-time conclusion marked as an inference. If a high-degree sample is truncated and cannot prove the absence of a direct edge, it abstains. The exact-identifier fast path above is wired into this loop twice, both zero-model, and reaches both the `reasoning` ask mode and every deep-report section retrieval (the report engine reuses `ReasoningRetriever` verbatim); knowhow completion turns it off (its query is a JSON envelope, not a question, and would otherwise probe the envelope's own field names on every request). A deterministic seed pass runs once right after the initial retrieval whenever the authoritative question itself names an identifier (recorded as an `exact_lookup` trace step, rendered 「精查」), scored by the identifier names it actually probed rather than the raw question — scoring the exact match against every unrelated token in a long question sank a genuine hit low enough to lose the character budget and the grounded/overview threshold — and the reflect model may additionally choose the `exact_lookup` action with the name in `query` (matched literally), scored the same way, when a named command's full definition is still uncovered. The action obeys the same identifier gate as the seed pass — an arbitrary low-selectivity string is refused rather than turned into a library-wide substring scan — probes each name at most once per run (the seed pass shares that ledger), is capped at 3 agent invocations per run, and feeds every skipped/duplicate/zero-yield attempt back into the next reflection with a reason the model can act on (deduplicated so a repeated invalid input does not grow the ledger unbounded). A question containing no identifier issues no call and adds no trace step. Strict / KG-grounded.

The shared Ask/Deep Report intent planner preserves the user's requested level of detail. Optional formulas, implementation details, benchmark suites, every model scale, and exhaustive library coverage must not become mandatory topics or constraints unless requested; retrieval-query variants are search aids, not additional obligations. References explicitly anchored to the current document or library stay anchored for later retrieval without reading corpus content or inferring source identities. A genuinely missing comparison subject still requires clarification. Normalization must not invent an identity or replace the subject with an "unspecified model" placeholder, and free-text clarification must not offer a "please provide a name" instruction as an answer choice. Whether to ask belongs to the understanding model: when it returns a schema-valid contract, its own verdict and ambiguity rows alone decide whether the web inline review, the MCP clarification handle, or the Deep Report "补充问题信息" step appears, and wording such as 这个/它/that is the model's to resolve from the question and the user-only history. The two wording rules — an unresolved referent (for example 这个/它/that) and a bare generic request (for example 帮我总结) — only stand in when no valid understanding exists: the model is unconfigured, the call fails, or its output fails schema validation (an ambiguity row without a question, or more rows than the contract admits, counts as invalid). An explicit `needs_clarification=true` from a valid understanding always asks: when every row the model gave is optional, a generic required question is added. The wording rules also remain the only gate for direct compatibility calls without `intent`, which run no understanding model.

#### Source scope is user-selected only

For confirmed Ask intent, the authoritative whole question is retrieved first, followed by directions seeded round-robin across mandatory topics. Invalid confirmation returns 422 before creating a durable conversation/job; aborting intent preflight signals cancellation to the model call.

Naming the current library specifies retrieval scope; it does not by itself request exhaustive output. An ordinary overview remains ranked with completeness not required. Explicit requests to list every item, count a complete collection, or introduce each document still use their complete, aggregate or hybrid scope. The planner must not add an all-items constraint to an otherwise ranked overview.

Retrieval source scope comes exclusively from the visible-source checkboxes described under [Source-selected retrieval scope](#source-selected-retrieval-scope); the model never infers which sources a question names. The corpus-blind intent planner emits no source identities, and there is no reviewed source-confirmation step: a reasoning run inherits the request's checkbox ceiling and nothing inside the run can change it.

An earlier revision let the intent planner emit a `source_refs` list that `/ask/intent` resolved against a bounded identity-only catalog by exact normalized match on stable id, display title, or original file name, gated behind a `source_scope_confirmation` review and a signed preview capability, with a `search_evidence(query, source_refs?)` Agent action able to narrow further inside a confirmed run. That whole contract is removed. Exact equality could not honor an abbreviation — asking about "pdagent" when the source is titled "PDAGENT-BENCH: Characterizing, Grounding, and Architecting LLM/VLM Agents for VLSI Physical Design" resolved to zero matches — and because the design failed closed, an ordinary question died with a deterministic 422 that no retry could clear. Since users already own the checkboxes, a second model-side guess added failure modes without adding reach.

#### Model JSON recovery and stream liveness

**Native JSON Schema negotiation.** The first scheduled chat call (including an explicit service test) probes strict `response_format.type=json_schema` using synthetic data before its business request. Reading status, resolving clients and startup configuration validation perform no network I/O. A random required enum appears only in the wire schema while the prompt asks for a different object, so accepting but ignoring the parameter does not establish support. One concurrent probe is shared across workloads and retained in memory for the backend process by protocol, endpoint, model and credential identity. Capacity, display-name and workload-policy edits reuse it; changing that identity or restarting the process probes again. The probe uses the existing scheduler slot, bypasses response caches, adds no provider retry, and is bounded by `MODEL_JSON_SCHEMA_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default **30 seconds**, range **1–300**) or a shorter caller timeout. Cancellation leaves capability untried. Rejected or ignored schemas retain ordinary JSON mode; other errors are recorded as unverified and conservatively do the same until the identity changes or the process restarts. Optional capability failures do not open the service breaker.

For supported services, representable hints become real closed JSON Schemas with typed properties, `required` and `strict: true`; optional fields become nullable and heterogeneous example lists retain all declared fields. Scalar examples express types, not fixed values; only pipe-delimited vocabularies constrain enums, and an enum also admits the empty string except on a required root field (a reflect `next_action`, an intent's `result_scope`), where the empty string is an invalid choice rather than "unused". Dynamic-key maps, arbitrary objects and ambiguous hints keep ordinary JSON mode instead of losing valid fields. A provider's rejection of one concrete schema is remembered separately and falls back to JSON mode. Native replies are validated locally in their original form before caching, repair or domain consumption; malformed roots, wrappers, types, non-finite values and duplicate keys remain failures, preserving finish reason and billed usage. Actual schema participates in cache identity, and a fallback never populates a strict-schema entry. Domain checks still own evidence and semantic validity. Capability events contain only safe service/model labels and fixed status/reason values, never prompts, proof values, raw replies or exceptions. The following legacy JSON recovery rules apply when native Schema is not selected.

**Domain acceptance.** Knowledge relations name their endpoints by integer 0-based position in the same reply's node array, read like the `ev` label (an integer or digit string, never a boolean or float); an out-of-range, self-referencing or dropped-node endpoint loses its relation while valid grounded nodes survive, and a fragment whose relations all fail this way is not cached. Paper classification requires an explicit boolean after shared normalization: missing/malformed `is_paper` writes no metadata row and remains retryable, while explicit false remains an idempotent non-paper result. Memory preview prose/tags, evidence-refinement items and report coverage notes/contradictions accept only strings; invalid preview prose uses the original-answer fallback, and invalid optional items are dropped. Sufficiency verdicts bind to outline sections by the 1-based number the prompt gives each section, never by title; out-of-range or non-integer numbers are ignored, and a verdict may lower but never raise the deterministic sufficiency. No suggested action is requested or stored. Offline evaluation explicitly parses booleans (including canonical true/false strings), excludes booleans from integer scores and safely rejects non-object replies; offline question generation discards non-text questions.

The shared answer style guidance follows the requested output granularity. A title inventory keeps every matching source record and citation, including separate same-title records, without unsolicited summaries or configuration details; necessary coverage disclosures remain. Overviews and mechanism comparisons retain the main reasoning, qualifications and requested detail. Numeric comparisons preserve metric, unit, version, configuration and scoring conditions. Each direction applies to one metric, version and configuration pair; a slash-separated group of different configurations cannot share one higher/lower conclusion when directions differ. Unclear source mappings between slash-separated values and scoring labels remain uncertain rather than guessed. Unless the user requests a complete matrix or itemized results, lead with the conclusion and necessary supporting values and decisive exceptions, instead of repeating both full tables before comparing them. Explicit completeness requests remain binding. A source's qualitative claim cannot override conflicting table values. Shared versus independent components, architectural versus numerical changes, and theoretical versus tested compatibility remain distinct. These are instructions inside existing synthesis calls, not an extra assessment pass or a reduction of output budgets; model compliance and factual quality must still be evaluated.

The final-answer prompt demonstrates one strictly valid JSON object containing both `answer` and boolean `grounded`. Markdown paragraph breaks, quotes, and LaTeX backslashes are escaped within the answer string; the model must not emit a second object. This output guidance does not relax strict parsing, schema checks, string-preserving repair, or the existing retry limit.

`ask_answer` explicitly keeps thinking enabled. It is the one bounded final synthesis call that must reconcile the selected evidence, conflicts, coverage disclosures, and citation wording into what the user reads; spending reasoning tokens there has materially higher leverage than spending them in every KG/chunk extraction window. A strict reasoning Ask may therefore use thinking both in its bounded `reasoning_agent` loop and in final synthesis, while the high-fan-out evidence-production paths stay non-thinking. Deployments may override this per workload in `[thinking]`; the current transport applies the resolved explicit mode to every bound chat service without inspecting its model name.

`reasoning_agent` decisions, `ask_answer` synthesis and the four Deep Report workloads (`report_outline`, `report_sufficiency`, `report_section`, `report_summary`) are strict-JSON-first. If strict parsing fails, the shared repair seam may accept only a complete object-shaped response with recoverable syntax faults such as missing quotes/commas. The repaired object must stay within the schema example's top-level keys, actual booleans remain booleans, enum-like example values remain in vocabulary, non-finite values are refused, and every nonempty string value must still appear verbatim in the raw response. Repair restores delimiters only: the keys and scalar values read in document order must be exactly the sequence the model wrote, so a repair that drops, merges, splits, reorders or authors one is refused as `string_changed` (two adjacent strings `"A" "B",` once came back as body `A` and a key `B","grounded`, silently shortening the body; a repeated key kept only its last value). A backslash inside a string that starts no JSON escape (LaTeX such as `\mathrm{V}`, `50\%`, `\_`) is read literally before this gate for every workload (see below); when it sits next to a real syntax fault the repair reads it the same way, and a string is also verbatim when it appears in the reply's strings decoded that way, which covers an answer mixing `\n` paragraph escapes with LaTeX (deepseek-flash, 2026-09-29). Truncated objects, arrays/scalars, unknown keys, type confusion, and string reconstruction remain malformed responses. A retriever failure degrades to a terminal persisted Ask response instead of aborting the orchestration on an absent result.

That scheduler exit now covers **all 29 chat workloads** in the current registry, not only Ask and Deep Report. The boundary follows the harness principle adopted on 2026-09-14: the prompt must be precise, the shared boundary tolerates the deviations a model plausibly makes, and only the domain parsers stay strict where being wrong would write bad data. Five deviations are absorbed before strict parsing, for every workload and independent of `MODEL_JSON_REPAIR_MODE`, because each has exactly one reading. First, a backslash inside a double-quoted string that starts no JSON escape (not followed by `"`, `\`, `/`, `b`, `f`, `n`, `r`, `t`, or `u` plus four hex digits — LaTeX `\mathrm{V}`, `50\%`, `\_` although the prompt asks for `\\`) has one reading, the characters written: the reply is delivered with each such backslash doubled, so it decodes to exactly those characters, and recorded as a content-free `model_json_repair` event with `status: "escaped"`, `reason: "stray_backslash"`; valid escapes keep their JSON meaning, so LaTeX commands that happen to be valid escapes (`\times`, `\frac`, `\nu`) still decode as JSON defines and only the prompt can prevent them. Second, a raw control character typed inside a string (a newline or tab in an answer) is written as its JSON escape and recorded with `status: "escaped"`, `reason: "control_char"`; whitespace between tokens is untouched. Third, an unescaped `"` inside a **value** string that is followed by text rather than JSON structure (`"所谓"恒流"模式"`, or `\"|DSML|"` with only one of the pair escaped) is read as a character of the text, escaped, and recorded with `status: "escaped"`, `reason: "inner_quote"`. A quote followed by `,`, `}`, `]` or the end closes the string, but only once the string's quotes — escaped ones and those read as text — pair up: with an odd count the closing quote may as well be the partner of the one read as text (`"这种模式叫"恒流"}`, `["a, "b"]`), and the reply keeps its rejection; a quote followed by `:`, by another quote (single or double), or by the start of any JSON value — a literal, a number, `[]`, `["`, `{"` (`["first" null "second"]`; a citation `[k1]` or LaTeX `{x}` is text) may start a key or mark a lost comma, so the reply keeps its rejection too; inside an array every quote that does not close the string is ambiguous (`["first"second"third"]` or `["a" b "c"]` may be items that lost their commas), so this reading applies to object values only, where unkeyed items are not JSON and `"the "foo" mode"` has one reading; key strings never take this reading (a key that swallowed a quote is a restarted or broken reply, not a key). This reading is tried last, because it is the only one that moves a string boundary the model wrote. Fourth, a complete top-level object followed only by stray closing punctuation (`}`, `]`, quotes, backticks, whitespace — a deepseek-flash report section once arrived as a whole valid object plus an extra `"}`), or by the same object written again (whole, repeatedly, or cut short by the token budget; whitespace between tokens may differ, whitespace inside strings must match), is delivered as that object, byte-for-byte, and recorded as a content-free `model_json_repair` event with `status: "trimmed"`, `reason: "trailing_data"`. Anything else after the object — a second object that differs anywhere, a cut copy closed into a different object, `, "key": value}` fields the model meant to include, prose — still fails as `invalid_json`. Fifth, a reply that restarted — one or more fragments, each repeated character for character (whitespace between tokens aside) by the text after it, none ending where a nested value may start (after `:`, `[` or `,`: `{"answer":{"answer":…}}` is a second reading), then a complete object: DeepSeek-V4-Flash answer syntheses arrived as `{"{"answer": …}` from 2026-10-09 and as `{"answer{"answer": …}` and `{"answer":"{"answer": …}` on 2026-10-14 — is delivered as that object, byte-for-byte apart from the escapes above, and recorded as a content-free `model_json_repair` event with `status: "trimmed"`, `reason: "duplicated_open"`. The fragments are dropped before strings are read (a stray quote in them would otherwise flip every string boundary after it), the object must share a top-level field with a non-empty schema hint, and only whitespace, quotes and at most one `}` per dropped fragment may follow it: a fragment the following text does not repeat (two different answers), a `]`, more fields, a second object, or a truncated remainder means the object is a nested value or incomplete, and the reply keeps the rejection reason it had before (`invalid_json`, or `incomplete_object` on repair workloads). The restart scan is linear: each fragment is compared only from the latest restart point and only the eight latest restart points are tried, so a reply that restarted many times is still read and one stuck repeating a fragment is rejected quickly. Concretely, after strict JSON parsing succeeds the boundary **rejects** a reply only when it is unusable to any consumer — not JSON, not an object, empty, truncated, carrying a number JSON itself cannot represent (`NaN`, `Infinity`, an overflowing exponent — a `+inf` confidence would otherwise clamp to the maximum in every numeric consumer), or an object containing none of the expected top-level fields (`{}` included). Every field-level mismatch against the schema example is handled in one of two ways and, either way, recorded as one `model_json_shape` event — except a `null` the strict projection of the same hint would accept (any nested object field, or a root field that projection treats as optional), which prompts ask for to say "unused" and which is therefore dropped without an event in either mode — (`status: "deviation"`, the workload, the safe `support_id`, and a bounded list of `path`/`reason`/`fix` entries such as `enumerate.kind: invalid_enum`; never the reply text), so a prompt whose example has drifted from what the model writes stays visible in `events.jsonl` without costing the caller its reply. A deviation with exactly one sensible reading is **absorbed** by the boundary (`fix` names it): a JSON `null` where the hint advertised a value is dropped, because absent and null mean the same thing to every consumer and a bare string conversion downstream would otherwise turn it into the literal text `None` and persist it as prose; `"true"`/`"false"` for a boolean hint and a numeric string for a number hint are coerced; one scalar where a list of scalars was advertised is wrapped into a one-item list instead of being iterated character by character; a scalar where a list of objects was advertised has no reading and is dropped, so a consumer iterating that collection sees it as absent rather than raising; a reply whose advertised fields were all `null` (or were all dropped) is treated as containing none of them and rejected. Every other mismatch — a wrong scalar type with more than one reading, a value outside an `a|b|c` enum hint, a scalar where an object was advertised, a nested object sharing no key with its example — is **delivered as written** (`fix` empty), and the domain parser applies its own tolerance (narrowing enums, dropping the one unusable item) instead of the whole reply failing. Before this change the same walk rejected on the first mismatch: one hallucinated edge type discarded a whole knowledge-graph extraction window, a `"year": null` failed paper metadata for every non-paper source, and the parsers' own tolerances were unreachable. Because these hints are examples rather than full JSON Schema documents, omitted optional fields remain allowed and this boundary never deletes provider-added fields; the JSON-repair path judges field shape by the same lenient walk and keeps strict only what repair itself could violate (a repaired string must remain verbatim in the raw reply). Every response still rejected at this shared boundary is written to the private analysis-artifact store with the complete model messages, schema hint, raw response, user question when one is explicitly available, and safe `support_id`; ordinary logs and list projections contain none of that content. Background or script calls without request-level notebook identity are still retained under `_unscoped`, so missing Notebook route context cannot make a failure disappear.

The admin issue projection classifies each stable workload id into seven areas. A shared workload invoked inside report execution is classified as Report rather than by its default area:

| Model area | Current chat workloads (29 total) |
| --- | --- |
| Ask `ask` | `ask_answer`, `plugin_engine`, `reasoning_agent`, `query_rewrite`, `gap_consult_query`, `external_evidence_answer`, `evidence_refine` |
| Deep Report `report` | `report_outline`, `report_sufficiency`, `report_section`, `report_summary`, `report_context_compress` |
| Source processing `source` | `source_summary`, `notebook_metadata`, `paper_metadata`, `chunk_question_generation` |
| Knowledge `knowledge` | `kg_extract`, `kg_refine`, `kg_glean`, `kg_merge_review`, `kg_concept_description`, `kg_conflict_review`, `schema_induction` |
| Memory and library understanding `memory` | `memory_preview`, `agent_profile_consolidate` |
| Knowhow `knowhow` | `knowhow_optimize`, `knowhow_reformat`, `knowhow_complete` |
| Retrieval optimization `retrieval` | `retrieval_experience_distill` |

Failures are also classified as `invalid_json` (empty, truncated, non-object, or syntactically invalid JSON), `schema_mismatch` (declared shape/type/enum mismatch or none of the expected top-level fields), or `repair_rejected` (repairable in shadow mode but deliberately not accepted). These labels explain why a response failed the common JSON contract; they do not replace a product feature's own business fallback or user-error contract.

`/ask/stream` sends a content-free blank NDJSON line every **5 seconds** while its delivery queue is idle and disables common proxy buffering. Existing clients ignore blank lines. This keeps the transport active during a slow reflection or synthesis call without fabricating a reasoning step; disconnect still stops only that client's delivery and the detached job still runs. The heartbeat protects against idle timeouts only—an ingress/CDN with an absolute total-request ceiling must be configured by the operator.

Interactive work is split by lifetime rather than forcing every endpoint into the same transport:

| Work shape | Current browser surfaces | Delivery and disconnect contract |
|---|---|---|
| Request-local model work | Ask intent, answer-to-Memory preview, Knowhow wording optimization, row completion, and reformat | Shared NDJSON request stream. The result belongs only to the open interaction; disconnect sets the same cooperative cancellation event used by retrieval/model I/O. |
| Durable long work | Ask answer, Deep Report, source parsing, indexing/KG maintenance, command catalog, notebook understanding | Start/detach and persist a job; reconnect or poll durable status. Navigation/transport loss does not cancel it; only its explicit cancel action may do so. |
| Bounded synchronous work | CRUD, paginated reads, status/configuration, deterministic validation and admission | Ordinary JSON/HTTP. These calls do not need artificial progress events. |
| Body or binary transfer | Upload bodies and binary downloads such as `reports.zip` | Ordinary HTTP with a visible busy state; source parsing begins as background work after upload admission. NDJSON bytes are never mixed into a file payload. |

The shared request-local protocol lives at the `.../stream` variants of `POST /notebooks/{id}/ask/intent`, `POST /answers/{answer_id}/memory-preview`, and Knowhow's `optimize`, `complete`, and `reformat` actions. It emits an immediate `started`, then a content-free heartbeat every **5 seconds** carrying only a fixed `stage` and monotonic `elapsed_ms`, then exactly one `final`, stable-code `error`, or `cancelled` event. The response uses `application/x-ndjson`, `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`, and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Exception text, prompts, notebook/source identities, evidence, and model output never appear in heartbeat/error frames. Authorization and deterministic scope/input checks finish before the first frame where practical, preserving their real HTTP statuses; failures after streaming begins use the stable error code and the browser's reviewed fallback copy. The browser displays elapsed time for Ask intent and Memory preview, and existing Knowhow loading/queue states remain active while heartbeats keep the transport alive. The original JSON endpoints remain available to compatibility clients, but the official browser uses the streaming variants.

This request-local protocol deliberately has different disconnect semantics from durable Ask. If its browser goes away, an ASGI frame send fails, or the user closes/stops/replaces the active interaction, the server signals cancellation and observes the worker to completion; provider code must re-raise cancellation instead of converting it into a normal fallback. The browser reader uses a bounded timer fallback so a background tab that suspends `requestAnimationFrame` still drains the terminal frame. If a future action must survive navigation or process restart, it belongs in the durable-job row above rather than in this stream.

### Reasoning effort and complete collection requests

The grade is picked in the Ask composer through the same graded-effort control as a deep report's research depth — one shared component, so the two never drift apart: a chip carrying the current grade name, opening a slider popover that shows that grade plus one neutral sentence about it. The interface deliberately exposes only the grade name and that sentence; the exact ceilings live in this table (mirrored by `frontend/app/ask-retrieval-effort.ts` and `backend/app/core/ask_retrieval_policy.py`) rather than being printed onto the control. `answer_element_items` and the three `enum_*` columns below are the exceptions to that mirror: they are backend-only fields with no frontend consumer, since they only shape the final synthesis prompt and the [collection-enumeration tools](#collection-enumeration-tools) budget server-side. `read_document`'s element and character sampling pools are the same kind of exception, and are not `AskRetrievalLimits` fields at all: the element pool reuses `document_overview_max_elements` (the same deployment knob the general-purpose document-introduction lane uses), and the character pool is computed on the fly as `limits.chunk_context_chars // 4` — both are read server-side only, so `ask-retrieval-effort.ts` does not need a matching field.

Reasoning Ask accepts the stable `retrieval_effort` ids below; the default is `standard`. The model may stop before a ceiling when evidence is sufficient, but it may not raise a ceiling. “Final floor/aspect/cap” means `min(cap, max(floor, aspect × executed query count))`. The context values are hard evidence-character ceilings: the source partition contains structured preview, chunks, and direct source elements; the KG partition contains KG objects/relations, confirmed Memory, and query-time chains. Their combined evidence block cannot exceed the sum of the two values. `answer_element_items` bounds how many direct source elements (formulas, tables, images, …) the final synthesis prompt admits; same-source normalized-text duplicates collapse before this cap, the remaining representatives are chosen by retrieval relevance descending rather than insertion order, and they still consume the shared chunk-context budget above. Reflection receives this same capped diverse element view, so it cannot judge sufficiency from passages that final synthesis cannot see. `enum_page_size` / `enum_pages_per_run` / `enum_rows_per_run` bound the separate collection-enumeration tools (`enumerate_elements` / `enumerate_kg_objects` and their `collection="sources"` parameter value, described below): a page size shared by every effort, plus a per-run pool of extra page round trips and total listed rows that grows with effort the same way the other ceilings do.

| Effort id | UI label | Per-query ranked take | Final floor / aspect / cap | Max reasoning steps / initial subqueries | KG / chunk context characters | Direct source elements in synthesis | Enum page size | Enum extra pages/run | Enum rows/run |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `overview` | 概览 | 4 | 8 / 2 / 12 | 4 / 2 | 4,000 / 12,000 | 4 | 50 | 2 | 100 |
| `standard` | 标准 | 8 | 20 / 3 / 36 | 8 / 5 | 6,000 / 30,000 | 6 | 50 | 4 | 200 |
| `deep` | 深入 | 8 | 24 / 4 / 48 | 16 / 6 | 8,000 / 50,000 | 8 | 50 | 6 | 300 |
| `thorough` | 详尽 | 12 | 32 / 5 / 64 | 32 / 8 | 12,000 / 80,000 | 12 | 50 | 8 | 400 |
| `exhaustive` | 穷尽 | 16 | 40 / 6 / 96 | 50 / 10 | 16,000 / 120,000 | 16 | 50 | 12 | 600 |

**Legacy reflect prefix layout.** Legacy keeps its existing decision protocol and candidate projection. Within the same user message, all question-independent instructions (including the JSON-only instruction) precede quoted-phrase grounding, the complete question, and the unchanged candidate summary. Roles, schema, action availability, parsing, stopping rules, retrieval/answer budgets, candidate order and excerpt limits are unchanged; there is no new strategy switch, history replay, evidence binding or detail expansion. The instructions depend on the existing tool gates, so reuse is only expected across matching configurations. This layout extends the stable prefix, particularly between questions whose quoted terms differ; it neither guarantees identical model decisions after text moves nor guarantees server-side cache reuse or lower latency. Measure complete Ask latency and answer quality; provider cache counters are optional.

`search_chunks` (source-passage search) is capped per run by the deployment setting `REASONING_MAX_CHUNK_SEARCHES` (default `3`, matching PPR and exact lookup); it is not an effort field. The deterministic first-round passage seed (independent of the knowledge graph) does not count against that cap, and each sub-query's seed take is the effort's per-query ranked take (`ranked_per_query_take`), not the `search_chunks` action's own MMR k.

The initial-subquery ceiling bounds **first-round concurrency only**; it is not a decision to drop the confirmed directions that do not fit. Every reviewed direction beyond that width is deferred into a bounded coverage pass that runs after the deterministic seed passes and before the reflect loop, sharing the same reasoning-step budget (the coverage pass may consume at most half of it, so the reflect loop always keeps a working share). Directions the step budget cannot reach are fed back into reflection every round so the model can prioritize them, and whichever remain uncovered once the reflect loop ends are disclosed in a single skipped trace step reflecting that final state; they are never silently discarded, and resubmitting a direction's short label — whether or not it has already been covered — is resolved against the direction's own identity rather than treated as an unrelated new query.

Candidate generation does not grow with effort; deployment settings control it independently. `CHUNK_RECALL` defaults to **200** and separately bounds each indexed Chunk/KG ANN and lexical window (at most 400 identities before deduplication at the default). `RELATION_RECALL` defaults to **200** and separately bounds Relation ANN and the total lexically expanded relation-id window (at most 400 before deduplication at the default); source and target directions still receive reserved shares inside that lexical total. Changing either deployment setting changes the effective candidate window, so the UI does not present those defaults as request-level hard ceilings.

Intent preflight classifies result scope as `ranked`, `complete`, `aggregate`, or `hybrid`, with an explicit completeness flag. The scope is **decided by the model and bounded by deterministic wording** (user decision, 2026-09-14: the model is the brain, the server only catches the two ways it can be wrong): explicit full-set wording in the question (“所有 / every / 一共多少 …”, with clause-local negation respected) fixes the scope deterministically, so a request such as “list all methods in this Knowhow table” never turns into a relevance Top-N; an explicit refusal of the full set (“不需要所有 …”) caps it at `ranked`; with neither, the model's classification stands — including a widening to `complete` / `aggregate` / `hybrid` — but only when the reply is consistent (a non-ranked scope must carry `completeness_required=true`) and its `confidence` is at least 0.5; a low-confidence or self-contradicting widening falls back to `ranked`, because collection enumeration is the expensive executor and a guess does not get to choose it. Which rule decided is recorded as `scope_source` (`lexical` / `model` / `default`) in the understanding status. Confirmation deterministically recomputes that scope from both the final edited wording and authoritative clarification answers. The deterministic executor admits only semantics it can prove from physical rows: a direct whole-table row/method list or a direct count of rows/records, optionally followed by analysis. Conditional subsets, distinct/type counts such as “how many kinds”, and grouped aggregation currently fall back to ranked retrieval with an explicit statement that exact completeness is unsupported. A supported 100-row table can return `100/100`. The shared enumeration safety contract is identical at every effort level:

| Complete-enumeration threshold | Exact limit |
|---|---:|
| Rows per cursor page | 25 |
| Pages per request | 50 |
| Physical rows scanned/returned per request | 1,250 |
| Tables per request | 8 |
| Selected columns per table | 8 |
| Cell excerpt available to the model | 1,000 characters |
| Structured result payload | 256,000 characters |
| Rows rendered inline in answer prose | 100 |
| Rows initially visible in each UI result card | 20 |

The 100-row inline ceiling is also the maximum row preview available to hybrid model synthesis; it does not delete rows from the authoritative structured result. Responses therefore separate per-table coverage, request/batch coverage (`selected_tables/known_tables`, returned/known rows), and hybrid synthesis coverage. For example, enumerating 200/200 rows while synthesizing 100/200 is “enumeration complete, analysis partial”. The 20-row initial UI view is presentation-only and remains expandable. A lightweight catalog query returns at most eight table descriptors and never hydrates cells, code attachments, or health payloads; it prioritizes an explicitly named table before applying that window, so a ninth-or-later table remains addressable. Aggregate counts and sequence sums still cover the whole notebook. Coverage says complete only after cursor exhaustion and stable before/after catalog values: projection `mutation_seq`, history-backed `enumeration_seq`, row count, column metadata, and selected/global scope. Every row add/delete records history in the same transaction, so an equal-count delete-then-add still changes `enumeration_seq`. Reaching the row/page/table/column/payload safety rail, or detecting a concurrent table change, produces `complete=false` with `explicit_partial` batch coverage and must never be worded as “all”; an individually exhausted selected table may remain complete when the overall batch omitted tables at the eight-table ceiling. Selecting a lower effort level does not reduce these explicit-completeness limits. This executor currently applies only to the direct physical-row Knowhow semantics above; other Knowhow semantics still disclose that complete enumeration is unsupported. It also runs only when every Knowhow table it can reach is inside the question's source ceiling: not in a global question (it reads the naming anchor's tables only), not under a narrowed source scope (a table is not a ticked source), and not after the notebook's sources changed since the question's scope was frozen; in those cases the question continues on the reasoning path, whose own channels filter row by row, and the completeness notice applies. Source-element, KG-object and document collections have their own bounded enumeration path — the [collection enumeration tools](#collection-enumeration-tools) below — which the model invokes explicitly rather than the intent-scope executor above; Memory and any other collection still disclose that complete enumeration is unsupported.

Retired ids `fast`, `global`, and `graph` are transparently remapped to `chunk`, and `auto` is transparently remapped to `reasoning` (old sessions/bookmarks never 422); any other unknown mode is rejected with HTTP 422.

The V2 experimental protocol and layouts are retired. Ask, Deep Report and Knowhow use Legacy; there is no V2 switch, evidence-history ledger, aspect assessment or synthesis aspect telemetry. Existing historical traces retain their ordinary summaries.

### Collection enumeration tools

Reasoning Ask can also list, rather than only rank, bounded families of collections through the model-invoked reflect actions `enumerate_elements` (source elements) and `enumerate_kg_objects` (knowledge objects), plus the `enumerate.collection` parameter value `"sources"` on either of them, which lists the library's own documents instead. The model-facing action space therefore stayed at ten ids through this feature: the third collection arrives as a parameter, not as a third action (genuinely new actions added later are unrelated to this one: the outline scratchpad described [below](#outline-scratchpad-and-section-by-section-synthesis) is the eleventh, Agentic Memory P4's `consult_memory` is the twelfth, and `read_document` — the "roster → per-document read" action described further down this section — is the thirteenth, and the in-document navigation pair `browse_sections` / `read_section` described [below](#section-navigation-inside-one-document-browse_sections--read_section) are the fourteenth and fifteenth; the count follows `domain/reflect_action.CORE_REFLECT_ACTION_IDS` (16 ids) and leaves out the terminal `answer` action). All three collections are served by zero-LLM executors: the model decides whether and how much to enumerate; the executor computes coverage as a fact, never from the model's own assertion. This is a separate mechanism from the Knowhow physical-row executor above — it shares the same effort-scaled budget table but not the same intent-scope gate, and it is never automatically triggered by `result_scope`.

**Who can trigger enumeration: the model, and only the model.** The triggers are the two model actions in the reflect loop; there is no third one. **The roster is the model's own choice**: `enumerate_elements` with the parameter `enumerate.collection="sources"` means "list which documents this library holds". The server does not deterministically seed a roster in the first round by matching the question's shape — in agentic mode, whether to list the roster is the model's judgement, and the catalog-question classifier (`overview_intent`) serves the chunk-native general-Q&A lane only. A later request for the same roster **at the same scope** is skipped as already listed (`already_enumerated`), so the same list is never enumerated — or charged — twice. **Which documents to read further is also the model's own choice**: once it has the roster, reaching for `read_document` to sample one document's original text — especially a row with no stored summary — is a step the model decides for itself from what the roster showed; the server never picks or seeds this for it.

**The roster's scope is a parameter of that same call**: `enumerate.scope` is filled in by the model and takes one of two values, `"all"` or `"current_notebook"`. **The default — absent, empty, or any value the parser cannot use — is `"all"`**: every document in retrieval scope, the active notebook plus its checked reference libraries. That is the same federated reach the `[Collections in scope]` line reports as `sources`, so the count the model was shown and the roster it gets back agree when it leaves the parameter alone. `"current_notebook"` narrows the listing to the active notebook's own documents — the parenthesised `current notebook` count on that same line. The parameter is spelled as a **string enum, never a boolean**, and that is a general rule for model-facing tool parameters rather than a local preference: the JSON validation layer (`model_json._validate_against_example`) rejects a non-bool against a boolean example outright, so a model answering `"true"` or `"yes"` would lose the whole reflect turn to the fail-open fallback; a string example instead carries the tolerance rule that an empty value is always accepted, and the enum values say what they do where `true` would have left the model guessing which side of the switch it is on. **An illegal non-empty string (`"yes"`, `"local"`) is still rejected by that validation layer** as `invalid_enum`, and a non-string (`1`, `null`, `{}`) as `invalid_type` — in both cases the turn is recorded as a fallback (see the reflect fallback contract below) rather than silently re-interpreted. The safe answers are therefore the two legal values, or nothing at all. The parser behind that layer is nevertheless fail-open on this field for its own sake: any value it cannot use falls back to `"all"` and never voids the action, not even under `fail_closed` — scope is not a question of action validity.

**Scope is part of a roster's identity, and it is visible.** The continuation ledger is keyed by scope, so a `"current_notebook"` listing that completed and a later `"all"` request are **two different chains**: the second is a real enumeration, not an `already_enumerated` skip, and the reverse order behaves the same way. Both chains draw on the one run-level enumeration budget, so re-listing costs what it costs and needs no special case. A narrowed listing says so wherever its numbers appear: the `enumerate` trace step carries `detail.local_only=true` (the key is absent at the default scope), and the on-screen step summary, the enumeration ledger fed back to the model, and **that listing's section header in the answer-synthesis evidence block** (`[Enumeration: documents（仅当前笔记本）, listed …]`) all carry the suffix “（仅当前笔记本）”, the same shape as the existing “（限指定来源）” suffix for a source-scoped element listing. All three take their suffixes from one rule (`reasoning_retrieval.enumeration_scope_suffix`, which reads the literal `collection_enumeration.LOCAL_ONLY_SCOPE_SUFFIX`), so the wording cannot be changed in one of them only. The section header is a requirement rather than a nicety: when one run lists both scopes, synthesis receives two document listings whose `listed`/`total` legitimately disagree, and without the suffix nothing in the block says which one excludes reference libraries.

**The result card carries the scope as a field, and shows the same suffix.** `TypedCollectionResult.scope` is `"all"` or `"current_notebook"`, mapped from the outcome's `local_only`; it is meaningful for `sources` only, and every other collection is always `"all"` (`enumerate.scope` exists on that collection alone, so a narrowed element listing is not a thing the wire can claim). The field is **additive** — `"all"` is its default, so a stored answer written before it existed, and any client that never sends it, both read back as the unnarrowed scope they actually were. The frontend (`answer-panel.tsx`) still composes the “来源清单” title from `collection` via its own lookup table, then appends “（仅当前笔记本）” when `scope === "current_notebook"`, so the card reads the same words as the trace, the ledger and the section header. `scope` is also part of the card's React key: `element_kind`/`object_type`/`source_id` are all empty for `sources`, so two scope-differing rosters would otherwise collide on one key and share expand/collapse state.

**A listing follows the question's source ticks, and says so.** Enumeration and `read_document` stay available when the request has [narrowed the retrieval scope by source](#source-selected-retrieval-scope) and when the notebook's visible sources changed after the question's scope was frozen. Whether collection reads are bound by the source ceiling is decided once per retrieval run: they are when the scope is narrowed or has drifted, and always in a global question, where each participating library keeps its own frozen visible-source list. The collection map, every listing and every count are then taken inside the ceiling, and a listing taken under a narrowed or drifted scope says so: the `enumerate` trace step carries `detail.source_scoped=true` (absent otherwise), the reflect prompt adds one sentence telling the model that listings cover only the selected sources, and the step summary, the enumeration ledger fed back to the model and the listing's section header in the synthesis evidence block carry their suffixes from one rule, in this order: “（限指定来源）” for an element listing restricted to one source, “（仅当前笔记本）” for a current-notebook roster, and “（仅勾选的来源）” whenever the listing is source-scoped. Each typed collection result carries `source_scoped: true`, and the key is omitted when false, so an unscoped response keeps its exact bytes; the result card appends “（仅勾选的来源）” after its scope suffix (a single-source card names the document instead of saying “（限指定来源）”). A global question's listings are not marked: their ceiling is each library's whole visible-source list, not a selection. The mark is sticky and is not part of the continuation key: when the source set drifts while a listing is in progress, the same listing continues from where it stopped — no restart, no second budget charge — and carries the mark. A continuation handle is bound to the source ceiling it was cut under; resuming it under a different ceiling reports a concurrent change instead of continuing.

**The reflect fallback step is a trace contract.** `reflect()`'s fail-open fallback (non-object response, invalid action, a JSON shape the validator rejected, a failed model call, an unconfigured model) must **identify itself** in the trace rather than masquerading as the model deciding the evidence was sufficient. A fallback turn's `reflect` step carries the sparse `detail` key `fallback_reason` (a stable machine code such as `invalid_enum`, `invalid_action:<action>`, `non_object`, `provider_rate_limited`, or `model_unconfigured`; non-fallback turns carry **no** such key) and a full-sentence Chinese `summary` — "反思结果无法采用（校验拒绝：`<reason>`），按直接作答处理" or "反思结果无法采用（模型调用失败），按直接作答处理". The marker lives in dedicated boolean/code fields on the decision, never as a prefix on `reason`: `reason` is model-authored free text, and putting the verdict there would let the thing being judged write its own verdict.

**Section-hint sparse key.** In a turn that actually computed the section-hint block (see [Section navigation inside one document](#section-navigation-inside-one-document-browse_sections--read_section)), the `reflect` step's `detail` carries the sparse key `section_hints`: `{sources, entries, vectors_read, vector_loads, process_cache_hits, vector_ms}` — the number of sources ranked, the number of hints listed, and that turn's increment in the retrieval layer's section-vector reads (vector rows read, read operations, process-cache hits, read time). It is written only when the turn really read or borrowed vectors (a non-zero `vector_loads` or `process_cache_hits` increment) or the block is non-empty; with the gate closed, `read_section` unavailable, or no computation in that turn the key is absent. `vector_ms` is wall-clock milliseconds, a diagnostic only and never a comparison baseline.

**Enumerable collections.** Source elements: `formula` / `table` / `image` / `code_block` (paragraph, heading, and other high-volume/low-signal kinds are deliberately excluded). Knowledge objects: `concept` / `claim` / `formula` / `procedure`, restricted to usable statuses. Both whitelists have exactly one source of truth (`app.services.collection_catalog`); nothing else may hold a second copy. The sources collection has no sub-type — a library's document roster is one whole collection.

**Source listing (which documents are in here).** Requesting `enumerate.collection:"sources"` (the other enumerate parameters are then ignored — the roster has no sub-type, and any other value of the field falls back to the action's own type) lists every document in scope, in the order the source tab shows them (by creation time, then id — so a truncated listing's prefix is the documents added first, the only reading of "the first N" the interface supports): display title (a grounded paper title wins over the upload name, the same rule citations follow), document type (the interface label from the upload picker's own type registry, omitted when the type was never detected), and an excerpt of the summary the library has already stored. It lists exactly what the source tab lists — the same user-visible-source predicate — so an answer can never show a document card the user cannot see in the source tab (Memory synthetic rows and a Knowhow table's hidden projection row are in neither). Its purpose is to let "analyse the articles in this notebook" or "which papers are in here" start from the roster and then go deeper per title through the ordinary follow-up-subquery mechanism, rather than sampling passages from whichever documents matched. It reads no document text and makes no model call; its cost is one bounded read per participating library plus one batched lookup per page. When a roster reaches answer synthesis, the prompt also carries a granularity instruction: a roster small enough to treat individually is answered document by document, a larger one is organized by theme with the documents named under each dimension. That judgement is the model's — it holds the exact count and knows how much the question wants per document — and no numeric threshold is applied anywhere.

**Reading one document's original text (`read_document`).** The source listing gives only a title, a type, and a stored summary; a row with no stored summary previously left the model with nothing better than a relevance search (`add_subquery`) to guess what that document was about. `read_document` closes that gap: within the same roster the source listing already resolved, it picks one document by title (copied verbatim from the listing) and samples its original text in document order, answering "what is this document about" rather than the "where is X mentioned" question `search_chunks` answers. The action can **only** open a document a previous `enumerate.collection="sources"` call already listed this run — list the roster first, then come back to read; a title that matches zero or more than one row in the roster is skipped, with the trace explaining why (zero matches means the title was mistyped and a verbatim retry will work; more than one match means the title was copied without its ordinal — the roster already numbers same-titled documents, see below — and copying it together with the ordinal works; several untitled documents are numbered the same way, see below), and it never degrades into a full-library title scan. What the model sees in the reflect round is the roster ledger: each title in its display form (an untitled document shows as the unnamed-source placeholder, long titles are cut to 60 characters, internal whitespace collapsed), and every row without a stored summary carries a `(无摘要)` marker — that marker is the read-selection cue; the ledger never carries summary text. **Same-titled documents get an ordinal.** Only when the run's roster (every source listing of the run, folded by document — one roster across libraries, not decided per library) contains same-titled documents does the ledger list those documents as `title（第 1 篇）`, `title（第 2 篇）`, … (numbers are issued in first-listed order and **never change once issued**, every one of them carrying its number), and the model copies one back verbatim to read exactly that document; the action's parameter is still just the title string, so its shape does not change. There is one numbering book per run: when a title group first reaches two documents both get their numbers at once, later same-titled documents take the next number, and neither an earlier listing chain being continued (which can slot new rows in front) nor a real title that only shows up later and happens to equal an already-issued placeholder ever alters an issued number — so an old string the model copied (including one in its own outline notes) keeps pointing at the document it was issued for. In the latter case the old string and that real title both match and the read is skipped as a same-title ambiguity rather than silently picking one. The ledger, title resolution, the already-read ledger, the read steps' trace summaries, and the source-name parameter of `enumerate_elements` (a placeholder is first translated into the roster document it was issued for, then targeted; before translating, book marks, the `(无摘要)` marker and a whole copied line are stripped exactly as title resolution does) all read that one book. When the copied string is at the same time the real title of a later-listed document, both readers reach the same verdict — ambiguity: `read_document`'s skip text then says the documents cannot be told apart (it no longer tells the model to copy the ordinal too, since the ordinal form is itself ambiguous), and `enumerate_elements` takes the existing "name matches more than one source" skip; neither silently picks one. "Same-titled" is judged on the form the model can see (whitespace collapsed, cut to 60 characters, surrounding whitespace and letter case ignored), so two titles that differ only after character 60 are numbered too. An ordinal placeholder, when issued, avoids every real title known at that point: when a real title happens to be `X（第 2 篇）`, the placeholder moves to the next spelling (`X（同名第 2 篇）`, then `X（同名第 2 篇·2）`, …), so among the titles known at issue time a real title matches only itself and a placeholder only itself. Untitled documents follow the same numbering rule (user decision, 2026-10-28): with two or more of them in the run's roster each becomes 「未命名来源（第 N 篇）」 (one untitled document stays un-numbered, as a single title does; a document whose real title happens to be 「未命名来源」 displays the same way and is numbered with them), and the resolver, the read ledger, the trace summaries, `enumerate_elements` and the in-document navigation echoes (`browse_sections` listings, `read_section` reads and the section hint block) all use the same numbers. They share a small sub-budget instead of each taking a title slot: all untitled entries of one listing together still occupy exactly the one title slot (and the same characters of the 800-character budget) the single placeholder took before, at the position of the first untitled row, so how many real titles are listed, in what order, and the `(+N more)` count do not depend on how many untitled documents there are. Inside that slot the first N untitled rows of the listing, in listing order, are shown with their numbers, where N is the run's effective per-run `read_document` cap (`REASONING_MAX_DOCUMENT_READS`, default 4: an untitled document usually has no summary either, so reading it is what the model can do with it, and listing more handles than the run can read adds nothing actionable); the rest are folded into `(另有 N 篇未命名来源从略)`. The `(+N more)` count after the titles counts only real titles that were not listed; the untitled rows report themselves through the group and its fold. Folded documents keep their numbers and resolve by them all the same. With no untitled document the ledger and the resolver are byte-for-byte what they were; with one, only the `(+N more)` count can differ (it used to be one short whenever an untitled document was listed). A roster with no same-titled documents renders and resolves byte-for-byte as before. Title resolution applies a few **deterministic** rewrites to what the model copied back before matching exactly: a copied `(无摘要)` marker, one pair of book-title marks or quotes, the `title · type: summary` tail of a copied preview line, and equality with the ledger's own truncated/collapsed form — none of them is fuzzy; a title that still differs after these rewrites stays unresolved. The `coverage` parameter picks the sampling shape: `"spread"` (the default — evenly spaced positions that always include the document's last element, since conclusions tend to live there) or `"opening"` (the first elements only, the cheapest useful read) — a string enum rather than a boolean, for the same reason as `enumerate.scope` above, so a model that leaves it blank still gets a working default. What comes back is always a **bounded sample** carrying its own coverage disclosure; the answer may only cite what the sample (or a stored summary) actually shows, never claim the whole document was read. A run may read at most `REASONING_MAX_DOCUMENT_READS` (default 4) documents this way, drawing on two run-level budget pools — one of elements (reusing `DOCUMENT_OVERVIEW_MAX_ELEMENTS`, the same knob "document introductions in general Q&A" uses) and one of characters (a quarter of the tier's `chunk_context_chars`). The `depth` parameter decides how much of what remains one read may spend: `"brief"` (the default) splits the remaining pools evenly across the reads still allowed, so an early read never exhausts the pool for documents read afterward — it suits introducing several documents; `"thorough"` hands this one document everything that remains (still minus what earlier reads used and the per-read header reserve) — it suits introducing one or a few documents, and a later read will usually find the budget spent and be skipped. Like `coverage` it is a string enum; case and surrounding whitespace are tolerated (`"Thorough"` reads as `"thorough"`), any other value reads as `"brief"`, and the next reflect round's ledger says so, so the model does not plan later reads around a budget it never got. Sampled text enters the synthesis evidence block through its own `[k]` key range, placed right after the source-listing preview: the model sees "which documents this library holds" first, then "which of them I actually opened and how much"; the result card is still the same source-listing card, with no new card type. The evidence and coverage constraints on sampled text hold for every question (only what a sample or a stored summary shows may be cited; **a complete directory listing is not the same as having read every document**); the per-document introduction **shape** applies only when the question asks what the documents are about (an overview of what each document covers): each sampled document then gets its own paragraph headed by its title, its research question, method, and contribution written only from that document's own sample or stored summary with the gap stated explicitly when the evidence falls short, and a document with neither a stored summary nor a sample this round is named as lacking sufficient evidence to introduce, never silently skipped and never guessed from its title alone. A focused question (comparing one method across two papers) uses the samples solely as evidence for that question and is never forced into a directory walkthrough or into introducing documents it did not ask about. This action shares the collection-enumeration gate's discipline through its own switch, `REASONING_DOCUMENT_READ_ENABLED` (default on): when any required condition fails (deployment switch off, no source port, no roster listed this run, the read cap at zero, or a budget configuration too tight to afford even one document), the action disappears from the prompt, the schema, and the allow-list together — the model never sees or picks it, and reasoning Ask reverts byte-for-byte to how it behaved before this feature. It shares the same gate as the rest of collection enumeration. Narrowing the retrieval scope by source does not withdraw it: the roster lists only the selected sources, and before reading anything the action checks the chosen document against the question's source ceiling and, in a global question, against the participating libraries. A document outside them is treated exactly like a title that is not in the roster — the same message and the same trace entry — and nothing from it reaches the prompt, the trace or the citations.

**A listing never contains private Memory.** A confirmed Memory belongs to one user, and every other channel already treats it that way: Ask reaches it only through the owner-scoped Memory retriever, and Knowhow completion excludes it from its candidate set by contract. A collection listing is scoped to a notebook's participants and has no owner filter of its own, so a Memory left in scope would be readable by every member of a shared notebook through its formulas, tables, images, code blocks, and the knowledge objects extracted from it. Both the map's counts and both executors therefore exclude the hidden Memory source and its objects — unconditionally, in a one-person notebook exactly as in a shared one, so one listing always means one thing. (The Knowhow projection source stays in: it is notebook-wide content already visible through the table itself.) This is deliberately narrower than the board's own knowledge count, which answers "how much does this notebook hold" and legitimately includes Memory-derived objects. An enumerated object's evidence references never point at a private Memory element either, so its citation card never quotes Memory text.

**What a binding ceiling admits.** When the ceiling binds, a knowledge object is listed and counted only when at least one of its evidence items comes from a source inside the ceiling — the predicate is applied below the page's `LIMIT` and re-checked on every returned row — so an object with no evidence is not listed; in a global question this also leaves out objects supported only by a library's hidden Knowhow projection source. A listed object keeps its section breadcrumb only when the source it was extracted from is inside the ceiling; otherwise the breadcrumb is omitted and the name is kept. An object's evidence references are filtered by the ceiling before they are cut to their bound, so its citation still reaches an in-ceiling element when out-of-ceiling references come first. Naming a source outside the ceiling is refused exactly like naming a source that does not exist, so the refusal cannot reveal whether an unticked document exists. A source added after the scope was frozen is outside the ceiling; if it is already there at the question's first collection read, that question's collection reads bind the ceiling, so the new source is not counted, listed, named or cited, and every listing carries “（仅勾选的来源）”. When the source ceiling binds (a narrowed or drifted scope, or a global question), a source added while a listing is in progress is outside the ceiling: it is not listed and does not make the listing report a change, while reparsing an in-ceiling source still does. When it does not bind (every source ticked and nothing drifted when the question first read a collection — the interface's default), a single-notebook question gets exactly the map, listings, counts and continuation handles an unscoped question gets. Each collection read of such a question still checks the sources it reads against the frozen list: the first read that sees a source added after the freeze records the drift, that question's collection reads bind the ceiling from then on, and the listing carries “（仅勾选的来源）”. So a source added after the freeze is never counted, listed, named or cited, and a listing it interrupts stays complete over the frozen sources.

**Collection map (count before list).** Before any of these tools is worth calling, a single line such as `[Collections in scope] elements: formula 12 (3 sources), table 5, image 0, code_block 0 | KG objects: concept 1234, claim 567, formula 89, procedure 0 | knowhow tables: 2 | sources: 7 (current notebook: 2)` (every whitelisted kind/type is always present, zero-valued when absent, so the model can tell "counted zero" apart from "not reported at all"; capped at 600 characters) is built once per run and injected into the plan/reflect context, scoped to the active notebook plus its currently valid mounted reference libraries. Counting is index-assisted and carries no source titles, file names, or excerpted text — it is prompt scaffolding, not evidence. The map's per-source count set is exactly the set the enumeration executor walks, by construction, so a discrepancy between "the map said N" and "the list returned M" cannot occur. The trailing `sources` count is the user-visible document count (the same figure the source tab and the document-limit check use) and comes out of the same helper as the source listing's denominator. It is the one count rendered **twice** — the federated total, then the active notebook's share in parentheses — because the source roster is the only collection whose enumeration takes a scope (`enumerate.scope`), so the model choosing between the two scopes has to see both numbers; in a single-notebook question the parenthesised figure is unconditional, so "the two happen to be equal" never looks like "the second number is missing". These counts have a second consumer inside the server: the denominator the oversize-listing guard compares against the run's remaining row allowance (see Budget and resumption) is whichever of them matches the request being made — same collection, same kind, same scope. The `sources` roster takes the federated total, or the parenthesised active-notebook figure when the request narrows to `current_notebook`; an element or KG-object listing takes that kind's or that type's own count. This is why the map **object** — not only its rendered line — is kept for the rest of the run. That costs no extra query: it is the same build, simply not thrown away after rendering. When the map holds no matching count — it could not be built at all, or the request narrows to a single source, for which the map has no figure — the guard does not fire: "unknown size" is not "known to be huge".

In a global question there is no current notebook: the map omits the parenthesised current-notebook share, and the document roster has no `scope` choice — the prompt does not describe it, the schema does not offer it, and a value the model sends anyway is ignored — so the roster always covers every selected library. The map's `knowhow tables` counts only the tables the Knowhow complete enumeration can actually read: the current notebook's own, and none when the source scope is narrowed, when the notebook's sources changed after the question's scope was frozen, or in a global question; mounted reference libraries' tables are not counted, because nothing enumerates them.

The same line also reaches the model that writes the final answer, as a short server-computed block at the head of the source evidence partition (a fixed header plus the capped map line, under 800 characters, carrying no `[k]` id because it is deterministic server output rather than a retrieved item). This closes a real gap: the reflect prompt tells the model that a collection far larger than the run's listing allowance should be answered with its count instead of paged through — and answer synthesis is a separate call that would otherwise never see that number — in the extreme case (a large collection, nothing else retrieved) synthesis would not have run at all.
