The block is injected whenever the tools are on and the map built, whether or not anything was enumerated, and it is placed ahead of every other block so a full evidence budget cannot make it the first casualty.

**Coverage contract.** Every enumerated collection carries a `TypedCollectionCoverage`: `returned_total` (rows returned so far across a resumed chain), `total` (the map's known size, or `null` when the size could not be established — rendered as an unknown denominator, never as `/0`), `complete`, `truncated_reason` (`budget` / `payload` / `concurrent_change`), and `overflow_semantics` (the shared `explicit_partial`). `complete=true` requires cursor exhaustion, a stable scope identity taken before the first page and after the last, and — across a resumed chain — that the running total matches the known size; anything else is `complete=false`. That scope identity includes the set of participating libraries itself, re-resolved when the walk closes: mounting, unmounting or invalidating a reference library part-way through changes what “the whole scope” means, so the result is reported as a concurrent change rather than as “all”. Alongside coverage, the result also carries `synthesis_rows` / `synthesis_complete`: the enumerated list and the bounded preview that actually entered the answer-synthesis prompt are tracked separately, so "enumerated 200/200, previewed 100" is disclosed as "enumeration complete, analysis partial" — mirroring the Knowhow batch's own enumeration/synthesis split. That preview allowance is shared across a run's collections and split rather than handed out first-come-first-served: each list is reserved an equal share first, then whatever a short list cannot fill is passed along in order. A run that enumerated two collections therefore previews both, instead of spending the whole allowance on the first and answering a multi-collection question from one list.

**Citation and attribution contract.** Every delivered source-element or KG-object row carries at most one bounded citation to a live original source element; for a KG object this is the first still-live id from its already bounded evidence-reference list. Mounted-library evidence is resolved server-side inside the active notebook's authorized participant set. The browser receives only the source title, location, locator and excerpt and never calls a mounted library's member-only source endpoint. Every row that actually enters the synthesis preview receives an isolated `k5001+` id and reverse binding. The model must cite that id whenever it uses the row, and only those bound row anchors count as attribution for the final answer. A source-backed exact deterministic row can therefore be grounded without pretending it had a semantic relevance score; an orphaned row may still be listed and cited as a row, but cannot make the answer grounded. Conversely, if an enumeration answer binds no anchor, the response exposes no unrelated ranked-retrieval fallback citations as though they sourced the list. The result card shows each row's original-source citation; both local and mounted-library rows may open the exact source element through the active-notebook proxy, while mounted sources remain read-only. A historical KG row whose referenced elements have all disappeared is labeled as having no available original source rather than receiving a fabricated citation. Document, element and knowledge-object rows each get a citation only from an element whose source is inside the question's source ceiling (the first such element that is still live). In a global question, a row is cited only when its library is one of the libraries the question resolved and froze, each with its own source ceiling; the naming anchor's mounts play no part, so every selected library's rows are citable and a library mounted on the anchor but not selected is neither listed nor cited. A single-notebook question keeps checking the notebook's valid mounts.
**UI presentation.** The Ask result card always shows its coverage badge, collection title, and optional single-source scope, but starts with its item content collapsed. Opening it mounts the grouped source elements or KG objects and shows the existing 20-item preview; a second control expands any additional loaded items. Partial-result and synthesis-preview disclosures live inside the collapsible content, and image rows are not mounted or fetched while the card remains closed.

**Budget and resumption.** One action pages automatically within its run-wide budget (`enum_rows_per_run` total rows, `enum_pages_per_run` extra page round trips, and the shared `structured_payload_chars` structured-payload ceiling) until the cursor is exhausted or a ceiling fires; only the second and later page of each visited partition (a source, for elements; a participating notebook, for KG objects) counts against the page ceiling, since a partition's first page is the only way to see it at all. All three ceilings are **per request, not per action**: each action receives only what the run has left, so several enumerations in one deep run can never return more structured payload in total than the documented request-wide ceiling. The payload ceiling is enforced twice, on two different measurements, because they answer two questions: the executor charges the compact internal row while it walks (that rail stops the traversal from reading more than the request may produce), and the response mapping then charges the *serialized* row — the shape that is actually streamed and persisted, which is materially wider. A row the second rail has to stop short reports its own `truncated_reason=payload` with `returned_total` equal to what was delivered, and the synthesis preview is rendered from the delivered list, so the prompt's coverage header and the result card always state the same number. That cursor is a run-internal handle — it never appears in the response; the client sees only the coverage badge and, when truncated, that the same reasoning run can keep listing further. `complete=false` always implies a resumable cursor, with exactly one exception: `truncated_reason=concurrent_change`, where the scope moved between calls and the chain must not silently restart. A repeated request for a not-yet-complete collection resumes from that cursor when the run's budget still has rows/pages/payload left; when the run's budget is exhausted instead, the request is skipped as budget-exhausted (still reported as a partial result) rather than as already enumerated. Only a collection whose chain already reached `complete=true` is skipped as already enumerated, since asking again could only repeat rows already reported.

**Scoping to one named source.** Internal source ids are never shown to the model — candidate summaries and citations carry source titles — so an element enumeration is narrowed to a single document by title. The server resolves that title deterministically against the sources the map already plans to visit for the requested kind: an exact match after trimming and case folding, never a fuzzy or ranked match, and bounded so a large mounted library cannot turn one reflection into a full label sweep. A title that matches nothing, or more than one source, skips the action and says so in the trace; it never silently widens into a whole-scope enumeration of a different question, and it never guesses one of several same-titled documents. When the scope holds more sources of that kind than the resolver is allowed to examine, it declines outright rather than answering from the part it did read: uniqueness is a property of the whole scope, and a second source with the same title could sit anywhere beyond the examined range.

**Knowledge-object listing on notebooks with a long governance history.** The knowledge-object page walk is a pure keyset read over `(notebook, type, created_at, id)`; deprecated and other unusable objects are filtered after the read, by the very same usable-status definition the map's counts use. Filtering after the read is what keeps one page O(page size) on a notebook where most objects of a type have been deprecated — a status predicate inside that query would have no index to ride and would visit an unbounded number of rows. The extra reading that filtering costs is itself bounded per action; when that ceiling fires, the result is an ordinary honest partial (`truncated_reason=budget`) with a resumable cursor, never a quietly shortened list presented as complete.

**Notebooks without a knowledge graph.** `search_chunks` performs semantic-plus-keyword passage search using the same `chunk_context_chars` evidence partition and citations as chunk Q&A. `read_document` samples one already-listed document in source order, and `browse_sections` / `read_section` move through one document's heading outline (see [Section navigation inside one document](#section-navigation-inside-one-document-browse_sections--read_section)). All of them are available on graph-bearing runs too. **First-round passage recall and per-direction backfill do not look at the knowledge graph**: whether or not the scope has one, the first round deterministically seeds passages per sub-query and, when whole-question high-/low-level keywords exist (from `plan()` when it ran, from the understanding step on the confirmed-intent path — see above), adds one lexical query from them, cut to the same per-sub-query width before merging. The **selection step** of passage search (one method shared by the `search_chunks` action, the first-round seed and direction backfill) is likewise independent of the knowledge graph: when `retrieval_rerank` is configured, the top `REASONING_CHUNK_RERANK_CANDIDATES` (default 50) baseline candidates by fused score go to a cross-encoder after recall (generated-question supplements are reranked separately after the baseline), and passages are taken in rerank order with the active-notebook floor still applied; unconfigured, a failed rerank, exceeding `REASONING_CHUNK_RERANK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 10 s), a pool no larger than the number of passages to take, `REASONING_CHUNK_RERANK_CANDIDATES=0` or `REASONING_CHUNK_RERANK_ENABLED=false` falls back to MMR selection; failures and timeouts only emit an event, never a banner, and cancellation still stops the run. Rerank decides which passages are selected; it never rewrites relevance, and the order within synthesis still follows the assembly order below. The confirmed-direction coverage pass and `add_subquery` likewise each add one passage recall next to their KG search. The only gate is the passage-search switch (`REASONING_CHUNK_SEARCH_ENABLED` plus the caller's policy bit, which knowhow completion turns off). On a graph-bearing run the passage partition is shared by concept-walk (PPR) passages and this seed, and Ask synthesis and deep-report section drafting (the latter for passages no outline item bound; bound passages still come first) share one assembly order: relevance descending, then two interleaved lanes (concept-walk passages and retrieved passages, each in its own relevance order; the former carry a per-run normalized score and the latter an absolute fused score, which are not comparable), then the first `REASONING_EXACT_RESERVE` exact-lookup passages take the prefix seats, then at most `REASONING_SECTION_READ_RESERVE` (default 6) passages a `read_section` read back whole (`section_read`) take the seats directly behind them in their current order (a section read is moved forward only by these seats; unlike an exact hit it is never injected across sections by per-section synthesis), and directly behind those the library prefix: when reference-library passages compete, up to `min(CHUNK_MMR_K, ceil(CHUNK_MMR_K × CHUNK_FEDERATION_ACTIVE_RESERVE))` seats (4 at the defaults) minus the active passages already in the exact and section-read prefix (an active section read back spends a seat here; it carries the notebook's own id and counts as active) move qualified active passages (the qualification and first-copy-per-text identity of the mix seats) forward in their current order; a Global Ask run, which has no subject library, shares those seats per library as the mix cut does. It is a reordering only — nothing is dropped — and inert with no reference-library passage (the concept-walk passages carry the notebook's own id and count as its own), so a notebook with no mounted library keeps its exact order. Exact passages do not alternate: they stay anchored at their relevance position, so a named section larger than the seat still stays together near the front. Relevance values are never rewritten. The prefix is a mechanical-cut rule only: per-section synthesis applies it inside each section's own outline-bound passages and never injects an unbound active passage into a section (only the user-named exact hits are injected), and deep-report drafting keeps outline-bound passages first — an active one among them already spends a seat — then the exact prefix, then the library prefix among the unbound passages. **Passage floor.** The structured blocks single-shot synthesis assembles ahead of the passages in the same partition — the Knowhow preview, the enumeration preview, sampled document reads and the spreadsheet block — are first rendered exactly as before. `floor = min(chunk_context_chars / 2, heading + rendered)`, where `rendered` is what the passage segment really spends on the prefix passages (exact seats, section-read seats and library seats): `kN: ` plus the text per line, one newline between lines, after the same same-source de-duplication the segment applies, and `heading` is the segment's `[Retrieved chunks]` heading with its joiner (21 characters); the half-partition cap keeps the structured side's own share. Only when that historical structured side is longer than `chunk_context_chars − floor` (less the collection map block that precedes it) — that is, only when it would push part of the reserved prefix out of the prompt — is it rendered again with that total as a ceiling: each block keeps its own budgets (the enumeration and document-read half-partition caps still read the whole `chunk_context_chars`) and is shrunk only when it would cross what is left; the roster reserves room for the document read only if that read then fits, and a document-read or spreadsheet block left out only for this ceiling leaves a one-line notice when the notice fits. Each block's own coverage disclosure states exactly what it shows (a partial preview says partial). Section-read seats count toward the floor, so in a turn that read a section back the structured side (Knowhow preview, enumeration preview, sampled document reads, spreadsheet block) is re-rendered smaller when it overflows. Every other run — no passage, no reserved seat, or a structured side that leaves the prefix whole — is byte-for-byte unchanged; the exact-seat part of the floor applies to a notebook without mounted libraries too and has no switch. When the prefix costs more than half the partition, the capped floor keeps the structured side at least half and the rest of the prefix may still be cut, as before. The first-round seed's recall concurrency shrinks with the participant count (recall workers × federated legs ≤ 8); rerank takes no database connection and runs concurrently per sub-query (at most 8), queued by the rerank service's own concurrency limit. These keywords are minted in the corpus languages. On the confirmed-intent path they come from the understanding step, and the arm does not run when it gave none or confirmation dropped them. `REASONING_MAX_CHUNK_SEARCHES` caps later search actions, excluding the initial seed.

**The optional `search_chunks` keyword parameter `keywords`.** In a reflect reply the single-argument actions `search_elements`, `exact_lookup`, `ppr_retrieve`, `expand_community` and `search_chunks` share one root-level search string, `query` (each reads it only when it is the chosen action; the outline scratchpad's section list likewise sits at the root as `outline_sections`, and unused branches and fields are written as null). Besides the search string `query`, the model may give a space-separated keyword string; after the semantic search the server runs one keyword full-text search with it (the same channel and the same scope as chunk-native Q&A's keyword supplement arm: a single-notebook ask searches only this notebook, a global ask federates per library), cuts the hits to the action's own width (`CHUNK_MMR_K`) and merges them, to recover the literal matches semantic search tends to miss — model numbers, terms, command names, code identifiers. The reflect prompt lists the run's **corpus languages** (the notebook's own for a single-notebook ask, the union over participating libraries for a global ask, falling back to zh/en when nothing was probed or the probe failed — a failed probe never fails the ask — and not probed at all while the keyword sub-gate is closed) and asks for keywords in those languages with their cross-language equivalents, abbreviations and full names, without identifiers the question does not name, even ones seen in the candidates (a different model number or command is a different thing, not another form of the named one), and without guessed answer values, while each term the question does name still carries its forms in the other corpus languages and its abbreviation or full name: the keyword arm scores coverage of the whole string, so extra terms dilute the match, and in a real-model spot check one padded string pushed the gold passage under the relevance floor. Left empty, the action searches by `query` alone and its trace and behaviour are what they were before the parameter existed; given, the step's trace adds `keywords` and `keyword_found`. When the keyword search fails the semantic half is kept and no banner is shown: a search failure inside the channel only emits one `ask_stage` event (`stage="chunk_keyword_union"`, exception class name only) — chunk-native Q&A's keyword supplement behaves the same way — while a failure of the channel call itself also adds `keyword_failed` to the trace; strict mode raises, and cancellation or a retrieval control error (`RetrievalControlError`) still ends the run. The keyword string (joined with spaces when the model writes it as a list) is truncated to 300 characters when parsed, leading whitespace not counted. An action with keywords still counts once against `REASONING_MAX_CHUNK_SEARCHES`. With the passage-search switch off, or when the keyword arm can return nothing this run (a global ask with `GLOBAL_ASK_KEYWORD_ARM_ENABLED=false`), the field appears in neither the schema, the prompt nor the parser — the model is shown exactly the parameters that take effect; under the same condition the first-round seed's lexical arm does not run either (the seed step's trace carries no `keyword_found`, the same shape as a run with no whole-question keywords).

Without a graph, `expand_graph`, `ppr_retrieve`, `expand_community`, `follow_chain` and `enumerate_kg_objects` are removed from the action enum, prompts and allow-list. Source and element enumeration remain available. The trace discloses 「本笔记本尚未整理知识图谱,本轮只用原文检索与集合清单」; `kg_required=True` keeps the graph-building suggestion without itself refusing an answer. A global ask removes `ppr_retrieve` the same way, with or without a graph: its producer is closed in a global ask (it would only search the naming anchor), so it always returns empty; `search_elements` stays in a global ask, federated per library, and is removed only when `GLOBAL_ASK_ELEMENT_ARM_ENABLED=false` (see the global-scope section); single-notebook runs keep both. When the model names a known core action this run does not offer (whichever gate removed it — no graph, global ask, effort tier or deployment switch), the trace records a skip step 「跳过模型所选的检索动作(本次检索不提供它)」 (`reason="action_not_offered"`, with the action name) and the reflect loop carries on under its usual stale and step limits instead of ending; only a name outside the core action set takes the invalid-action fallback (`invalid_action:<name>`), and strict callers still raise for any action not on the allow-list.

For a run without a restricted source scope, internal admission requires at least one usable lane: `REASONING_ENUM_TOOLS_ENABLED` with nonempty participant-set source/element/object counts, or `REASONING_CHUNK_SEARCH_ENABLED` with visible sources in the passage participant set. Passage retrieval is federated; only disabling `CHUNK_FEDERATION_ENABLED` returns its admission count to `active_sources`. The collection-map count does not subtract libraries past `CHUNK_FEDERATION_MAX_PARTICIPANTS`, so admission can be wider than the bounded producer set. Both lanes disabled, both empty, or failure to build the collection map takes the deterministic early exit: 「当前笔记本没有可检索的来源；请先添加来源，或挂载/整理一个已建知识图谱的参考库。」

A restricted source scope has an earlier, separate admission path: a nonempty include scope (or internal exclude scope) passes before these two lane switches are checked, because the selected documents always leave something to read. Enumeration remains available under that restriction and follows the source ceiling.

**HTTP availability follows the same passage lane.** `NotebookSummary.ask_available` has two reference-library criteria: a mounted library with a usable knowledge graph, **or** a mounted library whose visible sources have chunks that the federated passage lane will search. So a notebook with no local evidence (`local_evidence_available=false`) that mounts only a graphless reference library with parsed text is askable end to end: the browser composer is enabled and a direct Ask request is not refused with 409. The passage half uses the lane's own reach. Only mounts effective for the viewer count (a private library the viewer cannot read is not in their `base_notebooks` and props up nothing), and only chunks of visible sources count (a library holding only Knowhow cells or Memory projections does not, because those never enter the cross-library lane). It reads the same `CHUNK_FEDERATION_ENABLED` switch and the same `CHUNK_FEDERATION_MAX_PARTICIPANTS` bound in `MOUNT_ORDER`: a library past the bound is not searched and does not count, and with federation off no reference-library text counts. The frontend `isAskBlocked` and the route's 409 pre-check both read this one field, so all three agree by construction; the single-library empty-scope refusal asks the same judgement narrowed to the checked libraries (see the **409 "empty scope"** paragraph). The check runs only on the single-notebook summary and only when the notebook has no local evidence. It is a single `EXISTS` statement whose text does not change with the mount count, and it is skipped when nothing is mounted. The notebook list does not compute `ask_available` (it stays `true` there), so the list path is unchanged.

**Scope words are not search terms.** Phrases like “当前notebook”, “这个库”, “本库”, “整个库”, “the current notebook”, “this library”, “知识图谱 / KG” name the notebook the user has open together with its mounted scope — the scope every retrieval already runs in, not content that can be found inside it; no document contains the name of the library holding it. Intent understanding, both planning prompts and the reflect loop are therefore all told to resolve such a phrase into the scope and then **drop** it: never into a sub-query, a keyword or an exact term, while keeping the rest of the question intact (“what do the articles in this notebook say” is about those documents, and dropping the scope words must not turn it into a different question). A question about the library itself — how much it holds, what kinds of material, how many documents — is answered from the count line above and these enumerate actions, not by searching for the words. This is deliberately prompt-level only, with no deterministic strip list: a phrase table that edited user text would be lexical routing, and it would mangle the legitimate case of a document that genuinely discusses knowledge graphs.

**Counts follow a parse immediately.** Writing a source's elements advances that source's change signal in the same database transaction, so the per-source counts behind the map are invalidated the instant new elements commit. A source parsed a moment ago is therefore countable, plannable and listable right away — there is no window in which it reads as empty while its elements are already stored, and no wait for the status write that ends the parse. (An explicitly named `source_id` is still queried directly rather than inferred from the map, since one source the user pointed at is worth an index-seeked read.)

**Round-trip cost.** One enumeration action's page queries are bounded by its own budget, and the bound is enforced rather than assumed: sources with no items of the requested kind are never visited, and a source is only in the plan because items were counted in it, so visiting one produces rows — which the row allowance caps. Page allowance and row allowance therefore bound the round trips together. The first page of each visited partition stays free of the page allowance on purpose: charging it would make the ordinary shape of a real corpus — one formula each across a hundred sources — unable to reach complete coverage at any effort level.

**Cross-library items.** An item whose collection lives in a mounted reference library (not the active notebook) is labeled “来自参考库《名》”. Source-detail jumps and images use active-notebook proxy endpoints: the browser authorizes only against the notebook the user opened, while the server resolves the resource inside its current participant set. The mounted source remains read-only, and the browser never calls the reference library's member-only endpoint. The server may also include the bounded original-source citation described above, so cards and answer citation details can show the title, location and excerpt before a jump. A cross-library row of the SOURCE listing follows the same rule: it is labeled and it opens through the same proxy, because the document it names is exactly the resource that proxy resolves. One remaining honesty boundary is the disclosed count of sources parsed through a plain-text fallback (no structural parse), whose elements the element-kind enumeration cannot see at all: coverage states completeness only over elements that were actually stored, not over every source in scope.

**When the incomplete-result notice is omitted.** A completeness request that no executor can serve exactly ends with a brief notice that this answer has not been verified as complete; the answer does not lead with a catalog of supported collection types. The notice is suppressed only when four deterministic conditions hold together: the intent scope is not `aggregate`, the intent contract records no constraints, exclusions, or assumptions, at least one collection result card returned rows, and that card's coverage is `complete`. Anything else keeps the notice. The bias is intentionally toward warning too often: a card's coverage proves one physical collection was walked end to end, never that the physical collection is the filtered/grouped/deduplicated subset the question actually asked for — and there is no deterministic test for the latter, only a guess. Separately, an answer that carries the rendered paper table (`answer_layout=paper_table`) together with its coverage line omits the notice: that coverage line is the answer's single completeness statement — it says “可能还有更多” when the topic search has gaps and “不代表已列全” when no topic search ran — so a second, differently worded disclaimer after the table would only contradict it. Prose answers, and runs without a rendered paper table, keep the four-condition rule above.

The response's optional `completeness_notice` carries this server-written text for the Ask panel to render outside the model's Markdown, so an unclosed code fence cannot absorb it. Copying the answer still includes the notice. Responses without a notice omit the field.

The public conversation projection carries the same notice when present and renders it outside the shared answer Markdown too; its `answer_md` remains the stored answer text for reference selection and older clients.

`REASONING_ENUM_TOOLS_ENABLED=false` disables the enumeration actions and source-listing parameter. It does not disable the independent source-passage channel; admission can still read the collection map for that channel. The graphless early exit follows the lane and restricted-source rules above, not this switch alone.

### Section navigation inside one document (`browse_sections` / `read_section`)

**What it is for.** A specification's answer often sits in a chapter that passage search never reached: the model's search words stop at the vocabulary of the document's introduction while the chapter uses other words, and the document's whole table of contents is far too long to hand over. Two model-invoked reflect actions let the model move through **one document's heading outline** instead: `browse_sections` lists the outline (not evidence), `read_section` reads one whole section back as citable passages. Together with a vector **section-hint block** (below) they are the in-document counterpart of `search_chunks`, which finds passages across documents. They work on notebooks with or without a knowledge graph and are not tied to the source roster: the candidate documents are the sources that already appeared in this run's evidence plus the rows of any source listing, and a title the model copies is resolved with the same step-by-step exact matching as `read_document` (same-title ordinals included; zero or several matches skip with the same wording as `read_document`).

**One gate.** Both actions and the hint block are offered by a single predicate, `ReasoningRetriever.section_navigation_active`, read by the reflect prompt, the schema, the allow-list, the field parser, both executors' first line of defence, the first-round offered-action filter for experience rows and the hint computation: `REASONING_SECTION_NAV_ENABLED`, the caller's policy bit (Knowhow completion switches it off), `search_chunks` being active (so the same gate as passage search), an effort tier other than `overview`, a retrieval port that offers the three section methods, `REASONING_MAX_SECTION_BROWSES` + `REASONING_MAX_SECTION_READS` greater than zero, and `REASONING_SECTION_OUTLINE_MAX_ROWS` greater than zero. Each action then checks its own cap at execution. Below the gate, each action is also offered on its own: an action whose cap is `0`, or whose calls this run has already spent, disappears from the prompt, the schema and the allow-list (and the field parser ignores its request), exactly as if the gate were closed for that action alone; a model that names it anyway gets the generic `action_not_offered` skip, not a cap skip. Once `read_section` is unavailable this way, the hint block is not computed and listings stop suggesting `read_section`. When the gate is closed, prompt, schema, allow-list and hint block lose the feature together and the run is byte-identical to one without it. A model that names one of the two anyway gets the generic `action_not_offered` skip described above.

**The outline: heading occurrences, read at query time.** The outline is projected from the source's chunks (`chunks.section_path`, in document order, at most `REASONING_SECTION_OUTLINE_MAX_ROWS` chunks per source; a cut is disclosed as 「大纲只覆盖本篇前 N 段」); nothing is stored for it. A run of consecutive chunks with the same section path is one **occurrence**; the same title appearing again later is a different occurrence and is never merged. Navigation pages (table-of-contents and list-of-figures chunks, see above) are left out: an occurrence made only of them does not appear, and the flagged chunks of a mixed occurrence never enter a range. The hierarchy is generic and uses no label word list: breadcrumb sources by their ` > ` depth; flat sources by dotted numbering (`5.7.2.1`, `A.2`; a one-segment number such as `5` counts as a chapter only when the numbering sequence corroborates it, so `16 GT/s Data Rate` does not open a chapter); figure and table captions (`Table 5-18`), `Notes` and other unnumbered headings are **leaves** that never end the numbered section they sit in. A numbered parent that exists only through its children (a `5.7` that has chunks only under `5.7.1`, `5.7.2`, …) is synthesised as a **virtual node** owning no chunks of its own, so `read_section("5.7")` and the tree both work. A structural node's **range** runs from it to the next heading of the same or a higher level, so `5.7.3` contains `5.7.3.1`, the table captions after it and its `Notes`; a leaf's range is the leaf alone, and a document made only of leaves is not expanded into subtrees. `under` is a number prefix (`5.7` matches `5.7` and `5.7.*`, not `5.70`); a document without numbering refuses `under`, and the refusal tells the model to leave it empty or use `query`. A listing renders one line per entry, `[sN] title（N 段）`, indented by depth, within `REASONING_SECTION_BROWSE_MAX_CHARS`; a cut list ends with 「另有 K 条未列出，可用 under/query 收窄」.

**Addresses are a closed set.** Every section the model has been shown carries a run-local address `sN` (the hint block and `browse_sections` results issue them; only entries actually rendered are issued). `read_section.section` accepts an `sN`, or a title or number that is resolved inside the chosen source's outline (the outline is built once per run, so addresses stay stable): a unique match is used; when the same title exists in this library and in a reference library, this library's document wins (to read the reference library's, copy the roster's 「（第 N 篇）」 placeholder, which is accepted); several matches prefer the one whose range already holds a chunk of this run; still several → skip `section_ambiguous`, feeding back each candidate's `sN`; no match → `section_not_surfaced`. An address the run never issued is refused the same way. Addresses bypass `exact_probe_terms` entirely and cannot name anything outside what retrieval has already shown the run.

**`browse_sections`.** Parameters `source` (title of a document already seen this run — in its passage or element evidence, or a listed source roster; the owning library travels with it), `under` (a number prefix) and `query` (a few words). On the run's last allowed reflect turn it is not offered at all (its listing only feeds a next reflect round that will not happen; a call that still arrives is skipped as `section_browse_last_turn`, not counted), while `read_section`, whose passages are evidence, still is. With `query` empty the outline is listed in document order. With `query` the entries are ranked by the section-scoring rule below within `under`; when vector similarity cannot be obtained the listing falls back to document order and its header says 「向量不可用」. `query` is cut to `SECTION_QUERY_MAX_CHARS` (300) characters before ranking. A listing is **not evidence** and cannot be cited: it enters the next reflect round's summary, only the latest listing of each source is kept there (a newer one replaces it), and every browse or read is recorded one line each in the action ledger (titled 「章节导航记录」; executed entries read 「已浏览…」「已读…」, skipped ones are prefixed 「未执行:」) so the model does not repeat it. A round that newly delivered a listing without new evidence holds the stale counter where it is (neither advancing nor resetting it), like a consult or plugin delivery; `no_progress` itself keeps its meaning. The next reflect round then shows 「上一步列出了章节目录(目录不是证据)。可用 read_section 按 [sN] 读取…」 (without the `read_section` clause once reads are unavailable) in place of the generic "no new evidence, answer now" note, and the plugin off-site nudge is not added that round, because an unevidenced listing round is not an empty-handed search. A repeated `(source, under, query)` is not skipped: it records a `browse_sections` step with `detail.repeat: true`, puts the cached listing back as the source's latest one at zero I/O, does not count toward the cap and does not hold the stale counter. A listing that would be empty (nothing under `under`) is skipped as `section_under_empty`: it does not count and does not replace the source's previous listing. Each run has a cap. A failed read (outline or vectors) becomes a `section_browse_failed` skip, never an error that voids the ask: the attempt still counts, and cancellation (`AskCancelled`, `RetrievalControlError`) still propagates.

**`read_section`.** Parameters `source` (needed only when `section` is a title or number rather than an `sN`) and `section`. The whole section's chunk ids go to the retrieval layer, which keeps them in document order, drops navigation pages **before** counting, takes at most `REASONING_SECTION_READ_MAX_CHUNKS` (and never more than that setting, whatever the caller asks), and returns them as ordinary citable passages. They are de-duplicated into the run's passage evidence and **do not open a new evidence number range**; a section longer than the cap is cut to its first chunks and the trace step says so. When the outline scan (`REASONING_SECTION_OUTLINE_MAX_ROWS`) stopped inside a section — the range of the last scanned occurrence and of every section still open there, virtual parents included — that section may continue past what was read: its line in a listing, the hint block and an ambiguity reply reads 「（N 段，可能未完）」, and reading it, whether through a hint, a listing `sN` or a title, sets `truncated` and `scan_truncated` on the step and says 「大纲只覆盖本篇前 N 段,本节之后可能还有内容」. Each passage's relevance is the same ruler ordinary passage retrieval uses, `_fuse(keyword coverage, cosine to the question vector)`, with no floor, however the address was obtained. The passages carry a provenance flag `section_read` (not `exact_lookup`, which means “the user named it” and drives the exact reserve and per-section injection). A read that adds nothing counts toward the action's zero-hit nudge like other evidence actions. A repeated address is skipped, and each run has a cap. A failed read (resolving the outline or reading the section back) becomes a `section_read_failed` skip, never an error that voids the ask: the attempt still counts, the section stays in the repeat set so a persistent failure is not retried, and cancellation still propagates. When the exact-identifier shape gate rejects an `exact_lookup` term and this action is offered, the rejection feedback adds 「如果这是章节标题，请改用 browse_sections 或 read_section」.

**Permission lives in the retrieval layer.** `RetrievalPort.section_outline`, `section_chunk_similarities` and `section_chunks` check the run's source ceiling directly on `(notebook_id, source_id)`; in a peer-mode (Global Ask) run a library without its own ceiling is not a participant, and for any library that is not the run's own the source must also be one of that library's **visible** sources (the same list the passage channel's peer legs read), so another member's Memory or Knowhow projection is never outlined or read. A source outside the ceiling, a hidden one and one that does not exist all answer with the same empty result and no event, and the ceiling is judged before every memo read. `section_chunks` first checks that every chunk id belongs to the source's scanned outline, reads under the owning library's id (a mounted library's chunks stay attributed to their owner), and passes its output through the navigation filter and the same candidate filter `search_chunks` uses; the reasoning side calls through the same fan-out slot as passage search. Synthesis and the final answer apply no permission check of their own on these passages.

**The section-hint block.** Once the run holds passage evidence, the reflect summary may carry a block titled 「相关章节线索（可用 read_section 按章节读取原文）」, one line per entry (`[s3]《source title》 5.7.2.1 Loss and Crosstalk Mask（3 段）`), placed next to the consult and external-evidence blocks and before the collection map. It is computed lazily in the round-context builder: (1) **sources** are the first `REASONING_SECTION_HINT_SOURCES` sources, in order of first appearance, among the run's passage evidence, and only those whose outline has at least two real occurrences; (2) a section's **score** is the largest cosine similarity between any chunk vector in its range and any of the run's query vectors (the question and the queries actually executed, including confirmed directions that have run; directions not yet executed are left out because each would cost an embedding without having contributed evidence; the query vectors are the run's memoised embeddings, and new executed queries are the only new embedding work); (3) sections **already covered** — an occurrence holding one of the run's chunks of its own — and navigation sections are excluded, and ties by an ancestor are collapsed so a hit inside `5.7.2.1` yields `5.7.2.1`, not also `5.7.2`, the virtual `5.7` and `5`; (4) entries are merged across sources by rank (all rank-1 entries, then rank-2, …) and cut to `REASONING_SECTION_HINT_MAX_ENTRIES`, keeping only scores at least `REASONING_SECTION_HINT_RELATIVE_FLOOR` × the highest cosine any of the run's existing chunks reaches against the same query vectors — a relative threshold, so it survives swapping the embedding model; with no existing chunk able to produce a cosine there is no baseline and no block. Chunk vectors come from the notebook's warm vector matrix when it is already loaded (the check only peeks and never triggers a load; a large not-copyable notebook skips it), otherwise only the outline's own chunk vectors are read; vectors of another dimension than the query's are left out with a content-free `section_vectors_unavailable` event. A source's decoded vectors are held in a **process-level section vector cache** shared across runs (see Rails): its key is the database fingerprint, the library, the source, the source's `chunked_at`, a fingerprint of the outline's chunk ids and the query dimension, so re-chunking retires the entry; loads are single-flight, so concurrent first readers (parallel report sections) decode a source once; a source with no `chunked_at`, or with any outline chunk lacking a vector, is not cached (a source still being embedded would otherwise stay incomplete); `REASONING_SECTION_VECTOR_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` is its LRU byte budget and `0` disables it, in which case each run reads for itself. Known limitation: swapping the embedding model for one of the same dimension, or re-embedding a source in place without re-chunking it, is picked up only after the entry is evicted or the process restarts. `read_section` decodes only the vectors of the passages it reads, not the source's whole outline. Hint relevance is relative to the best chunk the run already holds, and the hint lists only sections not yet covered, which score lower than the covered ones the baseline comes from; this is why the default share is 0.5, and noise is bounded by the entry cap rather than by this threshold. The block is **fail-open**: unavailable vectors, a source without an outline or any error produce no block, no skip step and no banner (strict callers still raise). It is a hint, not evidence.

**Reserved seats at synthesis.** `section_read` passages are not injected section by section into outline synthesis. Instead the single passage order (`reasoning_passage_order`, shared by Ask synthesis and deep-report drafting) moves up to `REASONING_SECTION_READ_RESERVE` of them to directly behind the exact-lookup prefix (a section-read passage already inside that prefix keeps its seat there and spends none of this reserve), before the library-prefix step, so a section the model chose to read survives the `chunk_context_chars` partition. It is a reordering only: nothing is dropped, relevance is never rewritten, and `0` reserves none. The reserve is not split per library; the per-library floor normalises a passage stamped with the active notebook's id and an unstamped one as the same library.

**Trace, skip codes and experience.** The trace gains two step types. `browse_sections` carries `source`, `under`, `query` and `listed` (`listed` is deliberately not one of the evidence-count keys, so listing an outline is never counted as an evidence hit or a zero hit); its summary reads 「查看章节目录:《标题》 under 5.7,列出 N 条」. `read_section` carries `source`, `section`, `found` and `result_ids` (plus `truncated` when the section was cut); its summary reads 「按章节读取原文:《标题》 5.7.3 Standard Package,新增 N 段」. The Ask panel's step badges label them 「目录」 and 「章节」 (two characters, like the other badges, so they fit the fixed badge column). Skip steps never carry `result_ids`. The stable `detail.reason` codes are `section_nav_disabled` (defence in depth only), `section_browse_cap`, `section_browse_failed` (detail `error` = the exception class name; the attempt counts), `section_outline_empty`, `section_under_unsupported`, `section_under_empty` (detail `under`; does not count and does not replace the previous listing), `section_read_cap`, `section_read_failed` (detail `error` = the exception class name; the attempt counts), `section_read_repeat`, `section_not_surfaced`, `section_ambiguous`, and `section_source_unresolved` (shared by both actions). A repeated browse has no skip code: it is a `browse_sections` step with `detail.repeat: true`. Choosing a spent or zero-cap action goes through the generic `action_not_offered` skip. The two failure skips carry no `result_ids`. Both words are appended to the retrieval-experience action vocabulary (see the Agentic Memory table below) and to the first-round offered-action filter, so an experience entry recommending one of them is shown only when the run offers it.

**Rails.** The exact numbers live here only; deployment-side meaning is in the `REASONING_*` entries of `docs/deployment-and-configuration.md`.

| Rail | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Master switch (`REASONING_SECTION_NAV_ENABLED`) | on |
| `browse_sections` calls per run (`REASONING_MAX_SECTION_BROWSES`) | 3 (`0`–`50`) |
| `read_section` calls per run (`REASONING_MAX_SECTION_READS`) | 3 (`0`–`50`) |
| Chunks one `read_section` reads back (`REASONING_SECTION_READ_MAX_CHUNKS`) | 12 (`1`–`200`) |
| Reserved synthesis seats for section-read passages (`REASONING_SECTION_READ_RESERVE`) | 6 (`0`–`100`; `0` reserves none) |
| Characters of one rendered listing (`REASONING_SECTION_BROWSE_MAX_CHARS`) | 3,000 (`200`–`20000`; the floor equals the renderer's minimum so the truncation note itself is never cut) |
| Entries in the section-hint block (`REASONING_SECTION_HINT_MAX_ENTRIES`) | 8 (`0`–`50`; `0` shows no block) |
| Sources the hint block covers (`REASONING_SECTION_HINT_SOURCES`) | 4 (`0`–`20`; `0` shows no block) |
| Hint relative threshold (`REASONING_SECTION_HINT_RELATIVE_FLOOR`) | 0.5 (`0`–`1`; a share of the highest chunk cosine the run already holds) |
| Chunks scanned for one source's outline, and the vectors read for it (`REASONING_SECTION_OUTLINE_MAX_ROWS`) | 4,000 (`0`–`20000`; `0` withdraws navigation altogether) |
| `browse_sections.query` characters used for ranking (`SECTION_QUERY_MAX_CHARS`) | 300 |
| Per-item characters echoed into summaries/ledger/trace for section-navigation source titles, section labels and `under` (`_SECTION_ECHO_CHARS`, cut with 「…」; the ambiguous-candidate list is further bounded by `REASONING_SECTION_BROWSE_MAX_CHARS`, issues addresses only for listed candidates and states how many were omitted) | 200 |
| Process-wide cache for decoded section vectors across runs (`REASONING_SECTION_VECTOR_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`) | 256 MiB (`0`–`16 GiB`; `0` disables it; LRU, about 16 default-sized sources) |
| Run-wide cache for decoded section vectors (`SECTION_VECTOR_RUN_MEMO_MAX_BYTES`) | 128 MiB (past it vectors are computed again instead of kept; one source takes about rows × runtime dimension × 4 bytes, 16 MB at 4,000 rows and 1,024 dimensions) |

A deployment plugin whose reflect action is named `browse_sections` or `read_section` is refused at startup: both are core action ids and reserved names (see the registration rails of [Reflect plugin actions](#reflect-plugin-actions-askreflect_action)).

### Paper search, paper cards and per-paper extraction (`find_sources` / `get_paper_cards` / `extract_from_sources`)

**What it is for.** "List every paper in this notebook about X, with its key figures and innovations" cannot be answered by ranking passages: the roster shows at most 20 titles per turn and passage search returns a fixed number of passages. Three reflect actions (reasoning Ask only; chunk mode is unchanged) and one answer layout cover it. Each action has its own deployment gate (`REASONING_FIND_SOURCES_ENABLED`, `REASONING_PAPER_CARDS_ENABLED`, `REASONING_EXTRACT_ENABLED`); a closed gate removes the prompt line, schema branch and allow-list entry together, and the `answer_layout` field exists only while the cards or the extraction gate is open. A deployment plugin may not reuse these action ids or `answer_layout` (see the registration rails of [Reflect plugin actions](#reflect-plugin-actions-askreflect_action)).

**`find_sources`: find the documents about a topic.** Parameters: `query` (a natural-language description, for the semantic leg), `terms` (up to 6 literal words, aliases or acronyms, each up to 64 characters, most literal first; the reflect executor cuts the rest and says so in the ledger), `year_from` / `year_to`, `venue`, `author` (substring filters), `kind` (`papers`, the default, or `all`; `papers` also keeps eligible documents whose paper metadata has not been extracted yet, reported as `meta_pending`), `scope` (`all` or `current_notebook`, as for the enumeration actions) and `cursor`. At least one of `query`, `terms` or a filter is required. The source set is exactly the run's frozen source ceiling and participating libraries (the same set the enumeration actions use); the visibility predicate is the Sources panel's, so another member's Memory projections never appear. Two legs run: a metadata leg (case-insensitive substring over titles, file names, summaries, paper titles, venues, keywords and authors, with `%` and `_` escaped; each hit records which fields matched and whether the match is on a word boundary) and a semantic leg (up to `FIND_SOURCES_CHUNK_RECALL` passages per library, grouped by document, keeping each document's best fused relevance and passage count). Each document lands in a tier: `strong` (a word-boundary hit in the title, paper title or keywords, or best relevance at or above `FIND_SOURCES_STRONG_RELEVANCE`), `related` (other field hits, non-word-boundary hits, or best relevance at or above `FIND_SOURCES_RELATED_RELEVANCE`) or dropped. On the FTS-degraded lane, or when the passages carried no vector similarity, the relevance lines do not apply and a passage-only document needs at least two passages to be `related`. Ranking is deterministic (tier, number of matched fields, best relevance, passage count, publication year descending, source id); a pure filter query makes everything `strong`, newest first. A page holds 20 documents; every page turn counts as one `find_sources` call of the run. Each item carries a run-local handle `p1...`, the source id, title, year, venue, up to 3 authors, the tier, the matched `reasons`, the best passage (up to 240 characters) and the card status. The response also carries `counts` (strong, related, scope total, and the papers whose metadata is still missing) and a `coverage` block: `lexical_complete` is false when a year/venue/author filter excluded papers whose metadata is not extracted yet, when `terms` could only be checked against titles and summaries for such papers, or when a participating library was skipped (named in `skipped_libraries`); `semantic_recall_capped` is true when the last recalled passage was still above the related line. **When either flag says the search may be incomplete the answer must say so and must not claim a full list.** A cursor carries the parameter fingerprint and a digest of the scope's paper metadata: if metadata was extracted between two pages the old cursor is refused ("restart from the first page") because the order may have changed; handles already issued stay valid. Non-current libraries follow the federation rule of reading only warm indexes (no cold load, no whole-table scan), and the tier lines are calibrated for the deployed embedding model (see `docs/deployment-and-configuration.md`).

**Paper cards (`get_paper_cards`).** A card is a per-paper structured summary: `tldr`, `problem`, `method`, up to 5 contributions, up to 12 metrics (name, value, unit, setting, `compared_to`) and up to 8 datasets, every field citing source elements. Only sources whose paper metadata says they are papers get a card; other documents are answered by `extract_from_sources`. Cards are **lazy**: nothing is generated at import time and there is no backfill; a card is built the first time a caller asks and cached in `source_paper_cards`. The model reads a deterministic sample of at most `PAPER_CARD_INPUT_CHARS` of the document (opening first, then up to 6 tables, then evenly spread elements including the last). **Grounding is code, not trust:** every cited element id must have been in the sample; a text field left without a valid citation is dropped; a metric survives only when its value, normalized (full-width to half-width, thousands separators and trailing zeros removed, whole tokens only, sign and `+/-`/exponent forms kept together), appears in the text of the element it cites, and a bare single-digit integer is never treated as grounded. Values are cut number-safely, so a cut never leaves half a number. Dropped items and their reasons go to an audit envelope. **Validity is decided at read time:** a cached card counts only while its content basis (the source's element generation), its card version and the paper classification still match, so re-parsing, reclassifying or a prompt upgrade invalidates cards without cleanup code and the next request regenerates them; reclassifying a source as a non-paper deletes its card. **Failure cooldown:** a content failure (malformed reply, a card empty after verification, a failed metadata extraction) or a failure deterministic for that document is cooled down for `PAPER_CARD_RETRY_SECONDS` (after 3 consecutive failures, 24 hours); authentication or configuration errors write nothing, and transient errors (full or timed-out queue, open breaker, 429, 5xx, timeout) return `deferred` without counting as a failure. Per request, metadata extraction and card generation together spend at most the run's generation budget of model calls; the rest come back `deferred` and the answer names how many were not expanded. Per-status results: `ready`, `generated`, `not_paper`, `meta_pending` (metadata not extracted, or the notebook is a read-only mirror and cannot be written), `failed`, `deferred`, `not_found`. A reader may populate the cache for a mounted or referenced library they can read; the cache holds nothing about the asker. It is not synced between environments and is not exported or copied with a notebook (it is simply regenerated on use). `PAPER_CARD_ENABLED=false` stops generating new cards and still serves valid cached ones; it does not affect extraction.

**`extract_from_sources`: ad-hoc fields.** Parameters `sources` (handles or source ids) and `fields` (up to 4, each up to 80 characters, e.g. "mAP on COCO"). It works on any document, papers or not, and caches nothing. Per source it picks, for each field separately, the 4 passages most similar to the field (up to 12 after de-duplication, falling back to full-text search when the document has no vectors; the outline scan covers at most 4,000 rows and says so when cut), adds the opening elements, and makes one `paper_metadata` model call. A value containing numbers is kept only when each number group appears in the text of the cited element (a lone single-digit integer as the whole value is rejected); every kept value carries its own citation. Results per source: `extracted`, `no_text`, `deferred`, `failed`, `not_found`; per field either the value or why it is missing.

**Citations.** Card and extraction citations live in their own evidence key band `k9001`-`k9999` (at most 40 cards x 24 elements), above `read_document`'s band. All cited elements are registered for citation without consuming the prompt budget; the model sees one compact digest per paper (title, year/venue, TL;DR, the first 2 contributions, the first 3 metrics, each with its keys) and, when `find_sources` ran, a findings block (the coverage line plus the documents without a card row). A cited element whose source was deleted or re-parsed after the card was cached is not registered, and the claim built on it is not written.

**The deterministic table (`answer_layout`).** Any reflect turn may set the optional top-level field `answer_layout` to `prose` (default) or `paper_table`; the last value written wins, and `paper_table` is accepted only when the run really holds cards or extracted values (otherwise it falls back to `prose` with a ledger note). With `paper_table` the system, not the model, builds the final text after the model's body is written: a one-line **coverage statement** ("found N related papers (a strong, b related), M of them expanded" plus a "there may be more" clause when `semantic_recall_capped`, metadata is missing or a library was skipped; with several different `find_sources` requests whose overlap is unknown it says "at least N"), then the model's overview and cross-paper comparison (told not to repeat the table), then a **table** (paper, year / venue, main metrics, key innovations, and one "extra fields" column for extracted values; every cell carries its `[kN]`; at most 3 metrics and 2 innovations per cell, 240 characters per cell, pipes and newlines escaped), and finally an **unexpanded list** of the remaining related papers (titles only, up to 100). Rows are capped by the effort tier; the table shows the first 4 extracted fields and names the rest in the coverage line. Only keys registered for citation are rendered, and a paper none of whose claims survive is left out and counted in the coverage line. The coverage statement doubles as the answer's completeness statement only when it is rendered with the table; in a `prose` answer the generic "not verified as complete" notice is still appended. A source reached without a `find_sources` hit is shown with its stored title, never its raw id. In sectioned synthesis the digests and the table appear once, in the first section.

**Rails (effort tier, `AskRetrievalLimits`).** Per run:

| Tier | `find_sources` calls (pages included) | Card reads | Card generations (metadata + card) | Extraction papers | Inline table rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| overview | 1 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 6 |
| standard | 2 | 12 | 6 | 6 | 12 |
| deep | 3 | 20 | 10 | 8 | 20 |
| thorough | 3 | 30 | 16 | 12 | 30 |
| exhaustive | 4 | 40 | 24 | 16 | 40 |

One `get_paper_cards` call reads at most 10 papers and one `extract_from_sources` call at most 8. Generation runs in a bounded pool (`PAPER_CARD_MAX_WORKERS`, further capped by the `paper_metadata` service's concurrency) under the caller's interactive priority, honours cancellation, and a duplicate request for the same source waits for the first. The paper-card digest takes part of the structured-side prompt budget (order: Knowhow, enumeration preview, cards, document reads). If `REASONING_MAX_DOCUMENT_READS x DOCUMENT_OVERVIEW_MAX_ELEMENTS` exceeds 2,000 the `read_document` action is withdrawn and startup logs a warning. The trace, experience and profile vocabularies gain `find_documents`, `paper_cards` and `extract_fields` steps.

**MCP tools.** `find_sources`, `get_paper_cards` and `extract_from_sources` are `read`-tier tools (24 tools in all). **The latter two spend model quota on a `read` token** (a deliberate product decision); every call re-reads the token, the allowlist and the owner's access, and passes an explicit source set (since MCP has no run scope): every visible source, plus the owner's hidden sources **only when the token has `memory:read`** (the same switch as `search`); without it only Knowhow projections are added, so a read-only token cannot read the owner's private Memory through a best passage or an extraction, and another member's Memory never reaches a result. Extraction over MCP is governed by the `read` tier alone (`REASONING_EXTRACT_ENABLED` gates only the reasoning action); `PAPER_CARD_ENABLED` applies to both paths.

- `find_sources(notebook_id?, query?, terms?, year_from?, year_to?, venue?, author?, kind="papers", cursor?, limit=20)`: the parameters above except `scope`; paging is by `cursor` and `limit` (1-20), never by a raw offset (an offset would bypass the stale-cursor check). Returns the items, `counts`, `coverage` (`lexical_complete`, `semantic_recall_capped`, `skipped_libraries` and `lanes`, the retrieval lane each library used), a top-level `next_cursor` and a top-level `refs` table. A stale cursor is refused with a readable sentence ("restart from page 1"): either paper metadata changed between pages, or the notebook's sources were added or removed (each named separately); changing any other argument together with a cursor is refused as an invalid cursor. Page through all results first and only then call `get_paper_cards` / `extract_from_sources`, because generating a card can extract paper metadata and make an open cursor stale.
- `get_paper_cards(source_ids, notebook_id?)`: at most 3 sources per call and at most 3 model calls per call (metadata and card together); the rest return `deferred`, so call again for them. Each source returns its status and card. Each requested id is checked individually against the notebook (a source outside it, or another member's Memory, returns `not_found`), and both this tool and `extract_from_sources` re-check the token and the notebook's read access after the model work and before returning, like `ask`: a token revoked mid-call gets `token_inactive` and no payload.
- `extract_from_sources(source_ids, fields, notebook_id?)`: at most 3 sources and 4 fields.
- Responses stay within the shared 12,000-byte rail. Every cited element is listed once in the top-level `refs` list (resolvable by `read_reference`) and fields carry an index into it: `refs` for `tldr` / `problem` / `method`, `ref` for each list entry (contribution, metric, dataset, with its first anchor, because nesting depth is limited) and extracted value; a passage's `ref` is the ref of the chunk's first element. When a response is over budget it degrades by `detail` level (fewer anchors, shorter text, fewer entries, finally fewer items) and never clips a number in the middle; whatever was cut is reported in `truncation`; if trailing `find_sources` items are cut, `next_cursor` resumes at the first item not delivered.
- Each token owner may have at most 2 `get_paper_cards` / `extract_from_sources` calls running at once, across all their tokens and per process; beyond that the call fails with `busy`. `find_sources` makes no model call and does not count toward this limit. Limits at a glance: at most 3 sources per `get_paper_cards` / `extract_from_sources` call, at most 3 model calls per `get_paper_cards` call (the other sources return `deferred`), at most 4 fields, `find_sources` `limit` 1-20. Calls run with progress notifications and a stop event: a client cancel stops the work and unfinished sources return nothing.
- `list_sources` rows gain `authors` (up to 3 names), `pub_year` and `venue`.
- The server `instructions` describe the workflow: `find_sources` first, `get_paper_cards` in batches of 3, `extract_from_sources` for fields the cards lack, `read_reference` to verify key numbers, and never claim a complete list when `coverage` says otherwise.

### Notebook understanding blocks

The agent keeps a small, low-cost, LLM-consolidated summary of what it has learned about a notebook — "AI 对这个库的理解" ("what the AI understands about this library") — surfaced through five fixed label blocks and injected as prompt scaffolding into reasoning Ask's plan and reflect context (and, identically, into each section's deep-dive during Deep Report generation). It is never evidence: `ReasoningResult` gains no field for it, so it can never enter answer synthesis, be cited with `[k]`, or appear in a deep report's body.

**The five blocks and two ownership layers.** Three blocks form a notebook-wide **shared base layer** that every member reads: `corpus_shape` (what kind of material this library broadly holds), `key_entities` (names/topics that recur often enough to be worth knowing up front), and `corpus_gaps` (gaps the agent has already noticed — no tables/formulas/images/code blocks, or parse-quality warnings; parse failures and not-yet-parsed documents — the latter including in-flight queued/parsing ones — feed two separate counts — worth avoiding when phrasing a question). Two blocks form a **personal overlay** private to each member: `retrieval_notes` (that member's own accumulated phrasing/query experience, visible and effective only for their own questions) and `usage_gaps` (directions that member has asked about but the library did not answer, tracked as a zero-hit-query count rather than as source ids). The base layer is refreshed by a per-notebook consolidation job triggered by accumulated source changes; each overlay is refreshed by a per-`(notebook, user)` job triggered by that member's own completed Ask jobs or deep reports (a completed report reaches the threshold immediately, registered as a deliberately simpler trigger than counting reports toward the same accumulator as questions). A report is now **both a trigger and an input** (Agentic Memory P2): the refresh it schedules reads that member's recent Ask traces **and** their own recently completed (`status='done'`) deep reports, projected from each report's persisted `sections_json[i].attempted` account — per confirmed retrieval direction, that direction's own wording plus whether executing it errored, and nothing else. Never section markdown, citations, step type, duration or step sequence (that shape was never persisted, so it cannot be recovered). A member whose only activity is one completed report therefore no longer gets `no_usage_sample`; the report sample alone is enough.

**The report sample feeds `retrieval_notes` only, and contributes nothing to `usage_gaps`.** This is a decision, not an omission. The `attempted` account's one counter, `new`, looks like a hit count but is not: it counts knowledge objects newly added to the *run's shared candidate pool*, so it reads 0 whenever a direction returns material an earlier direction already collected (which a report's same-section directions do by design, since the section question seeds the pool before they run), reads 0 for every direction in a notebook with no knowledge graph, and never counts chunk or element hits at all. Reading `new == 0` as "this direction came back empty" would write "this library has nothing on X" into a member's private notes on the strength of a counter measuring something else, so zero-hit evidence (the `usage_gaps` count and the empty-search samples) stays **Ask-only**, exactly as before P2. What the report sample contributes is *wording* — how this member phrases research directions — which is what `retrieval_notes` is about. For the same reason the rendered report section never asserts a direction count: the attempt-row cap below is indistinguishable from "this report ran no directions" once the rows are gone, so a report whose directions were all truncated away discloses that they were not sampled rather than claiming a number.

The report sample's ownership predicate is `reports.created_by`, which is the report's *original* creator rather than necessarily the member who triggered this particular run — in a shared notebook, any writable member can (re)trigger generation of a report someone else created, so that trigger's own overlay refresh can legitimately come back empty (a normal `no_usage_sample` outcome, not an error) rather than summarise a report they did not create. This asymmetry is registered and deliberately the safe direction: only the member's own rows ever enter their own sample.

**Isolation is structural, not a filter.** The base chain's consolidation input is restricted, by construction, to corpus statistics and KG-object aggregates — its SQL literally cannot reference any usage/query/answer table (`ask_jobs`, `ask_trace_steps`, `answers`, `memory_items`, `conversations`, `reports`), enforced by a semantic allowlist guard (every function in the consolidation module must be classified, each class may only call the port methods on its own allowlist, and trace-read SQL must carry the ownership predicate) rather than a runtime check. The overlay chain's consolidation input is that one member's own retrieval trace **and, since Agentic Memory P2 (T4), that member's own completed deep reports** — never anyone else's — with the ownership predicate (`created_by`/`user_id`) written into the SQL that reads either one rather than filtered afterward in application code — the same shape as the `memory_items.created_by` boundary elsewhere in this document. A member who loses read access to the notebook loses their overlay the same way every other per-member read does (participant-set re-evaluation), and it is physically cleared when that member is removed from the notebook — job/status row first, block rows second, because the in-flight consolidation worker's revocation guards key off that row: deleting blocks first left a window where a still-running worker recreated them and settled green before the marker vanished. **A completion notification that arrives after that removal (P1's registered R4/R5 residuals, closed):** `note_ask_completed`/`note_report_completed`/`start_overlay` (the manual-rebuild entry point) each re-check the same live participant-set predicate immediately before bumping the signal counter or claiming the chain, rather than after — bumping first would recreate exactly the job row the check exists to keep from being recreated. The check fails open (an exception is treated as permission granted, matching every other fail-open rule in this feature), so the residual is narrowed from "always resurrects" to "only resurrects if that one bounded read itself fails"; the job/status-row-generation guard above (`claim_token`, Agentic Memory P2/T2) closes the companion race where the row was already recreated through some other path — a stale worker's `settle()` can no longer silently overwrite a newer claim's blocks, because `settle()` now distinguishes "the row is gone" (member really was removed — wipe) from "the row belongs to a later claim" (never wipe). The two base-chain aggregates that can see private Memory (KG-object type counts, recurring concept names) exclude the Memory synthetic sources *inside their own statements* rather than reading a Memory source-id roster first and then subtracting it / passing it back in as an exclusion list: those reads share no snapshot, so a Memory created or deleted between them makes the subtraction miss and the exclusion list drop a row — and what the second one drops is a **concept name**, written into a block every member reads.

**Blocks can be withdrawn — but never a user-written one.** "Omission keeps the previous value" is deliberate (a model with nothing to say must not clear existing content), but with only that rule a stale claim whose evidence has since been deleted or reparsed away stays in the block forever and rides in every planning prompt. The consolidation reply therefore carries an explicit retirement marker: the model may name a block to withdraw, and the server blanks its value while keeping the row and its change history, recording the origin as the job rather than as a person. Refusal stops at **user-authored** blocks and covers the ordinary update too, not just retirement: a job rewrite of a person's block would flip its provenance to `job` and open their words to retirement on the very next run, so while a user-authored block still has text the server refuses **any** job write to it — update or retire alike — records the refusal, and leaves the rest of the same reply untouched. A person hands a block back to the agent by clearing it: a cleared block keeps `updated_origin='user'` but an empty user block is deliberately not authoritative (otherwise clearing would freeze the label forever instead of meaning "let the agent fill this in again"). Retiring a block that is already empty (or was never written) is not a write.

**The retirement trigger is a rendered evidence-liveness reconciliation, not a guess.** Each refresh renders, beside every base-layer job-written block that carries evidence, a bracketed note reconciling that block's stored evidence ids against this same read's aggregates: ids still in the sampled statistics are named (`supported by: s1, s2`), ids that are still in the library but merely fell outside the sampled top-40 (or are healthy prose with nothing to list) are counted separately (`+N more still in the library`) and never reported as gone, ids no longer in the library at all are counted (`M no longer in the library`), and a block whose evidence has vanished entirely gets the unambiguous `[all supporting documents are gone]` marker instead of a count. Liveness is judged against the **full** user-visible document set from this same read, never the sampled statistics list — the two are deliberately different sets, and judging by the sample alone would report a perfectly healthy document as gone. The prompt is told this note is for reconciliation only: an id spelled out in it must never be copied into a *new* claim's evidence, which may only be drawn from the document ids in the statistics section. User-authored blocks never render this note (they carry no evidence, and can never be retired regardless).

**Evidence is clickable in the UI.** Each job-written block shows what it rests on beneath its text: the three base blocks list the documents behind the claim as clickable chips that open that document's detail (the same open path Ask citation cards use), while `usage_gaps` shows the server's own count — "N searches that came back empty" — as inert text, because its evidence is retrieval behaviour rather than a document. User-written blocks carry no evidence row.

**Values, numeric limits.**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Blocks | 5 (`corpus_shape`, `key_entities`, `corpus_gaps` in the base layer; `retrieval_notes`, `usage_gaps` per-member overlay) |
| Characters per block value | 400 |
| Characters per rendered block (all blocks concatenated) | 1,200 |
| Change-history ring buffer per block | 20 entries |
| Base-chain trigger | 5 accumulated source changes |
| Overlay-chain trigger | 10 completed Ask jobs for that member (a global Ask counts once per library it actually retrieved from or cited), or 1 completed deep report (direct threshold) |
| Overlay trace sample read per consolidation | last 40 asks |
| Overlay trace step rows read per consolidation | ≤600 (a separate cap from the 40-ask sample — 40 asks × however many steps each is not itself a bound; when this cap binds, the oldest asks' steps are dropped first) |
| Overlay report sample read per consolidation | last 10 completed (`status='done'`) reports (Agentic Memory P2, T4) |
| Overlay report attempt rows read per consolidation | ≤200 (a separate cap from the 10-report sample, same reason as the trace-step cap above; when it binds, the oldest report's tail directions are dropped first). A report left with zero direction rows is rendered as "directions not sampled" — the cap and "this report ran none" are indistinguishable by then, and with these defaults a full sample overruns the cap routinely |
| Report direction wording clip | 120 characters (the same per-item clip the ask question and step summary use) |
| Consolidation output budget | 2,048 tokens |
| Corpus-stats documents sampled | 40 |
| Evidence ids retained per claim (base chain) | 8 (also the cap on how many are individually named in the evidence-liveness note) |
| Top concept names surfaced to the base prompt | 24, ≤48 characters each, ≤600 characters total |
| Overlay prompt's usage section | ≤3,000 characters shared by BOTH lists (ask questions and report directions), plus ≤12 zero-hit-query samples at ≤120 characters each, plus fixed headers. One budget, allocated rather than first-come-first-served: while there are reports to render the ask list may spend at most half of it and whatever it leaves unspent rolls over to the report section, so neither can starve the other. A member with no reports is unaffected by the split and renders exactly as before this section existed |
| Observation ring per `(notebook, owner)` (Agentic Memory P3) | 200 rows — `append_observation` evicts the oldest beyond this bound in the same write transaction as the insert |
| Characters per observation | 500 (`add_observation`'s `text`) |
| Observation sample read per consolidation | ≤20 most recent, on its own separate query from the ask/report sample above |
| Rendered observation section budget | ≤600 characters — its OWN budget, never a slice of the 3,000-character usage-section budget above |
| Call-ledger ring per `(notebook, owner)` | 200 rows, held **separately** from the observation ring above — each kind evicts only within itself, so neither can crowd the other out |
| Call-ledger read width | ≤20 most recent by default (`call_limit`, capped at the 200-row ring), on its own query and its own response list |

**Injection surface.** A run that has `AGENT_PROFILE_ENABLED` on (and a bound profile store) injects the base layer plus the current user's own overlay into both the planning prompt and the reflect loop's context, ahead of the collection map section in each. A notebook the agent has not yet consolidated anything for injects nothing and records no trace step — this is a deliberately different rule from Memory's zero-hit `skip` step, because a Memory miss carries the cost of an embedding round trip and a vector scan worth disclosing, while a profile read is a sub-millisecond bounded primary-key lookup whose absence is pure noise on every single run of a fresh notebook. The block is injected even when the request has genuinely narrowed its source scope, and so is the collection map, whose counts then follow the source ceiling: the profile block opens no channel, is not evidence, and cannot be `[k]`-cited, so a narrowed run still benefits from knowing what the agent has learned about phrasing and known gaps. It is not injected in a global question, which has no subject library whose profile would apply. On Deep Report's side, the block reaches only each section's per-section deep-dive retrieval (`_deep_dive`), which always seeds its run with `intent_queries` rather than calling the planning model — so in practice the profile only ever reaches the reflect loop on the report path, never a report's own planning call.

**Endpoints and role matrix.**

| Endpoint | Who |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /notebooks/{id}/understanding` | Any reader; returns `enabled`, `base` (blocks with value/evidence/revision/`updated_at`/`updated_origin` — the change-history ring buffer itself is not exposed in v1, only current values), `mine` (the caller's own overlay, same shape), `job` (`{base, mine}`, each with status/pending/`updated_at`/failure_reason, `None` before a chain's first claim), and `can_edit_base` |
