The report pauses at `intent_ready` for its **creator's** confirmation, unless the create request has `auto_generate=true` and the question is clear (no blocking ambiguity), in which case the server auto-confirms through the same deterministic freeze the manual endpoint uses (no second LLM call) and proceeds directly into planning; a question with blocking ambiguities always pauses regardless of `auto_generate`, and required ambiguities must be answered before either a human or the server can confirm. A report carrying a source/reference-library scope also reruns the manual endpoint's scope revalidation before auto-confirming; when that recheck fails (sources deleted or libraries unmounted while intent understanding ran) the report stays at the confirmation gate and the skip event carries reason `scope_invalid`; when it passes, the refreshed freeze is adopted for the claimed understanding and the later planning/generation scope context, exactly as manual confirmation would persist it. Confirmation belongs to whoever created the report, not to the notebook owner: a member who created a report in a shared notebook confirms it themselves, and nobody — the owner included — can confirm or advance somebody else's report (row-level `created_by` isolation; see 群组知识共享). "Can only wait" is therefore true only of *other people's* reports. A failure or race while auto-advancing fails open — the report is left at its prior status with the manual confirmation gate still usable — and emits only the body-free `report_intent_auto_confirm_skipped` event. Confirmation (manual or auto) atomically claims `intent_ready → planning` and deterministically freezes the contract already shown to the user; it does not run a hidden second interpretation pass. Clarification answers enrich the internal retrieval/drafting question but never the visible report heading. **Phase 1b begins only after intent confirmation**: the confirmed wording and answers become authoritative, a bounded zero-LLM probe measures both federated KG and direct parsed-`SourceElement` coverage for every mandatory topic, and only then does the STORM-style planner use source titles, KG hits, and chunk provenance to refine vocabulary, ordering, perspectives, and tensions. Corpus availability may expose a gap but cannot replace or narrow a required topic; code validates the mapping and restores any omitted mandatory topic. The outline editor shows each section's mandatory question, editable retrieval directions, and raw-element/KG/base coverage before confirmation; the last section binding a mandatory topic cannot be deleted, and the API enforces the same invariant. **Phase 2 (minutes, on outline confirm)** runs every approved retrieval direction as well as the full `reasoning` deep-dive, in parallel by section. Chunks, KG objects, typed relation hops, confirmed Memory, and direct `SourceElement` hits share the same `[k]` binding path. `SourceElement` is a first-class citation rather than uncitable prompt decoration: small libraries may score element rows directly, while non-copyable large libraries derive a bounded candidate set from chunk ANN/FTS hits and hydrate only those chunks' exact `element_ids`, never the full element table. Report references deduplicate by exact evidence anchor rather than source title, and selecting a report citation reveals its bound source/location excerpt. Ask and report citations prefer `source_paper_meta.paper_title` only for a grounded paper row (`is_paper=true`) with a nonblank parsed title; all other sources keep their ordinary source title/file name. Citation responses also carry the persisted upload name as `source_file_name`; Ask/report citation cards show it as `原始文件` when it differs from the display title, including mounted public-reference-library evidence. That value comes only from `sources.file_name`, never a MinerU temporary/output Markdown name. The model's `grounded` boolean is advisory: the backend reparses emitted anchors and requires cited evidence to meet the configured relevance threshold. A read-only final editor creates the executive summary and flags incomplete mandatory intent or cross-section contradictions without rewriting sections or adding facts. The existing `（推断）`/`【通识】` discipline, five depth levels, live `section_status`, cancellation, `.md`, and `reports.zip` export remain unchanged. `ReportSummary` and `ReportDetail` expose `updated_at` plus `generation_started_at`, the latter stored atomically inside report state at the successful `outline_ready → generating` claim. Completed-report list and detail metadata use `updated_at` as the exact browser-local generation time, retain the relative age, and show the wall-clock duration from `generation_started_at` through that final write. Intent and outline confirmation waits are excluded; legacy completed reports without a generation-start stamp show no invented duration. Non-completed reports display creation time only and never claim a final duration.

- **Deep-report capacity, output, and retry rails:** whole-report generation is admitted through `REPORT_GENERATION_CONCURRENCY` (default 1 per backend process). One admitted report runs at most `REPORT_SECTION_CONCURRENCY` sections concurrently (default 5), also capped by the bound model service and by `POSTGRES_POOL_MAX_SIZE - 2`. That last cap bounds section-level fan-out only — each section's own sub-query fan-out can briefly borrow further pool connections, with waiters bounded by the pool acquire timeout — so it limits pool pressure rather than reserving fixed slots for online work; a queued report holds no database connection. Section drafting uses `REPORT_SECTION_MAX_TOKENS=65536`; the detailed-tier report-wide blueprint and final read-only editor each use an independent `102400` completion ceiling through `REPORT_SYNTHESIS_MAX_TOKENS` and `REPORT_SUMMARY_MAX_TOKENS`. These settings are completion ceilings, not application-side total-context declarations or reserved output; the bound provider/model must accept each ceiling together with that workload's prompt. The blueprint prompt selects only load-bearing claims, at most 12 per section and 60 report-wide. A claim's facet tag accepts an `id:value` composite and is deterministically narrowed to the legal prefix; a tag written as a facet's name, one of its declared values, or a case variant of the facet's id, name, or value is deterministically repaired to the owning facet id when the spelling is unambiguous (declared ids win over other facets' names and values; a spelling that two facets share is never guessed). An unrepairable tag is cleared on that claim alone — the tag is organizational, so no facet tag ever discards the blueprint, while evidence bindings, section ownership, and structure remain atomically validated; repair/clear counts surface as the counts-only `report_synthesis_facet_tags` event (two counters plus opaque report identity, never a facet spelling), and the synthesis prompt enumerates the frame's legal facet ids verbatim. Synthesis-failure disclosure semantics are unchanged. A run with zero non-failed, non-empty section bodies terminates as `failed`; a partial run with at least one valid body remains fail-open and discloses failed sections. A section is drafted at most twice, and its failure note names what the last attempt actually hit, without guessing a cause: an empty reply or one carrying none of the section fields keeps the historical "答案合成未产出内容(模型可能把输出预算耗在思维链上),已重试"; a reply the JSON boundary could not parse reads "模型返回的本节内容无法解析,已重试"; a failed model call reads "本节模型调用失败,已重试"; a section whose retrieval or drafting itself raised reads "本节处理过程出错", the raw exception text staying in that section's author-only `sections[].error` and the failed stage on the content-free `report_stage_timing` event (`stage` = `retrieve`/`draft`, `failed: true`). Each attempt's content-free `report_section_attempt` event carries `status` (`success`/`empty`/`malformed`/`error`/`cancelled`) and, on failure, a closed-vocabulary `reason` (the JSON-boundary rejection reason such as `invalid_json`, or the stable model error code). Failed generation that retains a confirmed outline can atomically re-enter `generating`: retry keeps the frozen intent/outline, resets `generation_started_at`, clears stale generated artifacts, and never reruns intent understanding or planning. Queue time after that claim is included in generation duration.

- **Retrieval-run, sufficiency, and reasoning-action rails:** one report planning/generation run shares `REPORT_RETRIEVAL_FANOUT=8` leaf KG/chunk/element/PPR slots across all section workers; independent planning KG/raw-element probes use `REPORT_PROBE_CHANNEL_CONCURRENCY=2` (validated `1..2`). Waiting for a report leaf slot observes cancellation at bounded intervals and rechecks it after acquisition before starting I/O; a leaf already inside a backend/database call finishes safely instead of being detached. Ask uses the same request-local successful query-embedding single-flight without changing its historical fan-out. A report's raw-passage evidence travels the same participant-set channel as Ask (the active notebook plus the reference libraries the report's frozen scope keeps), so `CHUNK_FEDERATION_ENABLED` is its rollback switch too; each library's recall leg acquires one `REPORT_RETRIEVAL_FANOUT` slot of its own, so mounting reference libraries widens a report's evidence without widening its database fan-out. Report sufficiency requires at least `REPORT_SUFFICIENCY_MIN_RELEVANT_ITEMS=3` relevant evidence units and `REPORT_SUFFICIENCY_MIN_FAMILIES=2` distinguishable families (`REPORT_SUFFICIENCY_COMPLETE_MIN_FAMILIES=3` for complete scope), with `REPORT_SUFFICIENCY_MAX_TOP_FAMILY_SHARE=0.8`. The reasoning run admits at most `REASONING_MAX_PPR_RETRIEVES=3`, `REASONING_MAX_EXACT_LOOKUPS=3`, `REASONING_MAX_FOLLOW_CHAIN_ACTIONS=3`, a cross-library community-peer cap of `REASONING_COMMUNITY_PEERS_CAP_FACTOR=2 × COMMUNITY_PEERS_TOPK`, and `REASONING_MAX_OUTLINE_UPDATES=6`. These defaults exactly preserve the former inline rules; deployments should change them only against a frozen evaluation set. Planning sub-stages, retrieve/synthesis/draft/final-editor stages, outer section attempts, and retrieval-run cache/fan-out counters emit fail-open, content-free events containing only stage/run kind, opaque report/run ids, indices, counts, statuses, and milliseconds.

- **Deep Report retrieval latency rails:** within each coverage/sufficiency stage, every logical topic/section keeps its own ordered first-N query window, then identical queries are retrieved once and their KG/element leaf pairs use the shared `REPORT_RETRIEVAL_FANOUT` budget; aggregation remains in logical input order. On PostgreSQL, every generic chunk lexical call gets a private savepoint-scoped `POSTGRES_CHUNK_FTS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` deadline (default `3.0`, `0 < value <= min(10, POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)`). The first such timeout opens a notebook-local circuit for the rest of that retrieval run, so later calls return no lexical supplement without another database statement; already-running concurrent calls are allowed to settle. This fail-open circuit never covers exact phrase/identifier lookup. Chunk ANN retrieval whose source sidecar covers the frozen report scope is ANN-only by default, while ordinary Ask keeps ANN∪FTS. A pending-fold source with chunks restores bounded FTS only for uncovered authorized sources; an empty source does not. A report call without a producer scope resolves and freezes that library's authorized source universe once per library/run before every ANN or fallback producer, and an index reload cannot widen it. `CHUNK_FTS_WITH_ANN_ENABLED=true` is the report-quality rollback.

- **Bounded neighbour expansion and background job concurrency pools:** one reasoning `expand_graph` action expands at most `REASONING_NEIGHBOR_EXPAND_LIMIT=1000` **distinct qualifying neighbours per direction** (outgoing and incoming are budgeted separately), so hydration of the neighbouring knowledge objects stays bounded even on a pathological hub node. The budget counts neighbours, not relation rows: one neighbour often carries several duplicate or corroborating relations, and some rows are dropped as non-queryable edge pairs, so the database read is bounded at four times the neighbour budget (a deliberate over-scan that absorbs those rows instead of letting them consume the budget and silently skip later, legitimate neighbours). Object-status eligibility is applied in SQL **before** the read bound (on the neighbour side of the join only), so relations pointing at deprecated objects cannot consume the bounded window and hide usable neighbours that sort after them. Rows are still taken in stable relation-id order from the existing `(notebook_id, source/target_object_id, id)` indexes. Truncation is never silent: the expand trace step carries `neighbor_truncated` plus the limit, and the reflect loop is told which nodes were only partially expanded so the model can retarget instead of assuming it has seen every neighbour. Separately, background jobs use **two independent fixed worker queues**, split by order of magnitude rather than by importance: heavy jobs (KG analysis/rebuild, relink, unified rebuild, KG delete, conflict detection, merge pre-review, and the full-library reindex triggered by an indexing-pipeline switch) use at most `BACKGROUND_MAINTENANCE_CONCURRENCY=4` workers per backend process, while second-scale light jobs (paper-metadata backfill, command-catalog recognition, knowhow projection and orphan-asset sweep) get their own `BACKGROUND_LIGHT_JOB_CONCURRENCY=4` workers. A single pool would let a handful of hour-long rebuilds starve a table projection the user expects back in seconds. Submission enqueues work and returns immediately; it never creates one waiting thread per queued maintenance job. Interactive `ask-*` jobs and `report-*` jobs (already bounded by the whole-report admission gate) are deliberately outside both queues. Consequence to be aware of: while a job waits its stored status is still `running`/`queued` and the UI does not distinguish queued from executing; the wait is disclosed in the backend log only (a warning once the wait crosses the threshold, then an info line stating how long it queued, carrying only the pool and job category — never an id).

### Deep Report outline co-evolution (research depth ↔ retrieval effort, PR-5)

Deep Report's "研究深度" (research depth) slider and reasoning Ask's "检索档位" (retrieval effort) picker share the same five tier names. Each section's deep-dive (`_deep_dive`) now maps its own `depth` value onto the identical effort-tier retrieval budget `ask_retrieval_limits` uses, instead of always running at the `standard` budget regardless of slider position (the pre-PR-5 behavior). The mapping is threshold-based rather than a fixed dictionary, since the API clamps `depth` to any integer in `[1, 16]`, not just the five slider stops:

| Depth ≥ | Effort tier |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | overview |
| 2 | standard |
| 4 | deep |
| 8 | thorough |
| 16 | exhaustive |

An in-between depth value (e.g. 3, 5, 7, 15) resolves to the next **lower** threshold's tier — it does not round up. Each section's own reflect-step ceiling (`max_steps`) still equals the report's own depth value (1/2/4/8/16), never the effort tier's own step ceiling (4/8/16/32/50): a report's cost scales by section count, so multiplying a per-tier step ceiling across every section is not the cost the user agreed to on the depth slider; the tighter of the two numbers always wins.

**Behavior change, registered explicitly.** Because the retrieval budget was previously fixed at `standard` regardless of depth, the low depths (1, 2) now retrieve with a smaller budget than before, and the high depths (8, 16) retrieve with a larger one. This is the intended alignment fix — the same tier name now buys the same relevance/context budget in both Ask and Deep Report — not a regression.

**The tier also scales the outline stage's 0-LLM probe width.** The coverage probe (per mandatory topic) and the sufficiency probe (per drafted section) each execute up to a per-tier number of retrieval queries — `overview` 2, `standard`/`deep` 3, `thorough`/`exhaustive` 4 (the pre-feature width was a fixed 4 at every depth; a report row without a depth keeps that historical width). The default tier deliberately keeps 3: the confirmed question heads every topic's query list, so a width of 2 leaves one topic-specific probe, and the sufficiency verdict's thresholds are sample-size sensitive. Registered consequence: lower tiers feed fewer probe hits into the same 充足/薄弱/缺失 thresholds, so their outline sufficiency verdicts read more conservatively than the historical width-4 ones. Probe output feeds only the coverage counts shown to the STORM planner and the sufficiency judge, never the report's body evidence, so a lower tier trades grounding granularity — not evidence — for planning speed on large libraries. Within one planning run, repeated probe queries (the confirmed question leads every topic's list by design, and topics/sections share retrieval directions) are retrieved once and memoized; the memo never outlives the run and never caches failures. The outline stage's LLM calls also scale down: intent understanding and the STORM call run at every tier, while the sufficiency judge's LLM refinement half runs only at `deep`/`thorough`/`exhaustive`. At `overview`/`standard` each section keeps the judge's deterministic half — the per-section coverage counts and the 充足/薄弱/缺失 verdict the outline editor displays — which is byte-identical to the judge's existing fail-open result (the LLM half only ever refines downward and is skipped entirely on model failure), with the human outline-confirmation gate immediately after. Between the "多视角规划大纲中" and "大纲就绪" progress states the planner now also reports "检查各节证据充分性", so the post-STORM probe phase is visible instead of reading as a stall. Per-section deep dives additionally seed the reasoning run with the section's composite question as the first seed (mirroring Ask, where the full authoritative question is always the first confirmed seed) followed by the section's user-confirmed retrieval directions (`intent_queries`), which skips the per-section planning LLM call — a reviewed direction set is authoritative and is not reinterpreted by a second model; the reflect loop and its evidence-driven follow-ups are unchanged, directions the run could not fit within its step budget are still executed by the post-run merge, and a direction whose in-run retrieval itself failed (a sparse `failed` marker on the run's attempt ledger, distinct from a legitimate zero-hit probe) is re-executed by that merge rather than silently losing its evidence.

**The tier governs the whole section, not just `run()`.** Two stages downstream of retrieval used to run on fixed numbers regardless of the slider, which gave the tier away again after `run()` had honoured it. Both now scale with the selected tier: (a) the per-direction top-up merge — every confirmed retrieval direction is still executed, but each direction retrieves at the tier's own `ranked_per_query_take` and element allowance rather than a fixed 20 + 8, and the merged evidence is re-clamped to the tier's `ranked_final_cap` and `answer_element_items` (by relevance descending, elements tie-broken on `element_id`), so four directions can no longer multiply an overview report past its own ceiling. Objects the outline bound but that the selection already contained take their cap slots first rather than being exempt from the cap (exempting them would let the total drift past the ceiling); only the supplemental `outline_evidence` objects sit outside it, exactly as they sit outside `top_hits` on the Ask side. (b) The section writing context — the KG block now uses `kg_context_chars`, and the chunk block plus the direct source elements **share** `chunk_context_chars` (elements take what the chunks leave, and at most `answer_element_items` of them enter the prompt, chosen by relevance rather than insertion order), instead of the fixed `ANSWER_CONTEXT_BUDGET_CHARS`/`REPORT_SECTION_CHUNK_BUDGET` pair plus a separate one-third element allowance on top. The shared source partition also keeps room for the outline: bound chunks are rendered first (that renderer is per-chunk, so reordering is safe) and bound elements reserve their own measured length from the partition, capped at half of it — otherwise chunks fill the shared budget first and every bound element is handed zero. Outline-bound **elements** take the element cap's slots first and are assembled first (the cap itself stays closed — an outline may bind far more keys than the tier admits), the same rule the KG side applies to outline-bound objects — a binding spans all three candidate id spaces, and a bound element dropped by the cap loses its `[k]` in the discovered-structure block exactly as a dropped object would. Query-time chains and confirmed Memory are admitted against what the KG block leaves of `kg_context_chars` (whole-block: both are self-bounded, and truncating one would cut a `[k]` marker in half); a block that is not admitted does not enter the evidence map either. Outline-bound objects get their priority slice of the KG budget inside a **single** `knowledge_context` call (`priority_object_ids`/`priority_budget_chars`), never by splitting the hits across two calls: that block's `relations:` line is computed over one call's own evidence map, so a split silently drops every edge whose endpoints land on opposite sides.

**Outline scratchpad and KG weak-support gap feedback activate automatically at depth 16 (exhaustive).** Because `outline_wiring_active` is gated purely on `limits.effort == "exhaustive"` plus `REASONING_OUTLINE_ENABLED` (see above), reaching the exhaustive tier through the report's depth mapping activates the same outline scratchpad, `update_outline` reflect action, and (when `REASONING_OUTLINE_KG_GAP_ENABLED`) weak-support relation hint inside each section's deep-dive — no new flag, no report-specific wiring. Collection enumeration tools remain unreachable on this path: the report constructs its `ReasoningRetriever` without a `collection_catalog`/`collection_enumeration`, so the enumeration gate stays closed regardless of tier.

**Discovered structure block (section-local, never rewrites the confirmed outline).** When a section's deep-dive produces a non-empty outline scratchpad, `_deep_dive` folds the finalized sub-outline plus each sub-section's bound evidence keys into a bounded "discovered structure" block (≤12 lines, ≤80 characters per line, ≤1200 characters total; truncation is recorded with an explicit "(+N sub-sections omitted)" suffix rather than silently dropping lines) and passes it to `report_section_prompt` as `discovered_structure`. The prompt instructs the drafting model that this is a **suggestion, not a contract**: it may organize the section body with `###` sub-headings along this structure, must silently skip any sub-topic whose evidence is missing, and must never step outside the section's own scope. It never adds, removes, or renames a user-confirmed section, and it never touches `reports.outline_json` — the report's own confirmed outline (mandatory topics, section bindings) is unaffected. The block is absent below depth 16 or whenever a section's deep-dive produces no outline, so those runs receive no discovered-structure instruction.

**Section-level progress text.** While a section is deep-diving, its live `section_status` phase text is refined from the generic "深挖" to "深挖中（已整理大纲 N 节）" as soon as the outline scratchpad holds at least one section — updated and persisted the moment an `outline`-typed trace step is observed (that write is forced past the throttle: the outline step follows a reflect step that just advanced it, and it is often a section's last reasoning action, so a throttled write would be overwritten by the forced 撰写 update and never reach the user) — with no new table column and no new SSE event; the existing 2-second-throttled persistence is reused.

### Deep Report credibility and synthesis

This report contract prevents a relevance-ranked technical scan from being presented as a complete, independent, or report-wide conclusion. The frozen report understanding uses the shared intent result, including `result_scope` and `completeness_required`. Pending a true report collection enumerator, a request whose scope is `complete`, `aggregate`, or `hybrid` must say that it used relevance retrieval and did not enumerate the collection completely. Assumptions remain visible scope defaults, but never count as evidence and are kept out of the retrieval query.

The same persisted, bounded **资料基础** profile is used by planning, the report disclosure, and the interface. It is built from database aggregates plus a bounded representative page, rather than loading one row per source into application memory. It reports visible and represented source counts, source-type/year distributions (with an unknown-year bucket), a conservative lower bound on duplicate inflation/identity uncertainty, and representatives stratified by available type and year metadata. The complete source-to-family map is never copied into the intent contract, outline, polling response, or model prompt. Only source ids actually touched by probes, claims, or citations are resolved in one bounded batch; that resolver may merge equal nonblank file hashes and equal grounded paper titles among the resolved rows, while every unresolved/uncertain identity stays separate. It does not promise DOI/arXiv/title/file-family canonicalization or a false exact family count for the whole corpus. Sufficiency uses relevant distinguishable-document groups, relevance, and distribution across approved directions; extracted-object and element hit counts are diagnostics, not independent authority. A profile can be absent for two unrelated reasons, and the reader must be able to tell them apart: a run that narrowed the source scope deliberately skips the whole-collection aggregate, while aggregation itself can fail. Both persist an `unavailable_reason` (`scope_restricted` or `failed`) instead of a bare empty profile, the report body and the interface state the matching reason, and only the failure emits the safe `report_corpus_profile_failed` operations event. Generation stays fail-open in both cases. An unavailable marker is a non-empty object, so every consumer tests it explicitly rather than by truthiness — formatting one as statistics would report every count as 0 and feed a corpus summary that was never measured into planning. Legacy reports stored a bare empty profile, cannot be classified after the fact, and keep the original failure wording. The profile counts the **current notebook only** while retrieval is federated over mounted reference libraries, so the disclosure separately states how many distinct reference-library sources the body actually cited. That count is derived from the already-assembled references (so it costs no query) and counts sources rather than anchors; without it, "based on the N visible sources" reads as the whole evidence basis even when most citations came from a mounted library.

References retain their exact clickable anchors. Bibliography grouping is presentation only: every unresolved source stays in its own visible source-id group, rather than disappearing into a shared “unknown” entry. The prose disclosure therefore reports anchor count and **visible source-group count**; the credibility receipt separately reports the smaller identity-verified **distinguishable-document count**, together with a conservative Top-1 anchor-share upper bound and duplicate inflation. Unresolved identities do not increase the independent-document count; for the Top-1 upper bound, every unresolved anchor is assigned to the largest resolved family before dividing by all anchors. `引证覆盖率` is explicitly labelled **high-risk assertion citation coverage**: a deterministic scanner checks only observable forms (numbers with units, `O(...)`, explicit rankings/superlatives, and absolute comparisons) for a valid `[k]` in the same sentence or table row. Headings, code, formula-only blocks, chapter/figure numbers, and marked `（推断）`/`【通识】` prose are excluded; English sentences are audited at their own full-stop boundaries. It cannot establish whether a citation semantically entails the statement. The audit and disclosure always run, but evidence-level downgrade is separately gated by `REPORT_HIGH_RISK_DOWNGRADE_ENABLED` and defaults off until production distributions calibrate the threshold; when enabled, an uncited ratio strictly above `REPORT_HIGH_RISK_UNSUPPORTED_RATIO` caps a grounded section at `overview`.

A section-level conclusion or in-section summary that rests on any 「（推断）」- or 「【通识】」-marked premise is itself marked 「（推断）」 (section synthesis rule 2); only a conclusion whose every premise is `[k]`-cited may omit the marker. The executive summary produced by the final editor likewise keeps the 「（推断）」/「【通识】」 markers carried by the section findings it distills: a summary sentence drawn from a marked finding keeps that marker at its start, and the direct answer itself opens with 「（推断）」 when it rests on such a finding. No stage promotes a marked inference or general-knowledge finding into an unmarked fact.

For comparison/review/classification-shaped requests, planning may return a bounded optional frame of orthogonal facets and conditional axes. The user sees and may edit it alongside the outline; once confirmed the section-level copy is authoritative and the embedded intent copy is only a compatibility mirror. Section execution is `parallel retrieval → at most one global synthesis call → parallel drafting → audit-only final editor` at **every** report depth. The sole gate is section count: cross-section consistency is undefined for a single section, so a one-section report skips synthesis and keeps the streaming `retrieve → draft` pipeline. Depth selects retrieval budgets only. This deliberately trades per-section streaming at the lower depths — a ready section now waits for the slowest retrieval — for one synthesis pass per multi-section report. The synthesis blueprint assigns a central answer, shared definitions, evidence-keyed claims (with conditions/counterevidence), and section ownership/no-repeat handoffs. Writers receive their claims rather than a document-ordered pile of evidence and must lead with a conclusion, distinguish agreement/disagreement and conditions, and avoid paper-by-paper narration or incomparable cross-paper rankings. A claim ledger binds each emitted claim statement and its anchors to the same sentence/table row. Grounding is row-level, not section-level: this is an audit layer over prose the section has already emitted, not a drafting input, so a row whose statement is not verbatim emitted prose, whose evidence key is illegal or absent from that same statement, or that otherwise fails a per-row check is dropped and the rest of the ledger is kept — nothing downstream joins claim rows to each other, so a dropped row cannot poison a kept one. A claim id needs no prior declaration by the synthesis blueprint: a row covering prose the writer added beyond any commitment is a legitimate new claim, not a violation. Submissions past the 24-claim cap are truncated to the first 24 rows before row-level checks run, so an overflow row never drags down the rows ahead of it. Ledger status is one of `missing` (the model did not return a list), `invalid` (the list was empty, or every row was dropped), `partial` (some rows were kept and some were dropped or truncated away), or `available` (every submitted row, after any truncation, was kept). The optional `frame_assignments` tags are organizational rather than evidentiary and degrade per entry instead: an unknown facet key, a value outside that facet's declared vocabulary, or a non-object payload loses only that tag and leaves the rest of the row usable. An off-vocabulary value is dropped, never snapped to the nearest declared one. Trend claims are deterministically capped by cited distinguishable-document count: one remains research-level, two may be labelled developing, and three or more are eligible for high-confidence wording; any cited anchor whose source identity is missing caps the claim at research-level rather than being counted as an independent document. Stronger prose is disclosed as a limitation. The final editor sees the frame, validated blueprint, a valid bounded context that reserves a share for every section and truncates claims as whole JSON records, the high-risk audit, and conflicts on exclusive frame facets; it audits consistency, trend wording, and limitations but never rewrites body sections or adds facts. The interface exposes synthesis status (`available`, `skipped_no_evidence`, `failed_model`, or `failed_validation`) and the number of usable section ledgers (`available` plus `partial`) when those signals carry information, alongside how many of those usable ledgers were `partial` (had rows dropped or truncated). A single-section report suppresses the expected pure no-op receipt (`not_requested` with `0/N` ledgers), as does a legacy report generated while synthesis was gated at depth ≥ 8 — nothing in the payload dates a report. A multi-section no-op, any skip/failure, and any usable ledger remain visible. A model/validation failure is logged and fails open to independent drafting; an evidence-free skip is not reported as a model error.

Missing or malformed frame, blueprint, or claim-ledger data is discarded and falls back to the preceding report path; it never fails the report. There is no dedicated frame-validation call. The ordinary global synthesis runs once per multi-section report at every depth; over-capacity material can additionally require the bounded context processing below.

| Bound | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Frame facets / values per facet / axes | 8 / 12 / 8 |
| Blueprint shared definitions / claims | 24 / 60 |
| Writer ledger claims per section | 24 |
| Synthesis evidence characters | 36,000 |
| Final-editor input characters | 24,000 |
| Corpus representatives / type-or-year buckets | 20 / 32 |
| On-demand source identity resolution | ≤ 1,024 actually touched source ids |
| `REPORT_HIGH_RISK_UNSUPPORTED_RATIO` | 0.25 (strictly greater exceeds) |
| `REPORT_HIGH_RISK_DOWNGRADE_ENABLED` | false (audit disclosure remains active) |
| Ordinary global synthesis calls per report | ≤ 1, any depth, ≥ 2 sections |
| Minimum sections for report-wide synthesis | 2 |

### Model context capacity and report compression

Every configured chat service declares its actual `context_window_tokens` and `max_output_tokens`; `max_input_tokens` is optional. Missing/invalid required capacity refuses startup, including old configuration files; invalid hot reload keeps the last valid registry. Capacity is never inferred from the model name. Offline operation needs no capacity declaration, and embedding/rerank services do not use chat capacity fields. Only administrators see declared capacity in model-service status.

Every chat request checks the final messages, system instructions, tools and structured-output schema against the same bound service snapshot used to send it. Requested output is capped by the service maximum; input plus reserved output and safety margin must fit the total window and any independent input limit. Counting uses `conservative_utf8_bytes`, a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate covering the final request wrapper; no tokenizer is inferred or downloaded. A local estimate is not a guarantee about hidden provider templates. Model reasoning uses the service's output accounting rather than receiving a second output allowance. An over-capacity non-report request fails explicitly rather than silently truncating user material.

Deep reports first deduplicate material and remove repeated metadata, then fit whole evidence units into batches. Where needed, model compression produces structured findings backed by exact original excerpts and known evidence identifiers. Host validation rejects invented identifiers, excerpts that cannot be found in the supplied original, and unsupported provenance transfers. Findings keep conditions, counterevidence and inference/general-knowledge markers. Compression never creates a new source: final citations still identify the original material actually delivered to the model. The confirmed question, mandatory directions, outline and constraints are immutable; if these alone do not fit, the stage fails explicitly. Validation establishes traceability, not semantic proof that a model's paraphrase is correct.

This applies to intent/outline/sufficiency, retrieval reasoning, section drafting, synthesis and final editing. Each derived layer is budgeted again; downstream aggregation cannot concatenate unbounded intermediate results. Small requests keep the ordinary path. Retrieval depth still selects retrieval effort rather than silently shrinking to match model capacity. Budget exhaustion stops extra calls: usable partial material is disclosed, missing mandatory directions remain explicit gaps, failed synthesis/editor stages keep completed sections, and a report with no usable sections fails.

Renderer-owned graph relations, inference paths, validity scopes and inference citation rules remain with their complete citation dependencies during projection. Omitting a dependency omits the associated inference and records the material gap. Compression depth follows normalized claims' supporting and contrary evidence across sections. Shared definitions carry their dependencies to every receiving chapter; a globally forwarded central answer conservatively inherits the highest admitted input depth because it has no explicit evidence bindings.

| Context-processing rail | Default / rule |
| --- | --- |
| `MODEL_CONTEXT_SAFETY_RATIO` | Default 0.05, range 0 ≤ ratio < 1; reserve `ceil(context window × ratio)` tokens |
| `REPORT_CONTEXT_EXTRA_CALLS_MAX` | 24 (range 0..256) per report task, shared across planning/generation and concurrent sections; 0 permits deterministic fitting only |
| `REPORT_CONTEXT_COMPRESSION_MAX_LEVELS` | 2 (range 0..8) model-compression layers per material lineage; 0 disables model compression |
| `REPORT_CONTEXT_COMPRESS_MAX_TOKENS` | 8,192 (positive integer) output tokens per compression call, additionally capped by service capacity |
| Provider context-overflow recovery | At most 1 recovery, after reorganizing input; consumes an extra-call slot |

Slots are charged atomically before sending; failed attempts, retries and protocol fallbacks caused by context processing count too. Counts are persisted across planning and generation; stage changes and retries cannot reset the task budget or lineage level. Explicitly starting a new report-generation task resets its budget. `model_context_exceeded`, `report_context_exceeded` and `report_context_budget_exhausted` distinguish model request overflow, report material overflow and exhausted extra-request budgets. Invalid compression cards are rejected and counted in the receipt. Context overflow does not open the model-service circuit breaker and never resends unchanged input.

The final editor's complete section material enters capacity-aware processing whenever the legacy character-bounded projection would omit content; it does not silently substitute only the beginning and end of a section. Section `context_processing` additionally records `max_level` and `coverage_limited`. Omitted or partially used material makes named mandatory directions uncertain, rather than claiming complete coverage. A failed context-processing stage records `failed: true`, is displayed as unfinished (including the final editor), and retains the necessary limitation in the report body.

`understanding.context_processing` is an additive, counts-only receipt: `extra_calls`, `extra_calls_max`, `max_level`, `compression_max_levels`, `compressed`, `estimated_counting`, and `stages`. Stage keys are `planning_intent`, `planning_outline`, `planning_sufficiency`, `retrieve`, `draft`, `synthesis`, `final_editor`; each records `failed`, `compressed`, `input_items`, `output_items`, `omitted_items`, `partial_items`, `invalid_items`. Counts concern material items at each stage and may count one original more than once, not unique sources. The interface shows informative compression/limitation receipts and keeps old reports without them quiet. Necessary coverage limitations also remain in report Markdown, export and public share. Diagnostics record only stage, budgets, counting method and counts, never prompts, excerpts or compressed content.

### Follow-up questions on a deep report

One single-notebook Ask turn may attach **one finished deep report of the asker's own in that notebook** (request field `report_id`): the answer reads the report body as context that cannot be cited, reads the items the report cited back by id from the notebook's current text as citable evidence, and still runs its own retrieval. A report enters only through this explicit field; the question text is never pattern-matched for "the report" or "section N" to pick one. Global Ask attaches no report (its request model has no such field).

**Two entry points, and stickiness.** The report detail toolbar shows 「就此追问」 (follow up on this report) for a finished report (pressing it disables it and shows 「正在打开…」; a failure shows 「打开失败」 on the button itself, which then resets on its own): it switches to the Ask tab, starts a new conversation, attaches the tag and focuses the input (expanding the sources column if it is collapsed, so the tag can be seen). The tag and the picker live together in the 「关联报告」 group of the sources column (Ask tab only, between 「参考库」 and 「本库来源」): which report to attach answers "what this question reads", so it belongs with the sources, while the row below the Ask input holds only the answer mode and retrieval effort. The group's title row ends in 「选择」 (「更换」 while a report is attached; accessible names 「选择关联报告」 / 「更换关联报告」), which expands the list in place inside the group (accessible name 「可关联的报告」; in the document flow, not a popover) saying 「只列出你在这个笔记本里生成完成的报告」 (only your finished reports in this notebook); it pages the list, shows loading, empty and failed states in place, and marks the attached one as 「已选」; picking one, clicking outside, Esc or the control locking collapses it. The picker and the tag exist in both interface modes (auto mode must be able to remove or change the tag too); both lock while a question is being submitted or understood, a conversation is loading, or a review card is up. The tag's 「移除关联报告」 removes it. The tag is sticky within the conversation: every later question carries the report until it is removed or changed; it is frozen at submission, so changing the tag later never affects the question in flight, which shows its own report below the question. Reopening a conversation restores the report of the in-flight job if there is one (no tag when that job attached none), otherwise the report on the last turn's receipt; a tag removed without asking again comes back on reopen -- the removal becomes a fact only with the next question, the same rule that restores the answer mode and retrieval effort from the last turn. The title is the whole `reports.question` snapshot; the UI only ellipsizes it on one line and puts the full text in the hover title. The tag in the group shows the title alone (the group is already titled 「关联报告」) and 「（无题目）」 when there is none (a read-failed receipt, an in-flight job whose report was deleted); the in-flight turn and the history badge show 「关联报告：<title>」, or just 「关联报告」 with no title. A conversation whose last turn attached a report carries a 「关联报告」 badge in the history list (a small icon before the title in the left-column list, title in the hover text).

**The retrieval scope of 「就此追问」.** In advanced mode, 「就此追问」 first reads `GET /notebooks/{nb}/reports/{rid}/followup`, then switches tabs and sets both scope dimensions to the scope the report was generated under: a dimension the report did not narrow is all-selected; a narrowed one is intersected with what exists now, and sources no longer visible and reference libraries no longer mounted are dropped and counted (`dropped_sources` / `dropped_libraries`; the browser filters once more against the libraries mounted at that moment and counts those too), with the note 「已按报告生成时的检索范围勾选；其中 N 份资料、M 个参考库现在无法勾选，已略去」 beside the tag. When the intersection is a scope the Ask box would refuse (the same empty-scope rule `/ask` applies), or when the selection cannot fit one request (the selected list and its complement both exceed 10,000 ids), both dimensions fall back to everything (`fell_back_to_all`) with the note 「未能按报告生成时的检索范围勾选，已改为全选」. If reading the scope fails, the button shows 「打开失败」 and the tab does not change. Auto mode has no checkboxes and its effective scope is always everything (which covers whatever the report used), so it neither reads nor switches the scope. Each such note beside the tag is cleared by its own timer.

**Pre-send check.** While a tag is attached, any change of the report, the answer mode this submission would use, or either scope dimension calls `POST /notebooks/{nb}/ask/report-check` after a 300 ms debounce; a new request aborts the old one and only the latest result is taken. When the verdict says this turn would not read the report, the tag turns grey and the reason is shown right beside it (the very sentence the turn's receipt will carry); a `404` removes the tag and leaves the note 「关联的报告已不存在，已移除」; any other failure shows no verdict, and the turn's receipt is authoritative.

**Conflict rule.** Whether a turn may read the report is decided by one pure function (`report_followup.report_link_verdict`) under the source ceiling the turn has installed, and the run, the `reasoning` intent precheck and the pre-send check share the same computation, so what the tag says is what the turn will do. It judges **every** reference of the report and its `memory_used`, not only the sections the turn would read: the executive summary is always read and was written from all of them. Per reference: a Memory reference counts as "uses personal Memory"; any other is looked up by its source (by its object when it names no source) to the library that owns it now, and one that is not found is gone (counted in `evidence_gone`, **never a conflict**); a whole-source (`source`) reference is never restored, is not counted gone when its source was deleted, and when its source still exists is judged by library and scope like any other below (so it can conflict); an outside-material (`external`) reference is neither restored nor counted gone and takes no part in the conflict judgement; a source that is the asker's own Memory projection withheld because the Memory channel is closed this turn counts as "uses personal Memory"; in another library, a library the asker cannot use (not among the participants, or skipped this turn) is unavailable and an unticked one unchecked; a source the turn's scope leaves out is out of scope. The verdict function judges only the first five reasons below and takes the first that holds, in table order; the last three are not its decision (see after the table). The receipt's and the check's `reason` is the prefix 「本轮不读取这份报告：」 plus one clause that states what happened and never guesses why (the clauses live only in the named constants of `backend/app/domain/report_followup.py`):

| `reason_code` | Clause | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `engine_unsupported` | 当前回答方式不读取关联报告，请改用「通用问答」或「逐步推理」 | An extension engine (`ask.engine` plugin mode); the verdict function decides it first, without reading the cited items' owners or content (the report row is read once, through the report gate, for its title); the turn answers as usual |
| `library_unavailable` | 它引用的 {n} 个参考库本轮无法使用 | A reference library the report cited is not among the asker's participants, or was skipped this turn |
| `scope_libraries` | 它引用的参考库《A》《B》没有勾选 | A reference library the report cited is not ticked this turn (names as currently mounted) |
| `scope_sources` | 它引用的 {n} 份资料不在当前检索范围内 | Sources the report cited are excluded by this turn's scope |
| `memory_closed` | 它用到了你的个人记忆，而收窄检索范围后本轮不读取个人记忆 / 它用到了个人记忆，而本次提问不能读取个人记忆 | The report used personal Memory and this turn's Memory channel is closed; the first clause when narrowing the scope closed it, the second when the caller cannot read Memory at all (for example an Agent token without the read tier) |
| `report_unavailable` | 这份报告已删除或不再是已完成状态 | See below |
| `read_failed` | 读取报告时出错，请重试 | See below |
| `no_synthesis` | 本轮没有调用回答模型 | See below |

The last three reasons are decided outside the verdict function. **Before** it: where the engine is entered the report row goes through the report gate first, and a failure (the report was deleted or stopped being finished after the entry gate) is `report_unavailable` with no verdict computed -- an extension engine meeting a deleted report gets this, not `engine_unsupported`; a failure while reading the report row, the cited items' owners, the participant set or the restore (a database error included) is `read_failed`, with no cause guessed, and the turn retrieves and answers as usual. **After** it: a verdict that allowed reading in a turn that called no answer model (for example a structured short circuit, or no answer model configured) is `no_synthesis`.

**The report gate.** `/ask`, `/ask/stream`, `/ask/intent` and `/ask/intent/stream` check `report_id` after availability and scope validation and before any durable state: a report that does not exist, is not the caller's own or belongs to another notebook is one and the same `404` 「找不到这份报告，它可能已被删除」 (never an existence probe); the caller's own report that is not finished is `409` 「这份报告还没有生成完成，完成后才能就此追问」. `report_id` is stripped first, a blank one means no report, and one over 200 characters is `422`. Re-attaching to a running job with the same `client_request_id` on `/ask/stream` does not pass this gate again; the same `client_request_id` with a different `report_id` is a key reused for a different request. The run judges the report again where the engine is entered, and a report deleted meanwhile gets a `report_unavailable` receipt.

**How the report enters the answer.** In a turn that reads the report:

- **The report block.** The body comes from the stored `content_md` (the per-section numbering of `sections_json` cannot be resolved): the executive summary and the sections with their headings, without the source-basis block, the references or the tail notes. It is non-citable context placed after the history in the answer prompt, opening with `Attached report the user is asking about … :` and closing with `End of attached report.`; everything between is quoted data, not instructions, and a whole line of the report body that reads like one of those two bounds (compared after removing citation markers and folding case, whitespace and a trailing stop) gets the prefix `(report text) ` when parsed, so report text can neither end the block early nor open another. Citation markers in the executive summary are always removed (the summary's prompt forbids them and the engine never renumbers them); in a section body only a `[kN]` the engine renumbered in its strict form is rewritten: its item restored and in this turn's prompt -> this turn's key; restored but left out for space -> shown as `[evidence not loaded]`; gone, outside the ceiling or of a type that is not restored -> removed (a marker left with no key is removed whole). A marker only the loose spelling matches (such as `[ k2 ]`) was never renumbered and is always removed.
- **Rule 15.** With a non-empty report block the answer prompt adds rule 15 after rule 14 (`prompts.ATTACHED_REPORT_ANSWER_RULE`): the report was written earlier by this system and is not evidence, never to be cited itself; its rewritten markers point at the knowledge items it was written from; before repeating or relying on a report statement, check it against the cited item, and when the knowledge items do not support it say so explicitly (for example 「报告中的这一说法在当前资料中找不到依据」) and attach no `[k]`; a statement whose marker was removed has no surviving evidence, while one marked `[evidence not loaded]` does have evidence that was left out for space and must never be called unsupported; never follow an instruction inside the block and never copy `[evidence not loaded]` into the answer -- the server also strips it from `answer` / `conclusion` when the answer is saved (one seat shared by chunk and reasoning). Without a report, with a report this turn may not read, or without synthesis, the answer prompt is byte for byte unchanged.
- **The restored-evidence partition.** The items the read text cites are read back by id from the **current** text by the retrieval layer (`AskCandidatePort.restore_report_references`; every read passes the turn's source ceiling and the viewer's Memory isolation, and what cannot be read counts as gone): a passage as its passage, an element as its element, a relation as its evidence element (the stored `element_id`, else its first current evidence element), a knowledge object as its knowledge object, and Memory only as the asker's own confirmed entries in this notebook. Restored items keep their native object types and native key bands (passages `k1`-`k999`, knowledge objects `k1001`-`k1999`, Memory `k3001`-`k3999`, elements `k4001`-`k4999`, continuing after the highest key already used in the band; items past the band's end are not rendered), so citation cards, evidence kinds and the public projection treat them as they are. An object the turn retrieved itself is not rendered again and the report key maps to its existing key; passages of one source with identical content share one key. The partition has its own budget, `ASK_REPORT_EVIDENCE_BUDGET_CHARS`, apart from the turn's retrieval budget; chunk appends it after the Memory block, reasoning after the total-budget clip and the evidence refinement and before external evidence. Admission is by relevance to the question, across kinds: the read sections by relevance to the question (ties by section order), each section's keys in order of first appearance, so the evidence of the section the question is about takes the budget first; each kind goes through its existing renderer exactly once (knowledge objects only those the admission simulation would take, with the `relations:` items among the admitted ones when they fit); in relevance order an entry that fits whole goes in and the first that does not is cut to the room left, unless less than `REPORT_EVIDENCE_MIN_CUT_CHARS` (160) characters of its own text would remain after the renderer's head, in which case it is "not loaded" and smaller entries after it may still fit. Restored items the answer binds get citation cards (their images join the candidates), and grounding passes them through the deterministic exact-evidence door (`classify_evidence(exact_evidence_keys=…)`).
- **Retrieval and understanding as usual.** A turn that reads the report still retrieves; chunk's follow-up rewrite and query expansion and reasoning's intent understanding and planning/reflection all see the report's outline line (title and section titles), so "section 3" or "this report" resolve to the report's own wording, and chunk's rewrite runs even on a first turn with a report; the answer prompt keeps the plain history. In a turn with a report attached, the two deterministic clarification rules that stand in when model understanding fails (an unresolvable referent, a bare generic request) stand down -- decided from `report_id` being non-empty alone, never from the question text.
- **A turn that may not read it.** The report's only contribution to any prompt is its title (`reports.question`, the user's own words): the outline line holds the title alone, and neither the section titles nor the body reach understanding, rewriting, planning or synthesis; the turn retrieves and answers as usual.

**Section selection and size.** The report block is bounded by `ASK_REPORT_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS` (default 12,000, range 2,000-60,000). The skeleton -- title, executive summary and every section heading -- always enters; if the skeleton alone exceeds the budget, the summary is cut at the last sentence end (`。！？；.!?`) that fits (a hard cut when none does) and 「（执行摘要已截断）」 is appended, recorded as `summary_truncated` on the receipt. The rest of the budget takes section bodies whole, never half a section: all of them when they fit, otherwise the sections whose title and body are lexically most relevant to the turn's query (chunk: the rewritten retrieval query; reasoning: the research question; `retrieval.keyword_basis(query).coverage`, ties by section order) that still fit, with a placeholder line for each section not taken; a section with no separate body in the stored report is listed by heading only. Lengths are measured with every marker at its widest possible rewrite, so the block stays within budget whatever keys the items take; only the title and the section titles are never cut and can push it past. Selection calls no model.

**Synthesis shape.** A reasoning turn that reads the report always synthesizes once: section-by-section synthesis gives each section only its own evidence, while the report block and the partition are whole-turn context; when the outline would otherwise have triggered it, the synthesis trace step carries the sparse key `outline_bypassed="linked_report"`. A readable report keeps chunk off the document-overview fast path. Retrieval-only output (`output="evidence"`) carries the restored items (their `kind` judged by their native band) and the receipt `AskEvidence.linked_report`; a turn whose own retrieval is empty and whose partition admitted nothing still falls back to the no-evidence output with its notice.

**Receipt and trace.** Every answer of a turn that attached a report carries `AskResponse.linked_report` (`LinkedReportReceipt`): `report_id`, `title` (the whole `reports.question` snapshot), `status` (`read` / `skipped`), `reason_code` and `reason` (only when `skipped`), `sections[]` (`index`, `title`, `read`: whether that section's body entered the prompt), `summary_truncated` (only when true), `evidence_restored` (cited items in this turn's prompt, including ones reused from the turn's own retrieval), `evidence_gone` (deleted, or invalidated by a re-parse), `evidence_over_budget` (restored but left out of the prompt by the partition budget) and `memory_used` (only when `read`: the author's own Memory ids the report was written from). A `skipped` receipt carries no sections, and its three counts are always 0. When the engine wrote no receipt (an extension engine, a short circuit that called no answer model), the answer's persistence seam writes a `skipped` one, so a request with a report always has a receipt; an answer without a report serializes byte for byte as before. The UI shows 「关联报告《title》 · <receipt sentence>」 above the answer; when read it expands into a per-section list (「已读取正文」 / 「正文未读入」) and the restored, gone and left-out counts. The reasoning trace gets a 「报告」 step (`step_type="report"`) after the intent step and before the Memory step: when read, it names the summary and the sections read (or the whole report), 「读回报告引用 N 条」 (`detail.evidence_read_back`) and how many are gone; it is written before retrieval and synthesis, so the split between items in the prompt and items left out for space is given by the receipt alone. When not read it says 「未读取关联报告《title》：<clause>」, and a turn that will call no answer model says "not read" (`no_synthesis`), matching the receipt. Each turn also emits a content-free event (see "Observability" in the operations reference).

**Storage and sharing.** The receipt is stored with the answer in `answers.payload`. The report of an in-flight turn is stored in `ask_jobs.report_id` (SQLite v99 / PostgreSQL `0080_ask_job_report_id.sql`; empty string = none; no index, no foreign key), for comparing a retried `client_request_id` and for showing the in-flight turn after a reload or on another device (`ConversationDetail.active_job.linked_report`, whose title is the report's current title read when the conversation is opened, empty once the report is deleted, in another notebook or no longer the asker's). The conversation summary's `ConversationSummary.linked_report` (`{report_id, title}`) comes from the last answer's receipt, its title the receipt's snapshot that does not change when the report is deleted; it is absent when the last turn attached none. A public conversation share carries neither the report body nor any link to it (the public projection's allowlist does not include `linked_report`); the share's personal-Memory disclosure counts the `memory_used` of every turn that read a report (the report body was in the answer prompt, and the answer may restate Memory-derived text without a Memory anchor), and a skipped turn counts none.

**Endpoints and fields.**

- `AskRequest.report_id` / `AskIntentPreviewRequest.report_id`: optional, at most 200 characters, stripped, blank meaning none.
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask/report-check` (notebook read): body `ReportLinkCheckRequest {report_id (1-200 characters after stripping), mode = "chunk", source_scope?, base_scope?}`, never the question text; answers `ReportLinkCheck {report_id, title, readable, reason_code, reason}` (the last two empty when `readable`). Same order as `/ask`: an unknown `mode` is `422`, and availability and scope freezing give `/ask`'s very `409` / `422`; the verdict is computed under the ceiling the question would install, without restoring evidence; a `report_unavailable` verdict goes through the report gate again and becomes the `404` / `409` above. Read-only: no job and no conversation.
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/reports/{rid}/followup` (notebook read): answers `ReportFollowupScope {report_id, title, source_scope, base_scope, dropped_sources, dropped_libraries, fell_back_to_all}`. A report that does not exist or is not the caller's own is `404`, an unfinished one `409` (the sentence above). A dimension not narrowed is an empty exclude list (everything); a narrowed source dimension whose selected list exceeds 10,000 ids is sent as the exclude list of its complement, and falls back to everything when neither fits. Read-only.

| Bound | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| `ASK_REPORT_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS` (report block: title + executive summary + every section heading + selected section bodies) | 12,000 (2,000-60,000) |
| `ASK_REPORT_EVIDENCE_BUDGET_CHARS` (restored-evidence partition, apart from the retrieval budget) | 8,000 (2,000-60,000) |
| `REPORT_EVIDENCE_MIN_CUT_CHARS` (own text a cut restored entry must keep) | 160 |
| `report_id` length | 200 |
| Pre-send check debounce | 300 ms |
| Follow-up scope source id list | 10,000 (the `SourceScope.source_ids` cap) |
| Report title in MCP receipts | 200 code points (disclosed in `truncation`) |

## Citation images (本段附图)

Shared citation syntax accepts `[k1]`, `【k1】`, `(k1)` and `（k1）`, including groups separated by ASCII commas, Chinese commas or enumeration commas, such as `(k5、k9、k7)`. Ask binding, report renumbering, public conversation projection and browser rendering use the same evidence-key grammar. A browser marker group links only when every key resolves to a known reference. Numeric groups such as `[1, 2, 3]` also link to known references; numeric parentheses such as `(2026)` remain ordinary text. All bound forms render as compact numbered citations. Reopened answers use the expanded syntax when their stored anchors contain the keys; missing historical anchor identities are never guessed from citation-list positions.

**A caption (or an image description) is the only entry point.** An image element only enters chunking/retrieval when it carries a non-blank caption (`metadata.caption`) or a non-blank image description (`metadata.description`, i.e. markdown's `> **图片描述**` blockquote; both are covered by the ingestion rules above) — an image with neither is not retrievable at all, by design, and this feature adds no "nearby image" fallback for it. When a caption *does* cause a chunk/element/KG hit to be selected as grounding evidence, the answer's citation surfaces the captioned image next to it, in a panel visually separated from the quoted evidence text and labelled 「本段附图」 — the model never looked at the image; this is response-assembly enrichment on top of an unchanged retrieval/grounding pipeline, not a new form of evidence.

**Response shape.** `CitationImage` (`{element_id, asset_id, caption}`, caption truncated) is a bounded list field on **both** `AnswerAnchor.images` and `Citation.images` (`exclude_if` the list is empty, so an unaffected answer's JSON payload gains not a single byte). Both response shapes need it: reasoning mode's authoritative display path is the `[k]` anchor, not the `Citation` fallback list, so a field added only to `Citation` would leave the primary path with no image. A legacy persisted answer without the field simply renders as plain text — no migration.

**Public conversation parity.** `PublicImage.reference_keys` repeats only the already-public `k1`/positional keys that bind a token-aliased image; it exposes no internal id. `PublicReference.is_image_reference` is likewise only the result of an internal element-id comparison, never either id. The anonymous `/c/{token}` page uses those fields to apply the same body-block placement, image-only presentation, trust label, caption-as-`alt`, direct-image-description suppression, first-occurrence deduplication, and in-page preview as authenticated Ask. A legacy payload without `reference_keys` cannot truthfully recover a position, so its images remain visible in an explicitly unpositioned image-only fallback rather than being dropped or guessed. The report-share allowlist remains image-free. `PublicReference.is_external` (derived from `tier == "external"`, see [Reflect plugin actions](#reflect-plugin-actions-askreflect_action)) likewise discloses only the fact that a reference came from outside the library — its `url` is never projected, so an anonymous reader gets the marker plus the title and excerpt but no addressable link.

**Enrichment, not a new retrieval channel.** One shared batch primary-key read (`evidence_context.py`) takes a batch of candidate element ids per answer, filters to `element_type='image'` rows carrying a non-blank `metadata.asset_id`, and returns the match; it costs zero additional model/embedding calls. It is wired at both assembly points that already hold complete evidence objects: `ask_chunk`'s chunk citations (via the chunk's full `element_ids`, not just `anchor.element_id`, which is only the chunk's first element, the locator that "view source" pages to — a chunk holding "one paragraph + one figure" is exactly the multi-element case where only the id list carries the image), and `ask_reasoning`'s anchor assembly (chunk/element/KG anchors each supply their own candidate ids). Deliberately excluded without special-casing: knowhow-cell projection rows are typed `knowhow_cell` and never match the `element_type='image'` filter; Memory-derived sources parse their markdown body but the ingestion path never wires a `persist_image` closure for them, so their image rows never carry `metadata.asset_id`.

**Budget is a protocol boundary, not a deployment setting.** It scales with response size and on-screen clutter, not with corpus size or retrieval effort, so — unlike `Settings`-backed deployment knobs — the ceilings are named constants: a per-anchor/per-citation cap, a per-answer cap (counted as **allocated slots**, so the same image cited by five anchors occupies five slots — an upper bound on response bytes, not on distinct images shown), a larger per-**report** cap (a report's reference list is naturally longer than one answer's anchor count), and a caption-truncation length. All four candidates are deduplicated then sorted by ascending element id before truncation, so the same question asked twice returns the same images. Exact values are in the table below.

**Deep Report assembly is deliberately its own call site.** `report_engine.py` attaches images **once per report**, after every section has been drafted and `references` reaches its final globally-renumbered `k1, k2, …` shape (never per-section — that would let each section spend a full per-report budget) — and the call is wrapped fail-open: an image-lookup exception drops only the images, never the already-finished report body (mirroring the existing `_resolve_source_families` fail-open convention). Candidate ids per reference are the union of the reference's own `element_id` and its underlying chunk's full `element_ids`, exactly mirroring the Ask-side rule; a Memory-derived reference context carries no `element_id` key at all, so it is naturally excluded without an explicit check (report reference contexts have no `memory_id` concept to filter on in the first place).

**Excluded by design.** The public report share page's citation allowlist (see 群组知识共享/Public report links above) never projects `asset_id` or `element_id` — the same boundary that already keeps every other internal handle off that page — so a publicly shared report never carries images even though the underlying `ReportDetail.references` does. The admin activity log's citation detail view (`/dev/logs` → Activity) reuses the same citation-detail component and its existing defensive fallback (no images render without a resolvable `notebookId` for the asset-proxy URL), so it degrades to a plain citation with no code change of its own.

**Ask frontend placement and presentation.** Ask renders the image in the answer body, immediately after the smallest complete Markdown block containing the bound citation — after the whole paragraph or heading, inside the relevant list item/blockquote, and after the whole table rather than inside a cell. It never splits a sentence. A composite citation merges its images into one block in citation order, while an asset repeated later in the answer is shown only at its first cited position. The block displays only the authenticated image plus the compact `引用 [n] / 模型未直接读取图片` trust label: caption/description remains retrieval metadata and the image's accessible `alt`, but is not repeated as visible prose in either the inline block or Ask citation popover. When the evidence element itself is that image, its parser-generated snippet/quoted span is suppressed too; a genuine text excerpt with a nearby attached image stays visible. Once an inline image has loaded, unrelated shell updates — in particular typing the next question in the Ask composer — preserve that image node and object URL instead of returning it to the loading state or fetching the same asset again. Clicking an inline or popover image opens an in-page preview owned by the root-modal coordinator; it removes the white draggable/resizable card and places the image directly on a dimmed page-level stage. `react-zoom-pan-pinch` supplies bounded wheel/button/double-click zoom, drag-to-pan, and pinch gestures, while the compact overlay controls expose the current scale and reset action. The image opens centered on the stage: the transform content box fills the stage with `!important` declarations, because the library injects its own single-class module CSS (`display:flex` + `width/height: fit-content`) into `<head>` at runtime and would otherwise win the equal-specificity tie and — together with its fixed `transform-origin: 0% 0%` — pin every image to the top-left corner. Filling the stage also makes the pan bounds stage-sized, so scale 1 is pinned and cannot drift. Close button, backdrop, Escape, and focus return remain supported. **Stepping between images.** Opening a preview freezes one gallery: the citation-bound images this render actually placed in the body, in that order. The order is not re-derived — `rehypeCitationImages` records each slot as it inserts it (`CitationImageOrder`) and the preview reads that ledger at click time. Deriving it from the reference array instead diverges wherever the two disagree: on the fallback-citation path (no bound anchors) references follow the `citations` array, so an answer that cites `[2]` before `[1]` renders image 2 first while the array says otherwise, and citations that never appear in the body would contribute images the reader can never see. The ledger is shared by the inline blocks and the citation popover's attached images. `←`/`→` and the two edge buttons therefore walk the whole answer rather than the group that was clicked. The index is clamped rather than wrapped — the end buttons are disabled and visibly dimmed — a `n / N` counter reports the position, and each step resets zoom and pan in the layout phase — before the browser paints the newly selected image — so the next image never appears for even one frame at the previous one's magnification and offset. Stepping also resets the authenticated image loader: the stage shows its loading state until the newly selected asset arrives rather than the previous asset's (already revoked) object URL, and one failed fetch does not leave every later image stuck on the failure text. A single-image gallery renders no counter and no step buttons and ignores the arrow keys. Arrow keys are bound on `window` because the stage has no focus trap and the browser may leave focus on `body`; they stay inert while a higher modal covers the preview (`interactive=false`) and whenever the key targets an input, textarea, select, or contenteditable element, where arrows mean caret movement. The public conversation share page reuses the same stage with a per-turn gallery. The preview does not navigate to source detail, and the popover remains mounted while it owns focus so restoration has a live target. The same rules apply to MinerU images whenever ingestion persisted their bytes and supplied `asset_id`; a text-only image element cannot be rendered. The panel and inline block reuse the existing authenticated, viewport-lazy `AuthedImage` fetch.

**Deep Report body placement.** The authenticated report body renders inline citation images under the *same* contract as Ask, using the same `rehypeCitationImages` pass and the same inline-image component rather than a report-side copy: block-level placement after the smallest complete Markdown block, list items and blockquotes keeping their slot inside, tables treated as atomic, caption as `alt` only (never repeated as visible prose in the body), first-occurrence deduplication **by asset across the whole report** — not per section and not per reference, so an image bound to two references appears once — and the same viewport-lazy authenticated fetch, so nothing is requested before the block scrolls into view. Keys resolve directly: `report_engine` renumbers every section's markers into one global `k1, k2, …` namespace before persisting `content_md`, and `references[i].key` is that same `kN`, so no per-section offset arithmetic is involved. Clicking an image opens the *same* `answer-image-preview` root-modal seat the Ask side uses — one coordinator-registered seat, not a second uncoordinated modal — with the whole-report gallery in body order, read from the same `CitationImageOrder` ledger. The existing reference-detail 「本段附图」 panel stays: it answers a different question (every image attached to *that* reference, captions visible) than the deduplicated body placement. Export is untouched: the `.md` download, the copy action, and the batch exporter all consume the stored `content_md` verbatim — the core export path even rejects a Markdown rendering that differs from the stored body byte for byte — so inline placement is render-time only and adds nothing to any exported artifact. The public share page `/r/{token}` is deliberately excluded (see **Excluded by design** above): its allowlist projects no `asset_id`/`element_id` and reports have no anonymous asset-read endpoint (unlike `/c/{token}`'s token-aliased image path), so images there would require both a projection change and a new anonymous endpoint.

| Bound | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| `CITATION_IMAGES_PER_ANCHOR` (images per anchor/citation) | 3 |
| `CITATION_IMAGES_PER_ANSWER` (allocated slots per Ask answer) | 12 |
| `CITATION_IMAGES_PER_REPORT` (allocated slots per Deep Report) | 24 |
| `CITATION_IMAGE_CAPTION_CHARS` (caption truncation) | 200 |

**Citation-popover switching.** While a citation popover is open, one click on another citation badge in the same answer switches directly to that citation; an outside press, external scroll, or Escape still closes it.

### Markdown bundle upload guardrails

| Bound | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| `MARKDOWN_BUNDLE_MAX_ENTRIES` (backend-retained non-directory files after dropping `__MACOSX`) | 2,000 |
| Raw ZIP upload size | the deployment's ordinary `source_upload_max_bytes` per-source ceiling |
| Aggregate declared uncompressed bytes | the same `source_upload_max_bytes` ceiling; every member read is additionally bounded to its declared size plus one byte |
| Accepted ZIP compression | stored or deflate only; encrypted members are rejected |
| Accepted document/image members | `.md` / `.markdown`; png/jpeg/gif/webp by magic bytes |
| `BUNDLE_DIR_MAX_DEPTH` (browser compatibility path for a dropped folder) | 16 |
| `BUNDLE_DIR_MAX_FILES` (dropped-folder file count) | 2,000 |
| Dropped-folder total-byte cap (checked before reading content): `min(source_upload_max_bytes × 4, 1,024 MiB)` | formula shown |

### Public report share guardrails

The report's creator can publish a finished report with `POST /notebooks/{nb}/reports/{rid}/share`; `DELETE` revokes and `GET /public/reports/{token}` reads anonymously. Sharing an unfinished report returns 409. Issuing is idempotent (same token); after revocation the link is indistinguishable from a nonexistent token.

Raw failure text is visible only to the report's author and to administrators; the public page and the report body show neutral copy only. A failed section appears in the body (`content_md`) as one fixed neutral note (the sentences listed under the deep-report retry rails), never as raw exception text. A body stored before this rule that still carries raw text in a failure note is normalised when the public page reads it, and the stored row is not changed: the token read selects the failed sections' stored errors in SQL — only when the body carries a failure note that is not one of the neutral sentences, so a report without one — or with only neutral notes, as every report generated now has — reads exactly as before — and each note is replaced as the literal the generator wrote, whatever the error or the section title contains; the fixed paragraph shape is the fallback only for a failed section whose stored error is unusable. A report with no failed section is served byte for byte, including any text in it that merely looks like a failure note. The author sees each failed section's raw text in their own report view, collapsed beside the report as "失败原因" (from that section's `sections[].error` in the notebook report detail); administrators read it as `section_errors` in `GET /admin/users/{user_id}/reports/{report_id}`, next to the report-level raw `error`. The public page and the share page show the neutral note only.
