This deliberately differs from the activity surface, where raw `error` is administrator-only and the author's own self-service call gets an empty string: the notebook report detail answers its creator alone, so it keeps the author's full diagnostics. A shared conversation's public page carries no reasoning trace, so a trace step's raw `detail.error` likewise reaches only the asker and administrators.

Anyone other than the report's creator — the notebook owner and the deployment admin included — gets the same 404 as for a missing report, so a report's existence is never revealed; the author-only rule below also answers 403 to a caller who is past that check but is not the author. Before publishing, `GET /notebooks/{nb}/reports/{rid}/share/disclosure` returns `{memory_count, foreign_memory_count}`. `memory_count` is the number of distinct private Memory entries of the author whose content the public page may carry: Memory the report cites (citations that are a Memory, and citations recorded at generation time as coming from the author's Memory) together with Memory that may have entered any prompt while the report was produced — the planner's Memory lines, each section's confirmed-Memory block, and the Memory behind every source that retrieval handed the planning and generation runs (the corpus map and coverage probes, the section research agent's observations including evidence it later dropped, the report-wide synthesis payload, the section contexts), cited or not — because the body can restate any of it without a citation marker. If a retrieval result is too large to record completely, the planning or generation fails instead of under-counting. `foreign_memory_count` is the number of other members' Memory entries the report cites; when it is above zero the report is never published: `POST .../share` answers 403 "The report cites another member's personal memory and cannot be published" whatever is acknowledged; clicking "Share" says so right below the button and creates no link; a link issued earlier stops serving — the public page re-checks on every open and answers the same 404 as a revoked link, and the author's page says the link no longer opens and offers only unsharing.

When `memory_count` is above zero, `POST .../share` must carry `{"acknowledged_memory_count": N}`; the server counts again on that request and inside the transaction that issues the token, and answers 409 `{"detail": {"code": "share_disclosure_required", "memory_count": N, "new_memory_count": M}}` with no token only when the count is above the acknowledgement (`M` is how many more). A count at or below the acknowledgement is accepted: it can only fall, when a cited Memory stops being recognisable, while the page still carries the excerpt the author saw counted; an acknowledgement above the count is accepted too (the client never sends more than it showed). On PostgreSQL that transaction holds share locks, until it commits, on the Memory rows and source rows behind the cited sources without a stored record — the Memory rows in Memory-id order, the order the Memory purge locks them in; on SQLite it holds the process-wide database write lock, as every write does. Re-sharing a report that is already public returns the existing link without asking. A report with no Memory publishes exactly as before, with no request body; revoking never asks. The public page is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Reports produced before this release are recognised only as far as they recorded. A report planned before this release but generated after it carries the generation's record, so only the Memory its planner saw is missing from the count. A report both planned and generated before this release carries no record of the Memory used while it was produced: only its citations can be recognised — citations that are a Memory, and cited sources that are still the author's (or another member's) Memory sources — so Memory restated in its body without a citation, and citations whose Memory source has since been removed, are neither counted nor refused. Text without a source — the fused concept definitions in the knowledge graph — cannot be attributed to a Memory. A finished report keeps the excerpts and titles it cited, and whatever its body says about them, after the cited Memory is deleted: its creator, the deployment admin (audit) and, if shared, anyone with the link can still read them. The admin audit detail shows each citation without the internal Memory record fields.

The anonymous projection allowlists body, research question, timing and citation title, original filename, location and excerpt. It excludes `source_id`, `element_id`, `object_id`, `notebook_id` and `understanding` (including intent/source scope); corpus-basis disclosure is already frozen into `content_md`. Anonymous handlers do not bind a request user or consult user-dependent repository methods. A citation of the author's own personal memory — a citation that is a Memory, one recorded at generation time as the author's Memory, or one whose source is the author's Memory projection (resolved in one batched read per page) — carries `is_memory: true`, and its title loses the engine's `Memory · ` label prefix; every other citation omits the field, so a page without Memory is unchanged byte for byte. The page labels such a citation's location "作者的个人记忆".

Every open also re-checks, as the report's creator, each mounted library the report quotes: if one is no longer an effective participant of the report's notebook — it was unmounted, or the mount stopped being effective — the page answers the same 404 as an unknown token, and restoring the mount revives the same link. Only citations the engine marked as coming from a mounted library (`from_reference_library`), or written before that mark, matter. Since this release a marked citation also stores that library (`notebook_id`, internal to the stored report, never on the public page), so it is named even after its source is deleted. At generation the library is the cited source's owning notebook, else — for a knowledge object cited without a source — the library its evidence came from; the library's tier is only the last fallback. Otherwise the library is read: the cited sources of any type — the hidden Memory and Knowhow projections included — in one batched read, then the knowledge objects whose source did not resolve (a knowledge object can be cited without a source) in one more. Whether another member's personal memory may be published is decided before this check and is unaffected by it. A marked citation whose library can no longer be named — written before this release, with its source and object gone — makes the page unreadable too, since nothing can show the library is still mounted: for a report generated before this release, deleting a cited source of a mounted library makes its link stop working. A report whose citations are all marked local reads nothing for this check. Publishing applies the same check up front: `POST .../share` of a report quoting a mounted library that is no longer effective for its creator answers 404 "部分笔记本已无法访问，请重新选择范围。" and issues no link. Whether a mount is effective depends on the viewer (see "A mount counts only for those who may read the mounted library"); here the viewer is the report's creator.

The public page shares the in-app citation/table/code/math rendering. Citation numbers come from their `kN` keys, not positions, and jump to the matching excerpt; entries lacking both title and excerpt are omitted. It cannot open authenticated sources. Wide content scrolls within its block; the page loads KaTeX styling. The projection and visible truncation disclosures follow the rails below.

| Bound | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| `REPORT_QUESTION_MAX_CHARS` (research question at **creation**; over-limit is refused with 422, never stored clipped — the composer enforces the same limit by blocking submission and saying so, counted in Unicode code points to match Pydantic rather than clipping the text) | 4,000 |
| `MAX_REFERENCES` (citations projected per report; excess is disclosed as `truncated_references`) | 500 |
| `MAX_REFERENCE_TITLE_CHARS` (per-reference title / original file name) | 400 |
| `MAX_SNIPPET_CHARS` (per-citation excerpt) | 1,200 |

The body is returned whole. The public question is the original `reports.question`, not the confirmed `understanding.resolved_question`. Creation rejects questions above `REPORT_QUESTION_MAX_CHARS` with 422; the composer counts Unicode code points, retains the input, states the current/maximum count and disables submission. Legacy over-limit questions are bounded with `question_truncated` and a visible 「研究问题过长，已截断」 hint; stored data is unchanged.

Over-limit reference title/original filename/excerpt sets `title_truncated`/`file_name_truncated`/`snippet_truncated` with a visible hint. Server-derived `key` (24), `location` (200) and timestamp (64) bounds carry no truncation flags. Creation rails live in `models/reports.py` and frontend `REPORT_INPUT_LIMITS`; projection rails live in `services/report_public_view.py`. Conversation constants below are independent, but share the disclosure rule.

### Public conversation share guardrails

A conversation's creator can publish completed turns at `/c/{token}`. Under `/notebooks/{nb}/conversations/{cid}/share`, `POST` issues/updates, `GET` reads the creator's token/watermark, and `DELETE` revokes. `GET /public/conversations/{token}` and `GET /public/conversations/{token}/assets/{alias}` are anonymous. Non-owner and nonexistent conversations both return 404; blank creators and conversations without answers return 409 (no token remains issued).

**MCP answer links (`alnk-`).** The third capability namespace: an Agent issues an expiring link for **one answered MCP job** with `delivery="link"` on `ask` / `get_ask` (table `answer_links`, SQLite v94 / PostgreSQL `0074_answer_links.sql`: link token, job kind and id, owner, issuing token, created/expiry times, unique per (job, issuing token), no foreign keys). It is served by the same public page `/c/{token}` and the same anonymous endpoints, routed by the `alnk-` prefix, so it can never resolve a `cshr-` / `gshr-` token. The page holds **that one turn only**, goes through the same allowlist projection (no ids, no reasoning trace, no intent) and carries `Cache-Control: no-store`; the response gains an `expires_at` that only this branch emits, which the page shows as the validity line. Every open re-checks on the server in a fixed order: an unknown token is 404; an **expired row that is still present** is 410 (the page endpoint returns the Chinese detail 「链接已过期，请重新提问」 via `user_error()`; the image endpoint keeps 404 for expiry) whatever the other checks would say; after that any failing check is a 404 indistinguishable from an unknown token. The checks are everything `get_ask` applies to the issuing token NOW -- token not revoked or expired, Profile enabled, owner still eligible, **the answer-links switch still on**, the Ask tier still held, the job owned by the link's owner and started via MCP, the single-notebook job's notebook still on the token's allowlist, a run that had the private-Memory channel open requiring the token to still hold `memory:read`, the owner still able to read the notebook -- plus the session share's snapshot predicate (shared code: mounted reference libraries still effective); a global job is checked against the allowlist as a ceiling. Retrieval-only (`output="evidence"`), unfinished and answer-less jobs are always 404. Turning the switch off and on again revives still-unexpired old links; revoking the token kills all its links at once. Image aliases are derived per link token and only the images that one answer quotes are readable; anything else is 404.

A link lives for `link_ttl_hours` given at issue time (default `MCP_ANSWER_LINK_TTL_HOURS`). Deleting a job, conversation or token does **not** cascade to link rows; they 404 on read because a check fails, and the space is reclaimed by a sweep run opportunistically on the issuing write (at most once per process per hour, marked only after the write commits): rows expired beyond the `MCP_ANSWER_LINK_GRACE_HOURS` grace period, rows whose issuing token is revoked or gone, and rows whose job is gone are deleted. Inside the grace period a reader sees 410; after the sweep the same link is 404 again, and so it is at once when the same token re-issues a link for that job (the expired row is replaced). A shadow switch does not copy the table, so old links 404 afterwards and `get_ask(delivery="link")` re-issues; in incremental cross-environment sync it is a local table and is not carried over.

Issuing retains the token and advances `shared_through_at`/`shared_through_id`. Body `expected_through_id` pins publication to the exact answer the user reviewed, excluding later arrivals; a deleted boundary returns 409. Empty/absent body selects the latest answer. The snapshot uses the boundary answer's `(created_at, rowid/ordinal)` keyset, so same-instant later answers stay excluded; if the answer no longer resolves, it falls back to the time interval. In-flight jobs without answer rows are excluded. A published prefix longer than `MAX_TURNS` is shown as its **newest** `MAX_TURNS` turns, so the shared answer is always on the page; the response then carries `omitted_earlier_turns` (how many older turns are not included; absent while 0, so a page of ordinary length is byte for byte as before) next to `truncated_turns`, and the page says so above the first turn: 「会话过长，此处只展示最近 N 轮，更早的 M 轮未包含。」. The read fetches only that window (backwards under a `LIMIT`) and counts the older turns only when there are any. The page, its image and Memory lookups, the live re-checks, the share window and the Memory disclosure all cut through this one window (`public_window`).

The payload uses the report-style allowlist and rendering, additionally omitting `reasoning_trace`, `intent`, `retrieval_scope`, `retrieval_query` and every addressable id, including `memory_id`. The receipt of a follow-up on a deep report (`linked_report`) is not on the allowlist: the public page carries neither the report body nor which report a turn attached. Cited private-Memory excerpts are disclosed, with their count asked of the author before sharing (below); a reference that is the creator's own personal memory carries `is_memory: true` and its title loses the `Memory · ` label prefix, any other reference omits the field. The page is served with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Result cards are omitted with `PublicTurn.omitted_result_sets`. Images use a per-token HMAC `conversation_asset_alias`, never real asset ids: only snapshot-referenced images resolve, `Cache-Control: no-store` applies, revocation kills them, and aliases differ across tokens. A global turn whose terminal citation check found failures exposes `PublicTurn.citation_check` (only when `failed > 0`, counts coerced to non-negative integers, `outcome` always `partial`) and `PublicReference.verification` (only the three public values) as a snapshot of the moment the answer was produced, and the page states it in the past tense; an image attached only to a flagged reference is neither listed nor served by its alias, and a flagged card offers no way into the original.

The history-card action publishes the current last answer; the action after an answer's copy button sends that answer's id. Failure to load detail never substitutes an empty body for that explicit boundary. Watermarks only advance: for an answer earlier than the live boundary, the dialog offers no publish action, says the link covers this answer plus N later turns, and computes disclosure counts from the full live scope. Narrowing requires revoke-then-reshare. A sixth position, `omitted`: the link is past the answer but the answer has slid off the page (the page shows only the newest 500 turns up to the watermark, judged on that window, never a fixed distance) — the dialog then says 「这条回答不在链接里：公开页只显示最近 500 轮，这条回答在没有包含的更早 N 轮里。现在复制发出去的快照不含它。撤销即刻失效。」 instead of "already in the link", offers no publish action, and points to 「公开范围只能往后推、不能收回；要让链接包含这条回答，请先「撤销分享」，再从这条回答重新分享。」. A conversation of at most 500 turns never reaches it. When the range is longer than the page, the dialog says so with the exact number: 「公开页只显示最近 500 轮，更早的 N 轮未包含。」 for what the link holds (or what sharing would publish), and 「更新后公开页只显示最近 500 轮，更早的 N 轮未包含。」 next to the update button; a conversation of ordinary length shows neither. A notebook conversation's dialog counts from the conversation's full turns (its detail read is not paged); a global conversation's dialog asks the counts endpoint (see [Global conversation sharing](#global-conversation-sharing)); both fall back to the no-number sentence under the same conditions (counts unavailable, the asked answer unresolved, the watermark unknown, or the personal-memory disclosure failed). Numeric bounds are below.

**Personal-memory disclosure (server side).** `GET /notebooks/{nb}/conversations/{cid}/share/disclosure?through_id=` returns `{memory_count, new_memory_count, current_memory_count}`. `through_id` is the answer the share would be pinned to, with the same meaning as `expected_through_id` (empty = the newest answer). `memory_count` is the number of distinct personal-memory entries of the author over exactly the turns the share would publish — the snapshot's keyset prefix ending at `through_id`, cut to the page's window (its newest `MAX_TURNS`) — read off every anchor and citation of those turns: citations carrying a `memory_id`, anchors that are a Memory, and anchors or citations whose source is one of the author's Memory sources (a Memory projection hit, resolved in one batched read); for a turn that read an attached deep report, also the `memory_used` of its receipt (the author's Memory the report was written from: the report body was in the answer prompt, and the answer may restate Memory-derived text without a Memory anchor; a turn that did not read the report counts none). `new_memory_count` is how many of them the page the link serves now does not carry — relative to the currently published watermark, 0 when `through_id` is that watermark, all of them before the first share — never above `memory_count`. `current_memory_count` is how many distinct entries the page the link serves now carries (0 before the first share), counted on that page's own window: once a conversation outgrows the page, the current page and the page the range would publish no longer start at the same turn, so an entry cited only on a turn the update pushes off the page is still public — `memory_count - new_memory_count` would miss it (while both pages start at the same turn the two are equal). The read runs every check the share runs and writes nothing: the creator gate (missing or not the creator: 404; creatorless: 409), the 409 refusals for a boundary that no longer resolves or sorts before the published watermark and for a conversation without answers, and the refusal of a range quoting a mounted library that is no longer an effective participant for the creator (404 "部分笔记本已无法访问，请重新选择范围。": such a link would 404 on its first open, so it is not issued — the global share refuses a lost library the same way). `POST .../share` counts again over the exact range and, when `memory_count > 0` and `acknowledged_memory_count != memory_count` (an absent value included), answers 409 `{"detail": {"code": "share_disclosure_required", "memory_count": N, "new_memory_count": M, "current_memory_count": C}}` with no token issued and the watermark unchanged; otherwise it publishes pinned to the boundary it counted, so an answer finishing in between is never published uncounted. An absent `acknowledged_memory_count` is never a 422. A conversation without personal memory publishes exactly as before. Only the creator reaches these endpoints, so a conversation has no non-author refusal (a report does: see above).

**Personal-memory disclosure (share dialog).** Before publishing or updating a conversation share link, the share dialog asks the server how many distinct personal memories of the author the public page will include (`GET …/share/disclosure?through_id=`; the browser never counts memories itself) and shows "The public page will include N excerpts from your personal memories." (after an update: "After the update the public page has N excerpts … (M new)."). Next to the link, N is what the link carries now — the server's `current_memory_count` when an update is on offer, never the update's total minus its new ones. When N > 0 the publish request carries `acknowledged_memory_count: N` next to `expected_through_id`; when N is 0, or the count could not be fetched, it does not (the body stays `{"expected_through_id": …}`). If the server's exact range differs it answers 409 `share_disclosure_required` with the exact counts, where `new_memory_count` is relative to the currently published watermark; the dialog replaces the disclosure line with those numbers and the button reads "Publish anyway" (确认公开) until the author confirms again. After a confirmed publish the disclosure line shows the confirmed number. A 403 shows the server's sentence next to the button. The result is shown on the publish button itself ("生成链接中…" while in flight, then "已公开" for 1.6 s); copying the link stays a manual action. Public pages (`/c/{token}`, `/r/{token}`) keep a memory citation's title and excerpt and label its location "作者的个人记忆" when the reference carries the structured flag `is_memory: true`.

**Mounted libraries are re-checked on every open.** Besides the creator's read access, every open of a notebook conversation's page (and of its images) re-checks, as the creator, each mounted library the published turns quote — named by the `notebook_id` on their anchors and citations: if one is no longer an effective participant of the conversation's notebook — it was unmounted, or the mount stopped being effective — the page answers the same 404 as an unknown token, as the global branch does when it loses a library, and restoring the mount revives the same link. A page quoting no other library does not read the mounts.

Every bound below applies **identically to a shared global (cross-library) conversation**: the two features share one projection module, one anonymous endpoint pair, and therefore one set of constants — see [Global conversation sharing](#global-conversation-sharing) for the two things that do differ (the watermark boundary is a job, and the live re-check covers a set of libraries).

| Bound | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| `ASSET_ALIAS_HEX_CHARS` (per-asset alias length: hex chars of the truncated HMAC-SHA256) | 32 |
| `MAX_REFERENCED_ASSETS` (distinct assets the asset endpoint scans per request; must stay ≥ `MAX_TURNS × CITATION_IMAGES_PER_ANSWER` — enforced by `test_endpoint_scan_cap_covers_every_alias_the_projection_can_emit`, since a later-turn image's alias would otherwise never resolve) | 6,000 |
| `MAX_TURNS` (turns rendered on one public page — the newest of the published prefix; older turns are disclosed as `omitted_earlier_turns` / `truncated_turns`) | 500 |
| `MAX_REFERENCES` (citations per turn) | 500 |
| `MAX_REFERENCE_TITLE_CHARS` (per-reference title / original file name) | 400 |
| `MAX_SNIPPET_CHARS` (per-citation excerpt) | 1,200 |
| `MAX_CAPTION_CHARS` (per-image caption) | 500 |
| `ASK_QUESTION_MAX_CHARS` (question at **submission**, `backend/app/models/ask.py`; over-limit is refused with 422 and never stored clipped) | 4,000 |
| `CONVERSATION_TITLE_MAX_CHARS` (title at **rename**, `backend/app/models/ask.py`; over-limit is refused with 422 and never stored clipped) | 200 |

Questions and conversation titles are served whole. Reference metadata remains bounded and discloses `title_truncated`/`snippet_truncated`/`file_name_truncated`.

The question rail applies to `POST /notebooks/{id}/ask`, `/ask/stream`, `/ask/intent` and `/ask/intent/stream` (422), and to MCP `ask` (readable “question too long” error). `PATCH /conversations/{id}` enforces the rename rail with 422; automatic titles use the first 60 question characters and MCP has no rename tool. Both browser rails (`ASK_INPUT_LIMITS`) count Unicode code points, reject submission and never clip entered text.

Historical questions/titles written before these rails can still exceed them and remain unbounded in public projection; closing that gap requires explicit disclosure, not silent clipping. Projection constants live in `services/conversation_public_view.py`; write limits live in `models/ask.py`.

## In-app user manual

`/manual` renders the repository's [user manual](./user-manual_zh.md) (Chinese) as an in-app page;
the account menu's 「使用手册」 entry points to it. Like the public share pages it sits outside the
login gate. The Next.js route reads `docs/user-manual_zh.md` at **build time** and prerenders a
static page — the offline bundle ships only the `.next` output, not `docs/`, so a manual change
takes effect after the frontend is rebuilt. Heading anchors follow GitHub's slug rules so the
hand-written table of contents works both on the repository and in the app; relative links to
other repository Markdown documents render as plain text instead of dead links.

## System update notice

After an upgrade, each signed-in user sees the headline release notes they have not seen yet, in a one-time **系统已更新** dialog. A change users need to know about carries a `release-notes/<slug>.md` file whose front matter declares `level` (`change`, `feature`, `fix` or `internal`), `audience` (`all` or `admin`) and a one-line Chinese `title`, followed by an optional short body; the file name is the note's id, so renaming a file makes it a new note. `scripts/build_release_manifest.py` (run by `scripts/pack.sh` for offline bundles and by `npm run start` on a git checkout) writes `release-manifest.json` (`schema` 2) at the package or repo root: the build's version and ordinal plus every note with its level, audience, title and body. A note whose front matter is missing or invalid fails the manifest build. A backend guard over the real `release-notes/` directory caps the title at 30 and the body at 160 Unicode code points; the manifest build itself does not check lengths, so an overlong note never costs a deployment its notices.

A note is visible to a user when its audience is `all`, or `admin` and the user is a system administrator. The dialog lists only the pending visible notes of level `change` and `feature`, newest first (ties by id), at most five, each showing its title with the body expanded on demand. Pending `fix` notes and headline notes beyond the fifth are counted into `more_count` and summarised as 「另有 N 项修复与改进」 with a link to the **更新记录** page (`/updates`, also in the account menu); `internal` notes are not counted. When no headline note is pending the dialog does not open and the baseline does not move, so those fixes are counted the next time a headline note arrives. The update-history page lists every visible note up to the running build, newest first, and hides `internal` notes until the reader ticks 「显示后台改进」.

Versions are compared by a **mainline ordinal**, not by a global "previous release": the ordinal is `git rev-list --count --first-parent` of a commit, and a note's ordinal is the first-parent commit that added its file. Master lands by rebase, so the ordinal only ever grows. Each user stores one integer, `users.seen_release_ordinal` (SQLite v86 / PostgreSQL 0066; `NULL` = never recorded, no backfill), and the pending notes are exactly those with `seen < note.ordinal <= build.ordinal`. So the baseline is **per user** — the last version that user was shown — and a user who skipped several releases is shown the headline notes of all of them at once, by the rule below.

- **New users are silent.** The first `GET` for a user whose baseline is `NULL` writes the running build's ordinal (a conditional write that only fires while still `NULL`) and returns no notes: a new account, or an existing one when this feature first ships, is not shown history it never missed.
- **Rollback is quiet.** If the running build's ordinal is below the stored baseline, nothing is pending. Marking as seen only ever raises the baseline (`max`), so upgrading again after a rollback does not repeat a notice the user already saw.
- **`through_ordinal` prevents over-marking.** The client sends the `build.ordinal` it was shown; the server stores `max(current, min(through_ordinal, build.ordinal))`. A server upgrade that lands while the dialog is open therefore does not get marked as seen by the click that closes it.
- **A missing or invalid manifest disables the feature.** Both endpoints then behave as "unavailable": `GET` returns `available=false` and the database is never written. An invalid manifest (a `schema` other than 2, bad field types or enum values, an empty title, duplicate ids) logs only a reason code, never a note body. The parsed file is cached per path and re-read whenever its inode, mtime or size changes.

## Wish wall and global question analysis

The authenticated global **Wish Wall** at `/wishes` is independent of notebooks. Any user may publish a `bug` or `feature` item; only an administrator may publish a `plan`. Titles are trimmed, required, and limited to 120 characters; details are trimmed, required, and limited to 4,000 characters. A user has at most one vote on each bug or feature, and pressing the same vote control again removes that vote. Plans do not accept votes. Every item carries an administrator-owned `status`: `open` (the birth value), `in_progress`, `done`, or `declined`. Only an administrator may change it, via `PUT /api/wishes/{wish_id}/status`; anyone else receives 403. The author of an item, or any administrator, may edit its kind/title/content with `PATCH /api/wishes/{wish_id}` (partial body, unknown fields rejected, at least one field required, the same trim/length rules as creation, and the plan-is-admin-only rule applies to a kind change) and delete it with `DELETE /api/wishes/{wish_id}` (204; the item's votes go with it). Other users receive 403 on both; a missing item is 404. The default `priority` order places plans first, then open/in-progress work above done/declined work, then bugs/features by vote count descending, and finally uses newest-first/id as a stable tie break; `latest` orders by publication time only and ignores status. Lists are offset-paginated with a default page size of 50 and a maximum page size of 100, filterable by `kind` and by `status`. The full HTTP surface is `GET /api/wishes`, `POST /api/wishes`, `PATCH /api/wishes/{wish_id}`, `DELETE /api/wishes/{wish_id}`, `PUT /api/wishes/{wish_id}/status`, and `POST /api/wishes/{wish_id}/vote`.

On the page, a card shows its edit and delete controls only to its author and to administrators; delete asks for a second confirmation inside the card, and edit opens an inline form in place of the title and body with the same validation as the composer. Administrators additionally see a status select on every card. Each action reports its outcome beside the control it was taken from: a saved edit rewrites the card from the server response, a deleted card disappears and the total count follows, and a card that no longer matches the active kind/status filter after such a change leaves the list. A status or kind change under `priority` order first re-sorts the visible window locally by the same rule (done/declined sink) and then reloads the same-sized window from the server to adopt its order and realign the load-more cursor, the same way a vote does; an item that sank out of the window stays at the end while the cursor counts only server rows, so paging continues without skipping the row that moved in. Load-more is disabled (labelled as refreshing the order) until that realignment finishes, because the old cursor would skip the row that moved in; an edit or delete that lands while a realignment (including a vote's window refresh) is still pending restarts it rather than dropping it. Edit, status change and vote on the same card are serialized: while one is in flight the other controls on that card are disabled, so a whole-item response cannot overwrite newer content or newer vote state. Realignment is tracked per request generation, so a superseded request that never returns cannot keep load-more disabled once its replacement has finished; changing a filter replaces the whole window and clears that bookkeeping, while the refresh that follows publishing a new item is itself tracked as a pending window replacement (load-more stays disabled during it) and is restarted, under any sort, if an edit or delete lands while it is in flight, so the new item cannot silently go missing. Only one status change is in flight at a time, so every status select is disabled while one is pending rather than accepting a choice it would silently ignore. If a realignment (a vote's window refresh or the post-publish refresh included) fails, the old cursor is not reused: load-more turns into a retry of the realignment, and only after that succeeds does it page again; the next edit or delete also restarts the realignment. A mutation whose card is no longer in the window when it lands (the user switched filters meanwhile) reloads the window under the current filters, so an item that now matches the newly selected filter appears instead of leaving a stale empty list. Only one deletion is in flight at a time, so every delete control is disabled while one is pending, the same way status changes are. Every successful edit, delete or status change also invalidates list reads still in flight (load-more, a vote's window refresh), so a late response cannot resurrect a deleted card or overwrite the new content; if a filter or sort change already put the page into its loading state, the change restarts that load under the current filters instead of cancelling it. Items whose status is not `open` show a status badge; done/declined cards are rendered muted. The toolbar offers a status filter next to the sort control.

While an Ask response is being generated, or a Deep Report is in `pending`, `running`, `planning`, or `generating`, the waiting surface mounts the same compact wish carousel. It fetches at most `WAITING_WISH_KIND_LIMIT = 5` priority-ordered bugs and the same number of features separately so non-votable plans cannot fill the window, keeps only `open` and `in_progress` wishes, then merges them by vote count, creation time, and id. Done and declined wishes stay on the Wish Wall but never rotate; the filter runs client-side without extra requests (the server's priority order already places closed wishes after open and in-progress ones), and an all-closed result shows the “no pending or in-progress wishes” empty state. It advances every `WAITING_WISH_ROTATION_MS = 8,000` milliseconds, pauses on pointer hover, keyboard focus, an in-flight vote, or the reduced-motion preference, and also provides previous/next controls. A card projects the kind and full title only; “view full details” opens the Wish Wall, so the detail body is not silently clipped. Users may agree or remove agreement in place; the control is disabled in flight and its success or failure is shown beside it. A carousel load failure never blocks the Ask or report job itself.

Administrators have a global **Question Analysis** page at `/admin/questions`. It combines user-authored questions from ordinary Ask jobs and Deep Reports, rather than requiring the administrator to drill into one user at a time. The valid original question is persisted and returned without an additional analysis-view truncation; for legacy completed Ask jobs, the full question recorded with the answer takes precedence over the older abbreviated job text. Unexpired question projections retained after notebook deletion remain visible for the configured user-activity retention period; expired projections and retained rows whose notebook is live are excluded. **Global Ask** jobs aggregate here too: each is a `type="ask"` row with `scope="global"`, belongs to no notebook (`notebook_id`/`notebook_name` are empty), and the notebook column shows the fixed 「全局问答」 (Global Ask). Each row also carries `submitted_via`, the entry point that submitted it: `web` for the session-authenticated browser/HTTP surfaces (`POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask`, `/ask/stream`, `/reports`; a global job's web surface is `POST /api/global-ask/ask`), `mcp` for the MCP tool (`ask` for both a notebook job and a global one), and the empty string for "not recorded" — every row created before this field existed, plus in-process callers that pass no entry point. The value is set only by the server entry point, never by a request field, and is not inferred for historical rows; the page shows it as 「网页」/「MCP」/「未记录」 in a 调用方式 column, and notebook-deletion retention keeps it. Each ask row also carries `output` (`answer` by default, `evidence` for an `ask(output="evidence")` call); the page shows 「仅检索」 beside the source for the latter, and retention keeps it. It supports source type (`ask` or `report`), a **scope** filter (`scope=notebook|global`, i.e. 笔记本内/全局; omitted shows both), submission surface (`submitted_via=web|mcp`), user, and question-text filters; returns newest-first rows with the user, notebook, status, and creation time; and reports counts for total questions, Ask questions, Deep Reports, **global Ask questions**, and distinct active users under the current filter — the global count is a subset of the Ask count, since a global job is the same kind of question as a notebook one and differs only in retrieval. Two more cards, 「有用」 and 「需改进」, count the 👍/👎 the filtered questions received (`stats.feedback_useful` / `feedback_not_useful`): a notebook question by its answer's `feedback` rows, a global job by its rating (first write wins; one global job counts once, never split across its libraries); each card notes 「其中全局问答 N 条」 underneath (`stats.global_feedback_useful` / `global_feedback_not_useful`, hidden at 0). Deep Reports carry no rating; a retention projection of a deleted notebook still counts as a question but carries no rating — the notebook's `feedback` rows are deleted with it and the projection keeps no rating — so it adds 0. Rows show no rating and there is no rating filter. The search rail is `ADMIN_QUESTIONS_QUERY_MAX_CHARS = 200` Unicode code points. Offset pagination defaults to `ADMIN_QUESTIONS_DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50` rows and accepts at most `ADMIN_QUESTIONS_MAX_LIMIT = 200` rows per request. The page pages through results with the shared pagination control (row range and total, previous/next, page count, jump to page; hidden when everything fits on one page), keeps the current table visible and marked busy while the next page loads, and when a page comes back empty because questions were removed while it was open, falls back to the new last page instead of showing an empty page. The HTTP surface is `GET /api/admin/questions`; it is administrator-only and follows the existing `USER_ACTIVITY_VIEW_ENABLED` observability gate. When that gate is off, the account-menu entry is hidden and direct navigation explains that the deployment has not enabled the capability. This first version is a searchable aggregate for human analysis and does not send question content to an additional model.

## APIs

Key local beta APIs:

- `GET /api/notebooks`, `POST /api/notebooks`, `PATCH /api/notebooks/{id}`, `DELETE /api/notebooks/{id}`, `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/cancel-delete`, `GET /api/me/notebook-deletions` — the delete endpoint returns **202** with `{"status":"pending_delete","delete_after":"…"}`: it commits a single-row status change into the one-day deletion window (`notebooks.status='pending_delete'`; see [Deleting a whole notebook: the one-day window](#deleting-a-whole-notebook-the-one-day-window) for the window, the owner's cancel and the notices) and returns immediately; the notebook is excluded from every list/read/search/mount surface from that instant on (`GET /api/notebooks/{id}` 404s immediately, with an explanation code for its readers), and once `delete_after` passes the delete sweep promotes it to `notebooks.status='deleting'` and the background delete below runs. Its **owner** gets **409** from a repeat `DELETE` on the same notebook (`notebook_pending_delete` inside the window) (codex #659 R6 P2: the delete endpoint's guard is owner-scoped and deliberately does not apply the same live-only visibility filter every other write endpoint does, precisely so a retried/duplicate delete request reaches this 409 instead of a misleading 404) — a **non-owner** still gets 404 either way (existence is never leaked to a caller without access). The actual database and disk cleanup runs afterward as a background job (materializing source file paths, waiting out any knowledge-graph rebuild already running against that notebook, then one atomic finalize step that archives the deleted content into the user's retained-activity history and removes the row). The browser already treated a successful delete as fire-and-forget (it tombstones the card client-side and refreshes the list), so this is a behavior change only for direct API callers that previously relied on 204 meaning "fully deleted" — poll `GET /api/notebooks/{id}` (404) to confirm invisibility, or (administrators only) `GET /api/admin/users/{user_id}/activity` for confirmation the retained-activity archive has landed. The archived `deleted_at` timestamp is the finalize step's moment, which can trail the delete request by anywhere from under a second to tens of minutes on a large notebook. A full KG **rebuild**'s own delete phase (a different path from notebook deletion) likewise drains the old graph in bounded pages before its single atomic reset; the page/threshold row budget is `KG_GRAPH_DRAIN_PAGE_ROWS` (default 2000, allowed 50–20000 — the ceiling stays under SQLite's default SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER because drain pages bind selected ids as SQL parameters).
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/analytics` — the knowledge analytics panel (any reader of the notebook). `feedback_useful` / `feedback_not_useful` and `usefulness_rate` include the **global Ask ratings attributed to this notebook**: a global rating counts once in every library its run searched or cited (when it did neither, in its participants minus the skipped ones — the same rule as the post-Ask learning chain, `global_ask_attribution`); `feedback_useful_global` / `feedback_not_useful_global` are that global subset, which the panel notes after 👍/👎 as 「（其中全局问答 N 条）」. `low_rated_questions` (「低分提问（知识缺口）」) lists notebook questions only — a global question's text never appears there — and ends with 「另有 N 条来自全局问答」. The response carries counts only, never another participant's id or name. `answers_total` (the panel's 「提问」) likewise includes the **global Ask answers attributed to this notebook**: the notebook's own answers plus every finished (`done`) global Ask job attributed to it that is not past its retention stamp, one count in every library a job is attributed to; `answers_global` is that global subset, noted on the panel as 「（其中全局问答 N 条）」 (hidden when 0). The global part is an index count over `global_ask_job_notebooks`; jobs not yet backfilled after the upgrade are counted through the payload predicate (the same rule, so the number is the same before and after the backfill).
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/analytics/content-overview` — viewer-aware content assets: `memory` (`total`, `confirmed`, `candidate`, up to three recent `id`/`title`/`status`/`updated_at`) and `knowhow` (`table_count`, `row_count`, `projection_pending`, `projection_failed`, `stale_code_count`, up to three recent table summaries)
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/checkup` — read-only pipeline health check (dashboard hot path): aggregates source/index damage-and-pending signals — empty source, missing retrieval segments, missing retrieval vectors, sources pending analysis, stale/corrupt retrieval index — each with a count, a bounded sample, and a repair action (read-only items carry the action `none`: they are shown as a notice without a button because the system handles them). `healthy` is true when every repairable item (action other than `none`) counts zero; read-only items are still listed with their counts but do not count toward `healthy`, and they neither ring the bell nor keep the repair polling alive. Consumed by the dashboard's source-status and index blocks plus the bell; a healthy notebook stays neutral and undisturbed. The two missing-retrieval-vector counts are served from an event-driven per-notebook memo: the app's own vector writes (ingest embedding, "backfill vectors", re-parse) invalidate it on completion, so the next poll reflects the new counts; **cross-process** writes (an operator running the offline CLI backfill/import on the server) and a few rare background-failure paths are invisible to these events and fall back to the backstop cache — counts may be **up to 300 seconds stale** in those scenarios.
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/sources/reparse` — checkup repair: batch re-parse the given sources (empty/missing-segment damage), scheduled through the existing pipeline in the background, filtered to the notebook scope.
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/backfill-vectors` — checkup repair: backfill the notebook's missing retrieval vectors in the background (missing-only, idempotent, embedding-only — never re-parses and never rewrites the knowledge graph). Document chunks are embedded with the chunk embedding model and Knowhow table chunks with the Knowhow embedding model, in batches. A gap is counted only where a vector can be made: a blank chunk is never missing, and a Knowhow hidden source whose table is gone is not counted. The request is accepted only when the embedding model for the gap is configured; otherwise it answers `accepted: false` as it does for a healthy notebook. It shares one per-notebook run with the background re-embed job, so a request while a run is in flight joins it rather than starting a second one.
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/paper-meta/backfill` — owner-triggered paper-metadata backfill (background, idempotent/resumable), returns `{queued}`; 409 when the LLM is not configured. The source panel's 「补全论文信息」 button is **shown only when there is work to do**: it hides when `NotebookSummary.paper_meta_missing` (filled precisely only by the single-notebook `GET /api/notebooks/{id}`, an EXISTS probe over the same predicate the backfill queue uses; `null` = not computed on list projections and older backends) is `false` **and** the visible source page has no `paper_meta_status="missing"` row. `null`/absent keeps the legacy always-visible behavior — hiding is triggered only by an explicit `false` — and the button stays visible while a backfill is running to host its 「补全中…」 state.
- `GET /api/system/config` — authenticated, non-sensitive browser configuration; currently returns `source_upload_max_bytes`, the parsed deployment cap used by the source picker; `source_upload_max_files_per_batch`, the fixed request-count guard; and, for the markdown-bundle upload pairing pre-flight (see "Citation images (本段附图)" above), `source_image_max_bytes` / `source_image_max_per_source` (mirroring `MINERU_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` / `MINERU_MAX_IMAGES_PER_SOURCE`; `null` on an older backend that omits them means "skip local pre-flight, the server guardrail decides", while an explicit `0` is a legal value meaning "persist no images at all" and is equivalent to image storage being off) and `source_images_enabled` (mirroring `MINERU_RETURN_IMAGES`; a missing field defaults to `true`, since the switch never previously existed and a stale frontend must not manufacture a warning against a normal deployment), and `notebook_transfer_max_bytes` (the parsed `NOTEBOOK_TRANSFER_WEB_MAX_MB`, the web export/import limit)
- Notebook export and import: `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/export`, `POST /api/notebook-imports`, `GET /api/notebook-imports/uploads/{upload_id}`, `GET /api/notebook-transfers[/{job}]`, `POST /api/notebook-transfers/{job}/download-ticket`, `GET /api/notebook-transfers/download?ticket=`, `DELETE /api/notebook-transfers/{job}` — contracts in [Notebook export and import](#notebook-export-and-import-snbk).
- `GET /api/system/extensions` — authenticated metadata-only projection for build-time workspace UI contributions. It returns API version plus stable plugin/display/version/contribution identifiers, live availability, and only `disabled | unavailable | null` as the unavailable reason. It never returns capability names, dependency/trust topology, endpoints, paths, credentials, or exception text. Production registers the existing Agent Profile launcher as `builtin.ask_agent_profile.workspace_panel` in `workspace.side_panel`. The browser reads this projection once per authenticated actor generation after a workspace commits; collection and signed-out views do not call it, notebook switches reuse it, and unavailable/missing/older servers fail closed. The contribution itself performs no Agent Profile read until the user opens the existing panel.
- `GET /api/me/release-notes` — signed in; returns `{available, build: {version, ordinal} | null, notes: [{id, ordinal, level, audience, title, body}], more_count}`: up to five pending headline notes (`change` or `feature`, newest first, ties by id) visible to this user, and the count of further pending headline and `fix` notes. `available=false` (no usable manifest) writes nothing; a user with no recorded baseline gets one silently and an empty list. See [System update notice](#system-update-notice).
- `GET /api/me/release-notes/history` — signed in; returns `{available, build, notes}` with every note visible to this user whose ordinal is at most the running build's, `internal` included, newest first. Reads and writes no user state.
- `POST /api/me/release-notes/seen` body `{through_ordinal}` — signed in; raises the user's seen baseline to `min(through_ordinal, build.ordinal)`, never lowering it; 204, no write when the manifest is unavailable, 422 for a non-integer or negative value.
- `GET /api/admin/extensions` — system-admin-only, read-only projection of the loaded deployment-plugin topology (six whitelisted fields per extension) plus the current runtime-toggle state per row; see [Deployment extensions](#deployment-extensions).
- `PATCH /api/admin/extensions/{plugin_id}` — system-admin-only, turns an already-loaded deployment plugin's runtime admission on or off without a restart; see [Deployment extensions](#deployment-extensions).
- `/api/extensions/{plugin_id}/…` — the sole mount point for a deployment plugin's own HTTP routes, behind router-level session auth; see [Deployment extensions](#deployment-extensions).
- Workspace UI contributions use the build-time `SILICON_NOTEBOOK_UI_PLUGINS` workflow and deployment contract described in the [extension SOP](./deployment-extensions-sop.md). The injected `actions.api` confines requests to `/api/extensions/{plugin_id}/`, strips supplied authorization/cookie headers and fixes request auth/tag/unauthorized policy. `requestTask()` consumes the shared NDJSON task stream, exposing only elapsed time, fixed stages and safe fallback errors; empty responses use `requestVoid`. Since unauthorized handling clears the browser bearer and reloads, plugin routes reserve 401 for actual session invalidation and translate upstream credential failures to 502/424. The administrator topology page reads the running backend via `GET /api/admin/extensions`, independently of this frontend build input.
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/sources` — multipart file upload (async parse/extract). Each file is bounded while the multipart stream is spooled and is rejected with 413 above `SOURCE_UPLOAD_MAX_MB` (default 50 MiB); each request is also rejected above 20 files. The browser reads both guards above, blocks its file inputs until they are known, rejects oversized selections immediately, and rechecks staged files before sending. Each accepted file lands on disk as `{source_id}_{sanitized client name}`; that component is clamped to the filesystem's 255-byte path-component limit (stem clipped on UTF-8 bytes, extension preserved — a browser may legally submit a 255-byte file name, which composed with the 37-byte id prefix would otherwise exceed the cap on ext4/XFS/NTFS and fail the upload). Only the derived disk name is shortened; the stored file name and title keep the client's value whole
- `GET /api/sources/{id}`, `DELETE /api/sources/{id}`, `POST /api/sources/{id}/parse`, `GET /api/sources/{id}/elements`, `GET /api/sources/{id}/elements-page?offset=&limit=&anchor_element_id=` — owner-or-member scope, keyed on the source's own notebook; a Memory projection source and its elements are readable (the three `GET`s) only by the Memory's creator, anyone else gets the missing-id 404; `DELETE` and `POST .../parse` never address a Memory or Knowhow projection source (the missing-id 404 for every caller, the Memory's creator included — Memory is deleted through the Memory endpoints and re-ingested by the Memory service, Knowhow rows are kept in sync with their table). The paged reader returns `{items,total_count,offset,limit}`, caps `limit` at 100, and moves `offset` to the page containing a valid anchor. The `GET /api/sources/{id}` detail (not the list projection) carries `updated_at`, the row's last write: every status-machine step (`set_status`), element swap and rename moves it. The batch reparse endpoint only hands `process_source` to the KG job pool and does not touch the source's status before returning, so a client following a reparse reads `updated_at` just before submitting and treats a terminal status as the end of that run only once the run was seen to start or `updated_at` moved past that baseline (a rename can also move it; that only ends the follow early).
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/sources/{source_id}/elements-page?offset=&limit=&anchor_element_id=` — the bounded source-detail reader under active-notebook participant authorization. The browser uses this endpoint; the proxied unpaged element endpoint remains backward compatible.
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/sources/{source_id}`, `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/sources/{source_id}/elements` — the same two reads, authorized on the **active** notebook in the path and resolved inside its valid participant set (itself plus the reference libraries it has effectively mounted). Mounting a reference library never grants direct membership in it, so the browser keeps filtering on the active notebook only and the backend proxies the read internally; the participant set is re-evaluated per request, so a demoted/transferred/mid-copy library or an unmounted edge returns 404 immediately. Same-notebook sources take this identical path (the participant set always starts with the active notebook), and the response reports the source's real owning notebook so the client can render it read-only. Writes are deliberately not proxied — re-parse and delete stay direct operations on `/api/sources/{id}` under the `sources:write` capability (owner ∪ group admin since P2). The detail response is a narrower model than `/api/sources/{id}`'s: it drops `file_path` and the raw `error_message` (both can carry server-side absolute paths) and reports a `parse_failed` boolean instead; a cross-library source of a hidden synthetic type (`memory`/`knowhow` projection rows, which the collection map deliberately counts) is refused outright, and in the active notebook itself a Memory projection source opens only for the Memory's creator (Knowhow projection rows stay readable)
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/assets/{asset_id}` — image assets (knowhow cell images, source figures) under the same participant-set rule: the notebook in the path is the viewer's active notebook, the asset declares its own owning notebook, and any asset outside the active notebook's valid participant set is 404. An asset served from a mounted library is `Cache-Control: no-store` so unmounting takes effect immediately; assets of the active notebook itself keep the long private cache
- Command catalog routes and response/error contracts: [Command catalog (tool manuals)](#command-catalog-tool-manuals).
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/understanding` — notebook understanding ("AI 对这个库的理解"); any reader; returns `enabled`, `base`, `mine`, `job`, `can_edit_base` — see [Notebook understanding blocks](#notebook-understanding-blocks)
- `PUT /api/notebooks/{id}/understanding/{label}` body `{scope: "shared"|"mine", value, expected_revision}` — `shared` needs the `agent_profile:write` capability, `mine` needs only read access plus row-level ownership; 422 over the 400-character limit, 409 on a stale `expected_revision`
- `DELETE /api/notebooks/{id}/understanding/{label}?scope=&expected_revision=` — same capability split as the write endpoint and the same optimistic concurrency: `expected_revision` is the revision the browser displayed (required; stale → 409); clears the value, keeps the row and history
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/understanding/rebuild` body `{scope}` — same capability split; 409 while busy or while `AGENT_PROFILE_ENABLED` is off
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/understanding/experiences` — this notebook's own slice of the retrieval strategy experience library; any reader; returns `enabled` (follows `RETRIEVAL_EXPERIENCE_ENABLED`), `count`, `updated_at`, `can_manage`, `entries` — see [Retrieval strategy experience](#retrieval-strategy-experience)
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/understanding/experiences/distill` — requires `agent_profile:write` (404 without it); manually schedules one consolidation. 409 with three distinct sentences: the single-flight slot is taken, `RETRIEVAL_EXPERIENCE_ENABLED` is off, or the cooldown holds (last batch under 10 minutes ago with no new asks since)
- `DELETE /api/notebooks/{id}/understanding/experiences` — same capability split; clears this notebook's slice and returns `{removed}`; 409 deleting nothing while a batch for that slice is running or queued; still allowed while the gate is off
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/knowledge-types`, `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/knowledge?type=concept|claim|formula|procedure|...`, `PATCH /api/notebooks/{id}/knowledge/{knowledge_id}` (read access; a read-only member only moves her own Memory object between approved and deprecated, see "Memory in the knowledge graph")
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/graph`
- Knowhow tables: `GET|POST /api/notebooks/{id}/knowhow`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE .../knowhow/{table_id}`, `POST .../knowhow/{table_id}/reproject` — plus import (`POST .../knowhow/import/preview`, `POST .../knowhow/import`), column/row/cell editing (`POST .../knowhow/{table_id}/columns`, `PATCH|DELETE .../columns/{column_id}`, `POST .../knowhow/{table_id}/rows`, `DELETE .../rows/{row_id}`, `PATCH .../rows/{row_id}/cells/{column_id}`), the Excel template round-trip (`GET .../knowhow/{table_id}/template`, `POST .../knowhow/{table_id}/append` with `mode=preview|commit`), an explicit suggestion-only wording rewrite (`POST .../rows/{row_id}/cells/{column_id}/optimize`), reasoning-backed row completion suggestions (`POST .../knowhow/{table_id}/rows/{row_id}/complete`, optional `target_column_ids`, response `retrieval_mode` + `retrieval_scope` + `retrieval_status` + `reasoning_trace` + `evidence` + `suggestions`), and deterministic/LLM-assisted cell reformat (`POST .../rows/{row_id}/cells/{column_id}/reformat`). The official browser uses the corresponding `optimize/stream`, `complete/stream`, and `reformat/stream` variants; the JSON routes remain compatible.
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/search?q=`
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask/intent/stream` — official browser's heartbeat-capable, corpus-blind `reasoning` intent preview; accepts `{question, conversation_id?}`, reads at most the latest five user questions, creates no conversation/job, returns the editable intent contract in `final`, and signals the model cancellation event when its client disconnects. `POST .../ask/intent` remains the JSON compatibility endpoint.
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask` — grounded Q&A with `[k_i]` citations (`mode`: `chunk` default | `reasoning`; `auto` is a retired alias that maps to `reasoning` (the same mechanism as `fast`/`global`/`graph` mapping to `chunk`, kept for not-yet-refreshed tabs/bookmarks; it is never a displayed engine); `reasoning` accepts `retrieval_effort`, default `standard`; the official browser sends timezone-aware `asked_at` as display-only submission metadata; responses expose the authoritative persisted completion instant as `answered_at`; collection-aware responses may include structured `result_sets` plus exact coverage; a reasoning response may additionally carry `gap_suggestions` — non-evidence pointers outside the notebook, see [Gap consultation](#gap-consultation-askgap_consult) — empty and absent from the JSON payload on a deployment with no such plugin; a reasoning response's `citations`/`anchors` may likewise carry a `tier="external"` row with a non-empty `url`, see [Reflect plugin actions](#reflect-plugin-actions-askreflect_action) — absent for every row on a deployment with no such plugin; federation follows the mode-specific boundaries above)
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask/stream` — NDJSON Ask progress stream (same optional timezone-aware `asked_at` request field; first a `started` event with the durable `job_id` and `conversation_id`, then progress/final events). The frontend uses that conversation id to publish/reopen the in-flight session before an answer exists. `mode` is already resolved to a concrete registry id by the time the job is created, so `ask_jobs.mode` holds that id throughout — there is no delayed-selection window — and the synthetic start step is emitted right after `started`. Leaving the workspace before `started` and returning to the same notebook still re-attaches the question from the frontend's local in-flight record on the same stream. The reasoning-mode intent understanding and clarification review that precede submission are likewise not aborted by leaving: understanding continues while away, a clear intent starts the Ask job directly, and a requested clarification re-opens when the notebook is reopened. Both phases are also kept in the browser's per-tab session storage: after a full reload of the same tab, returning to that notebook re-issues the understanding or re-opens the clarification card; closing the tab discards them. The request also accepts an optional `client_request_id` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, `-`; at most 128 characters), one key per submission, which the official browser sends on every submit; a repeat POST with the same key by the same user does not create a second job — the stream re-emits `started` with the existing job and conversation ids, replays the persisted progress steps, and ends with the saved answer as `final` (or the job's `cancelled`/`error`). That is how a reload landing between the reasoning preflight's hand-off and `started` is resumed automatically: the tab re-sends the same submission under the same key and attaches, instead of handing the question back as a draft. The attach is decided before the route's own preflight (availability, scope, mode registry) — only notebook authorization stands in front of it — so a retry replays the job even if a fresh ask would now be refused. A key the same user already spent in another notebook ends the stream with an `error` event and creates nothing. The synchronous `POST …/ask` accepts the field but does not persist or honour it: it always creates. A transport disconnect stops delivery to that client only; the detached job keeps running and can persist its answer
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/ask/jobs/{job_id}` — read detached Ask job `status`, `trace`, and `answer_id`; the job must belong to the path notebook and current user; on `done`, the frontend reloads the conversation to obtain the final `AskResponse`
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask/jobs/{job_id}/cancel` — explicit interrupt endpoint; the job must belong to the path notebook and current user; sets the cancellation event and stops the worker before a cancelled final answer is saved
- `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/ask/report-check` — the attached report's pre-send check (read-only, no job); request and response shapes and error codes in [Follow-up questions on a deep report](#follow-up-questions-on-a-deep-report). `/ask`, `/ask/stream`, `/ask/intent` and `/ask/intent/stream` all take an optional `report_id`, gated as described there
- `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/conversations`, `GET|PATCH|DELETE /api/conversations/{id}` — the list's summaries and the detail carry `submitted_via` (`web` / `mcp` / empty = not recorded; read from the conversation's earliest job, empty when an answer predates that job), and each turn of the detail carries its own `submitted_via` (the origin of the job that produced that answer); the browser does not read it, and it is what MCP `list_conversations` / `get_conversation` report. When the conversation's last turn attached a deep report, the list's summaries and the detail also carry `linked_report: {report_id, title}`; a question still running in the detail carries `active_job.linked_report`; each answer carries its receipt `linked_report` (see [Follow-up questions on a deep report](#follow-up-questions-on-a-deep-report))
- `POST /api/answers/{answer_id}/feedback`
- Memory: `GET /api/memories`, `GET /api/notebooks/{id}/memories`, `GET|PATCH /api/memories/{memory_id}`, `POST /api/memories/{memory_id}/confirm|reject|deprecate|promote`, `POST /api/answers/{answer_id}/memory-preview/stream` (browser; `/memory-preview` remains JSON-compatible), `POST /api/notebooks/{id}/memories/from-answer`
  - Endpoints that take an answer id (`POST /api/answers/{answer_id}/memory-preview`, `.../memory-preview/stream`, `POST /api/answers/{answer_id}/feedback`, and `POST /api/notebooks/{notebook_id}/memories/from-answer`) act only on the caller's own answers: the caller must be able to read the notebook AND must have created the answer's conversation. Another member's answer (the notebook owner included), an answer without a conversation, and an unknown id all return the same 404 `Answer not found`. `answer_owner` in the sharing store returns the notebook owner and is not used for authorisation.
  - A deployment admin reading a user's answers through the admin user activity log is audit access; it is a separate, admin-only read and is not subject to the answer-owner rule.
- Agent access: anonymous machine-readable onboarding at `GET /api/agent-mcp/onboarding`; authenticated `GET|POST /api/agent-profiles`, `PATCH /api/agent-profiles/{profile_id}`, `POST /api/agent-profiles/{profile_id}/tokens`, `GET /api/agent-tokens`, `GET /api/agent-tokens/{token_id}/secret` (copy the plaintext again, owner only), `PUT /api/agent-tokens/{token_id}/access`, `DELETE /api/agent-tokens/{token_id}`; Streamable HTTP MCP is mounted at `/mcp`
- Knowhow agent surface: `GET /api/agent/knowhow/tables?notebook_id=`, `GET /api/agent/knowhow/tables/{table_id}/discrimination`, `GET /api/agent/knowhow/rows/{row_id}`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /api/agent/knowhow/rows/{row_id}/cells/{column_id}/code` — reachable by either a signed-in session or an Agent Bearer token; reads need the `read` tier, code writes need the `contribute` tier (see [Memory and Agent MCP](#memory-and-agent-mcp))
- Unified KG: `POST .../unified-kg/rebuild`, `GET .../unified-kg`, `GET .../unified-kg/pending-merges`, `POST .../unified-kg/merges/{id}/confirm|reject`
  - `GET .../unified-kg/pending-merges` returns every pending candidate as `{id, canonical_a, canonical_b, score, status, name_a, name_b, kind}`. `kind` is `spelling_variant` when the two sides' decision keys (seeds, or canonical ids without `K-`) are equal once their spaces go — the names differ only in spaces, hyphens, underscores, dots or brackets; the 「待确认合并」 row shows 「同名不同写法」 — else `similarity`; the keys themselves are not in the response. `name_a` / `name_b` are the display names of the two merged knowledge objects: the published concept cluster's stored name, read by one bounded point lookup per distinct id of the response (at most 900 ids per statement; none for an empty list). The names follow the cluster label rule of the KG detail reads below: when the notebook holds a hidden source the viewer may not read, a cluster that may hold a hidden member is named by its first visible member (member-id order). A cluster with no visible live member does not exist for that viewer (as in the detail reads), so a row naming one is left out of that viewer's list — its canonical id carries a hidden member's seed; every other row goes to every reader. `""` when no published cluster row carries the id (a bridge candidate whose cluster was never formed). `canonical_a` / `canonical_b` are the row's handles, not display text: the 「待确认合并」 list shows the names and 「未命名概念」 for an empty name, never the id. Cost of the label rule: deciding whether anything is hidden takes the same one or two reads bounded by the notebook's Memory and Knowhow count as the KG detail reads; when the notebook holds Memory the viewer may not read, each load of the list adds one statement for the live objects owned by those Memory sources, one `cluster_fold_rows` statement per 900 such objects, and, only when a returned cluster may hold a hidden member, one batched read of those clusters' first members — the same rule and cost as concept detail.
  - **Concept merge seeds (`CLUSTER_ALGO_VERSION` 4; design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-19-kg-analysis-findings-design_zh.md` §五 S1).** A concept name first loses the whitespace, hyphens and underscores of its **original** text, then the other punctuation becomes spaces: "Q-Former", "Qformer" and "Q Former" share one seed, while "Llama 3.1" and "Llama 31" stay two seeds (a difference made by dots or brackets is left to a human). The acronym alias table still matches words, its values are squashed the same way; claim / formula / procedure seeds are unchanged. Every library records the seed space of its **published** merge in `unified_kg_state.concept_seed_version`, written by the same statement that publishes a full merge: 1 for every library that existed at the upgrade, the current space (2) for a library created since and after a knowledge-graph delete or an indexing-pipeline publication (nothing is published then); a notebook without a state row reads as the current space, and a deep copy carries the space of the clusters it copies (a copy of a library not yet re-merged since the upgrade keeps 1; a dirty source's copy carries no clusters). The upgrade gives a notebook that holds concept clusters but no state row (a copy made before it) a clean state row in space 1, and `scripts/merge_dbs.py` gives an imported library that keeps concept clusters one carrying its source's published space. Incremental fusion, catch-up, bridge candidates, duplicate grouping and the dedup of contributions to a public library all follow the published space, so until a library's next full merge after the upgrade new content keeps joining the old merged knowledge objects; a placement whose space changed under it (that full merge published in between) is placed again in the new space, never written into the new merge with the old seeds. A library's first full merge under the new rule recomputes its stored merge decisions (`concept_merge_candidates.seed_version` 1; a row without seeds is keyed by its canonical ids without `K-`) from the **current objects' names**: a confirmed decision joins every pair of the two sides' new seeds, a rejected or deferred one makes every pair a cannot-link; when a rejection or deferral would put both sides on one new seed, the objects involved keep the old seed as `~v1:<old seed>` (recorded in the decision row, applied by every later merge and incremental placement), and the decisions already stored under the new rule that name the seeds those objects leave follow them onto `~v1:<old seed>` (a confirmation that then joins the two sides of the rejection wins, as everywhere); a decision a side of which no current object carries stays as it is and is retried by the next full merge. One seed pair holds one decision: when several name it (a recomputed rejection landing on a confirmed pair, or contradicting rows already stored), the strongest holds, confirmed, then rejected, then deferred, in every reader whatever the row order, and the merge that writes such a pair removes the weaker rows. The recompute lands in the pending-merge refresh's transaction and emits `kg_merge_decisions_recomputed` (translated, suspended, keys kept on the old seed, new-rule decisions moved, rows superseded); the decision rows it adds are counted into the merge input version, so the next "update analysis" does not re-merge again. Almost every multi-word concept's merged knowledge object id changes once in that merge; concept descriptions are reused by signature, not rewritten for the new ids.
  - **"Same name, different spelling" candidates.** The pending-merge refresh has one more tier: merged knowledge objects whose seeds differ only in the spaces punctuation made (equal once the spaces go; seeds starting with `~` never count) get one pair each with the member-richest object of their group, scored by the cosine of the two representative vectors (0 without vectors), deduplicated with the similarity candidates by pair (one row, the higher score), and never re-proposed once rejected or deferred. At most `KG_MERGE_SQUASH_CANDIDATES_MAX` pairs per full merge (default 1000); pairs already rejected or deferred are left out before the cap, so they never take a place a group still to review needs; hitting the cap keeps the member-richest groups and emits `kg_merge_squash_candidates_capped`.
- **KG maintenance:** the three actions below require `kg:write` and have no LLM-configuration prerequisite. They start background jobs; starts return `{status, notebook_id, job_id}`, not result counts. Their notebook-read status endpoints return `{job_id, notebook_id, status, running, ...counters}`, with `status=running|succeeded|failed|idle`.

  | UI action | POST path under `/api/notebooks/{id}` | Start status | GET status path | Counters |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 重新合并 | `/unified-kg/rebuild` | `rebuilding` | `/unified-kg/rebuild/status` | `clusters` |
  | 补上关联 | `/kg/relink` | `relinking` | `/kg/relink/status` | `isolated_before, edges_added, isolated_after` |
  | 删除知识图谱 | `/kg/delete` | `deleting` | `/kg/delete/status` | `objects_deleted, relations_deleted` (zero until success) |

  All share one per-notebook maintenance slot and reject a competing click with 409 naming its holder. The slot also cross-excludes extraction (`buildkg-`/`rebuildkg-`, including MCP `build(target="kg")`) in both directions; the indexing-pipeline switch retains its saved intent and returns its retryable 409. Direct in-process script KG deletion is refused while maintenance runs. Claims/status are per serving process (production uses `--workers 1`); offline CLI processes are not covered. `idle` means never run here, process restarted, or another maintenance kind holds the slot. Polling is bounded, notebook-specific busy state cannot affect another notebook, and every terminal state refreshes the current graph range. Rebuild also refreshes pending merges and unified status. The separate `GET .../unified-kg/status` describes visualization building.

  **重新合并** runs without an LLM prerequisite; configured `kg_merge_review`/`kg_concept_description` provide fail-open enrichment. The content-version gate skips unchanged inputs; forced reclustering after settings changes remains CLI-only. Pending review keeps the deterministic highest-score representative per canonical component pair. Rejected/deferred seed decisions survive confirmed unions as component cannot-links. One decision locks and settles all duplicate pair rows atomically; pending-generation replacement reapplies live decisions in its refresh transaction. Rejecting a wholly pending pair removes it without dirtying/rebuilding; reversing any confirmed sibling invalidates the materialized union. Confirming a pending pair starts reclustering. If the slot returns 409, the browser retries after its holder finishes, retaining the retry mark across transient failures within the poll attempt cap. This is tab-local best effort: reload loses the mark; the durable fallback is 「待重建」 plus a manual click, with no server retry queue.

  **补上关联** is deterministic and zero-model. The explicit endpoint and successful-build tail share the same slot. A tail unable to claim emits `kg_relink_skipped` with notebook id/holder and skips; a skip behind reclustering is dropped, not deferred, so missing links wait for a manual click. The pass reads one source partition at a time, including empty/missing-source partitions and cross-source adjacency. Per-source commits publish KG changes even when a later partition fails. At a binding per-node edge cap, stable insertion order can select a different valid same-source partner from the older update-order implementation; edge/isolation counts are unchanged.

  **删除知识图谱** requires `kg:write` and UI confirmation. It removes user-document objects, relations, facts, embeddings, extraction runs/search rows, clusters, merge candidates and KG-analysis artifacts, then resets unified state. Conflict candidates go when either side they cite no longer exists, whatever their status; candidates between two surviving hidden objects or relations stay. The notebook's merge-review progress row goes unless it is running, so after a delete the merge-review status reads `idle` and a previous run's `failed`/`done` result is no longer reported (the UI only shows this progress while a run is in flight). A conflict-detection pass that was adjudicating when the delete committed writes none of its candidates back: it reads `kg_reset_epoch` before reading the graph and every write is conditional on it (on PostgreSQL under `FOR SHARE`, so a write racing the reset waits for it). A candidate or a finished merge-review row that still commits while the final reset transaction runs is removed by one post-commit sweep of those two steps, after the cache eviction; it never costs a retry round, and a failing sweep is logged without failing the delete. The rebuild-derived tables (`canonical_relations`, `communities`, `community_members`, `concept_comentions`, `mention_edges`) are deliberately kept until the next rebuild replaces them wholesale (deleting the notebook removes them with it): clearing them in the delete job was measured on a production-shaped notebook as a large slowdown. Their rows are not read in the meantime — re-extracting a concept mints the same canonical id, so the delete marks each layer: the published community generation becomes -1 (no community row carries it) and the canonical-relation and mention-bridge sequences become -2, which their readers (relation support, mention edges, co-mention peers) treat as having no derived data. A layer reopens only when that layer itself is rewritten by a rebuild, so the old rows stay unread while a rebuild is still clustering and after a layer's recompute fails. Each layer's rewrite is also conditional on the delete epoch it started under, so a recompute already in flight when the delete commits (an offline rebuild process) is rolled back instead of reopening the layer with the deleted graph's rows. Also kept: sources, parsed elements, hidden Memory/Knowhow projections (which can still yield `kg_ready`), rebuild checkpoints (version-checked before any reuse), the concept whitelist and per-run rebuild scratch rows.
