### Reflect plugin actions (`ask.reflect_action`)

A second production extension point lets a deployment plugin lend the reasoning Ask retrieval agent a function of its own — typically an internet or literature search. Registering it contributes exactly one action: its name, one-paragraph description, and parameter descriptions are projected into the reflect prompt, into the reflect schema hint, and into the action whitelist, and the model itself then decides whether to call it once the in-library retrieval channels have come back empty. Unlike [Gap consultation](#gap-consultation-askgap_consult) — a deterministic, once-per-run call made only after the response draft returns, whose output is never evidence and cannot move a word of the answer — a reflect action is model-triggered, called from inside the reflect loop while a run is still under way, and what it returns is genuine external evidence: it enters synthesis, it is citable with `[k]`, and it carries an openable URL. The two points coexist; nothing here retires `ask.gap_consult`.

**Trigger.** Reasoning Ask only, the same call sites `ask.gap_consult` never reaches (deep reports and Knowhow's row-completion retrieval each construct their own `ReasoningRetriever` and call `run()` directly, without this run state). Which actions are registered and live-available is asked exactly **once, at the start of the run** — not re-probed on every reflect turn — so this is a run-level topology fact, not a per-turn one: a plugin an administrator disables mid-run stays formally "offered" for the remainder of that run, but the host itself re-checks live availability inside every `invoke()` call, so a call against it still fails as an ordinary `plugin_action_failed` skip rather than reaching the disabled plugin; the toggle's effect on what gets *offered* only takes hold on the run's next start. Given that run-level topology is non-empty, four further conditions are decided fresh on every reflect turn: the effort tier is not the lowest one this repository defines — `overview|standard|deep|thorough|exhaustive`, with `overview` closed and every other tier open, and a caller with no effort tier at all (a report's per-section deep-dive, Knowhow completion, a narrow test double) is treated the same as the closed tier, because the cost of this channel has to be bought by an explicit effort choice; `REASONING_MAX_PLUGIN_ACTIONS` is greater than zero; the caller actually wired the egress-gated question string (an empty string closes the whole channel fail-closed, rather than falling back to a less-reviewed alternative); and this run has already come back empty from an in-library channel at least once — some action's consecutive zero-hit count is above zero, or the previous reflect turn was `no_progress` or `stale`. That last condition is the one true gate rather than a routing rule: it never prevents the model from choosing the action, it only withholds the option until the library itself has been tried and found wanting — including on the very first reflect turn, if that turn's own retrieval already came back empty. A turn with empty run-level topology, or one where any of the four re-decided conditions fails, has a `reflect_prompt`, `reflect_schema_hint`, and whitelist identical, byte for byte, to a deployment with no such plugin.

When the in-library fact gate opens through no progress, stale evidence or zero hits on a turn where a reflect plugin action is offered, core appends a fixed Chinese nudge to that turn's model-facing summary. It suggests calling an offered outside-search action if external or recent information could help, and answering directly only when outside search is inapplicable. The nudge contains no plugin text and is absent when the action gate is closed.

**What leaves the deployment.** One `ReflectActionCallContext`: `question` (the wording the user actually saw — the composed `research_question` intent contract never leaves, exactly as at `ask.gap_consult`) plus `arguments`, a flat string map the model itself wrote for the action's declared parameters, already validated against the descriptor (an unrecognized enum value is cleared before it reaches the plugin; free text is clamped to `REFLECT_ACTION_ARGUMENT_MAX_CHARS`; an unset optional parameter arrives as an empty string, so every declared parameter is always present as a key). No candidate text, no sub-query, no gap phrase, and no notebook/actor/source id of any kind ever reaches this context — the call-context type has no field for any of them. The arguments are logged verbatim into the persisted `plugin_action` trace step's detail, which is the transparency mechanism this feature relies on in place of a content filter: the person who asked the question can always see exactly what text left the deployment on their behalf.

**Budget and fail-open.** The reasoning host runs a contribution's availability check and its call together under a hard wall-clock deadline, `REASONING_PLUGIN_ACTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 8.0s) — the same private-daemon-worker, no-thread-pool, no-`contextvars.copy_context()` shape `ask.gap_consult` uses, for the same reasons: one hung plugin leaks one thread on the affected request rather than an outage-wide shared worker, and a plugin cannot inherit this request's frozen retrieval scope or a leaf-I/O fan-out slot simply by running underneath it. Three budgets stack: the descriptor's own `max_calls_per_run` and the deployment policy's `REASONING_MAX_PLUGIN_ACTIONS` (default 2) are taken as their minimum for that one action's per-run cap; `REASONING_MAX_PLUGIN_ACTIONS` is separately the run's total call budget across every action; and `EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_MAX_PER_RUN` (default 10) caps how many admitted items a run may accumulate across every call and every action. The per-action and run-total budgets above are debited **before** a call is made, not after it returns — a plugin that always times out would otherwise cost the model a fresh 8-second wall-clock wait every turn for free — so a call that only failed or timed out still spent a slot. What IS remembered per (action name, normalized arguments) pair is success: only a call that actually admitted material marks that exact pair seen, so retrying the identical arguments after a failure is allowed (and is bounded by the up-front budget debit instead) — repeating arguments that already worked is what gets skipped. Six stable reasons appear in a skip step's `detail.reason`, always phrased as instruction rather than rebuke: `plugin_action_disabled` (a depth-defense catch — the action was not actually offered this turn), `plugin_action_missing_argument` (a required parameter came back empty, naming which one and what it needs), `plugin_action_cap` (the per-action, run-total, or admission budget above is exhausted), `duplicate_plugin_action` (the same action name and normalized arguments already admitted material earlier in this run), `plugin_action_last_turn` (there is no following reflect turn left to consume the result, mirroring `consult_memory`'s own last-turn skip), and `plugin_action_failed` (the host could not retrieve anything — timeout, cancellation, a malformed or `UNAVAILABLE` result, or a raising contributor all collapse to this one code, carrying the host's own stable sub-code in `detail.code`; this step discloses `arguments` verbatim exactly as the successful `plugin_action` step does — the request had already left the deployment before the failure was observable, so the audit answer to “what was sent on my behalf” cannot depend on whether it worked — plus `attempted: true`, which is what separates *attempted* from the successful step's *delivered*). Cancellation never raises out of the host itself: `invoke` answers with the `plugin_action_cancelled` failure code, and the reflect loop re-reads its own cancellation token immediately afterward and propagates from there — cancellation still ends the run at the first opportunity, on the loop's own reading of it. A call that returns zero admitted items is not a failure: it records a normal `plugin_action` trace step with `found: 0` and counts as a zero-hit for that action name, feeding the same "library already came back empty" fact the trigger gate reads. Anything that goes wrong here — no plugin registered, an unavailable or misbehaving contribution, a malformed return shape — leaves the run byte-identical to a deployment with no such plugin at all, aside from the recorded skip step.

**Availability.** A plugin declares the capability its action probes through its own manifest `provides`, exactly like every other contributor kind, plus the administrator's own runtime plugin toggle (#635's three gate points). There is deliberately no dedicated `*_ENABLED` setting: the plugin registration itself is explicit, boot-frozen configuration, the admin toggle is already a live switch, and `REASONING_MAX_PLUGIN_ACTIONS=0` is already a complete deployment-level kill switch that removes the prompt line, the schema branch, and the whitelist entry all at once — a fourth switch would only be one more place for the three to fall out of step. A deployment with zero registered actions costs zero probe calls and zero events — the host's own `specs()` returns immediately — though the calling run still computes its one fixed per-turn deadline regardless, exactly as it does whenever the channel is closed for any other reason.

**External evidence.** An admitted item becomes evidence with `tier="external"`, `object_type="external"`, and always-empty `source_id`/`element_id` — structurally empty, not merely unset, because external material has no row in any notebook's source or element tables. Every field on it — title, excerpt, source label, location label — is folded through a control-character filter at admission time: any run of control characters, line separators, or bidi overrides collapses to one space, which is what keeps a hostile excerpt from opening a second, forged evidence line inside either of the two blocks below (both render one line per item, and the reverse binding back to an admitted item depends on that shape holding). Reflect's own candidate-summary preview and the final synthesis context render the SAME admitted items in two different shapes, not one. The **preview** (`_external_block_text`, rebuilt after every admitted call — including a call that admitted nothing but carried a `note`, which renders under a `[External evidence] (nothing admitted so far)` header with only the `Note:` line, so a plugin's explanation of an empty search still reaches the next turn; only when items and note are both empty is the block absent) opens with a fixed `[External evidence] (outside the library; citable, labelled [external · <source>])` header line, then one `x{n} · [external · <source_label>] · <title> · <excerpt>` line per item — `x{n}` is only this preview's own display index, never the `[k]` number a citation actually uses — with the excerpt cut to its first 160 characters (enough for the model to judge what the material is, not a second full copy to read), then an optional trailing `…(+N)` line disclosing how many further items its own `EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_REFLECT_BLOCK_CHARS` budget (default 1,600 characters, spent whole-item) could not fit, then an optional `Note: <note>` line carrying the plugin's own one-sentence observation. The **synthesis** block (`evidence_context.external_context`) instead renders `k{n}: [external · <source_label>] <title> (<location_label>) — <excerpt>` with the full excerpt and the actual `[k]` number, spending its own independent `EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE_CONTEXT_CHARS` budget (default 4,000 characters), appended after every in-library section has already been assembled. An item whose URL is empty or is not `http://`/`https://` is skipped entirely from the synthesis block rather than rendered half-complete, and skipped items do not consume a key — admitted items are always numbered with no holes. In both blocks, an item that does not fit inside its own budget is dropped whole rather than clipped mid-excerpt, because a half-quotation attributed to a named outside source is a misquotation, not merely a shortened one. Sectioned synthesis appends the identical synthesis block to **every** section (unlike the Memory/derivation-chain/collection-map blocks, which stay fallback-path only), because external material is not bound to any one section's outline the way those are, and leaving it out of some sections would let the merged citation table cite material a given section's own draft never actually saw. `answer_prompt` gains one extra numbered rule, and only when the composed context genuinely contains an `[external · …]` item: cite it with `[k]` like anything else, but never describe it as notebook or library content, and when it disagrees with a notebook item, say which side is which rather than merging them; a run with no external evidence leaves `answer_prompt` byte-identical to before this feature existed. A citation is only issued for an item that actually entered a prompt the model saw — items the per-item budget dropped, or that failed the URL rail, never reach the citations list, and the run trace discloses the gap sparsely as `external_included`/`external_dropped` counts (present only on a run that actually surfaced external evidence, never zero-padded onto an ordinary answer's persisted detail). `grounded`/`evidence_level` are unaffected in shape: an external anchor is read through the same deterministic evidence-key door an exact-lookup citation already uses, never through a synthesized relevance score — there is no retrieval score for material nothing in this deployment ranked.

**Front end.** A reference card for an `object_type == "external"` item shows an "打开链接"/Open-link action, rendered only when the URL is `http`/`https`, opening in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and an "导入为来源"/Import-as-source action that reuses the exact same core URL-import endpoint and callback a Gap consultation suggestion's own import button uses (`POST /notebooks/{id}/sources/url`, `sources:write` capability); a read-only workspace that never wires that callback renders neither button. The two surfaces share one row-state controller keyed by URL: importing a link from the gap-suggestions panel or from an external-evidence citation card immediately shows "已导入"/Imported on both, because the backend import endpoint neither single-flights nor deduplicates by URL on its own — importing the identical URL again in a later turn is a second, ordinary import, not a no-op. The source-distribution summary tag's third bucket, 「外部 N」, is rendered only when that count is above zero; a run with no external evidence leaves the tag exactly as it read before this feature existed. The `plugin_action` trace step carries the front-end label 「扩展检索」; its own skip steps render the backend's own `summary` text verbatim, the same convention every other reflect skip step already follows. The arguments the model sent are disclosed in two tiers: the collapsed step row shows a summary clipped to 120 characters (marked with `…`), and the expanded row lists every non-empty argument in full, one `name: value` line each, never clipped — for the successful `plugin_action` step and equally for a `plugin_action_failed` skip step carrying `attempted: true`, since the request had left the deployment either way; skip steps without `attempted` (budget, duplicate, last turn) never sent anything and disclose nothing.

**Public share.** `conversation_public_view.public_reference` adds `is_external` (`tier == "external"`) to the existing reference projection; it deliberately does **not** project `url`. An anonymous `/c/{token}` reader is told the item came from outside the library and sees its title and excerpt, but gets no addressable link — the same "nothing addressable" rule the rest of that projection already applies to every internal id.

**MCP.** `ask`'s `anchors` and `citations` carry the same `url` field the HTTP endpoint does, present only on rows whose `tier` is `external` (`exclude_if` empty, so every existing payload without external evidence serializes byte for byte as before).

**Registration rails (freeze time, loud failures).** An action name must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,31}$` and must not collide with any of the 19 core reflect action ids or any of the 17 top-level reflect schema field names (their union, `RESERVED_REFLECT_KEYS`) — otherwise a plugin action would either share a name with a core action or write its arguments into a core schema slot (`browse_sections` and `read_section` are core ids and top-level schema fields since in-document navigation shipped, so an already-deployed plugin whose action carries either name fails startup after the upgrade until it is renamed; the same holds for `find_sources`, `get_paper_cards`, `extract_from_sources` and the top-level `answer_layout` field of the paper tools). A parameter name must not be `name` or `reason`, there may be at most `REFLECT_ACTION_PARAMETERS_MAX` (4) of them, and an `enum` parameter must declare between 2 and `REFLECT_ACTION_ENUM_VALUES_MAX` (8) values — the 2-value floor exists because the schema-hint validator decides "this is an enum" by the presence of a `|` character, so a single-value enum would read as a closed choice to the model while validating as free text underneath. Every plugin-authored string — the action description, each parameter description, the source label — is checked, never silently clamped: over its length limit or carrying a control character (a newline included) fails registration outright (`ExtensionRegistryError`, a startup failure), because the descriptor is deployment configuration reviewed at boot, not user data a runtime clamp is allowed to reshape.

## Professional Excel analysis and automatic parsing-issue archive

Uploaded `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, and legacy `.xls` sources keep the ordinary document-parsing
path and additionally receive a deterministic spreadsheet snapshot during ingestion. The
snapshot preserves typed cell values, detected headers, sheet/range identity, source-row
anchors, formula counts, and formula cached-value gaps. It never executes formulas, macros,
external links, or workbook code. Failure of this optional compiler does not change the
source's ordinary parse status or remove it from text retrieval.
Header detection keeps the earliest structurally plausible row, including numeric labels
such as year columns; a later all-text data row cannot silently replace it.

Only `reasoning` Ask can consume the snapshot. The lane remains dormant unless the frozen,
user-selected source scope contains a compiled workbook and the question has an analytical
spreadsheet intent. Include/exclude scopes are resolved through the same frozen `allows`
semantics as retrieval across the active notebook and every allowed mounted participant;
excluded workbooks and excluded reference libraries never reach the planner.
Global Ask has no current notebook, so there the lane takes its federated form: the participants
are the original-text channel's own set (the selected libraries that passed the read re-check,
bounded by `CHUNK_FEDERATION_MAX_PARTICIPANTS`; with `CHUNK_FEDERATION_ENABLED=false` only the
first library remains), and each library contributes only visible sources inside its frozen
source ceiling, so an unselected or unreadable library and a deselected workbook are neither
listed nor read. Each library's source-list read gets the passage channel's preparation
protections: a cancellation check, then a read inside the global run plan's per-library budget
(`GLOBAL_ASK_NOTEBOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`); a library whose read fails or times out is dropped alone
(the trace step's `skipped` lists it with its reason code), a library the passage channel already
failed to prepare in this run keeps that reason and is not read again, and a cancellation still
ends the whole run. All participants' workbooks form one catalog: only libraries that actually hold
a workbook take part in the ordering and rotation; they are sorted by notebook id, the rotation's
starting library is derived from a digest of the question (deterministic per question, even across
questions, and the nominal first library gets no head start), then one workbook per library per
round, each library's own in source order; a source id is listed once. When two or more libraries
contribute workbooks, every catalog entry also carries `library` (the owning notebook's name as the
asker sees it), the planner prompt explains it, and the synthesis model's table block names
`library=` too, so same-titled workbooks in two libraries can be told apart; the names count
against the catalog byte budget. The catalog shares the single-notebook
`SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_PLANNER_CATALOG_BYTES` budget and workbooks are read one at a time, stopping
the moment that budget is spent, so planner calls (at most one), executed sheets (at most
`SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_MAX_TARGETS`, the single-notebook cap, possibly from different libraries),
catalog length and workbooks read are all capped by the single-notebook bound and do not grow with the
number of libraries; when only one library contributes workbooks the catalog is byte-identical to
the single-notebook one (no `library`). What does not fit is disclosed by count: the planner prompt
states "X readable workbooks across the participants, N listed in library rotation, M not listed"
(a workbook found corrupt while reading is not counted in X), the result card carries the same
sentence, and the `spreadsheet` trace step adds `notebook_id`, `libraries`,
`contributing_libraries`, `workbooks`, `listed` and `skipped`, with the summary naming the library
(when several tables are analysed, `notebook_id` moves into each `tables[]` entry and the summary
names each table's library).
Results and receipts carry their owning notebook and that notebook's tier (in peer mode the first
library keeps its id too), and a global result also carries `notebook_name`; when the table comes
from another library (any library in Global Ask, a mounted reference library in a notebook ask)
and the UI knows its name, the result card's title line says which, in the citation card's
wording. Intent requires either
explicit workbook/table context (including a closed set of Chinese "...表" table nouns such as
「报表」「报价表」「价格表」「明细表」「统计表」; a bare 「表」 does not count) plus an analysis phrase
(including 「比较」/「对比」), or an unambiguous table operation;
an isolated `行`/`列` character inside an unrelated word does not qualify, and bare English
verbs such as `count`, `top`, or `group` require table context unless they form a clear
construction such as `sum Amount by Region`. The lane then
reuses the deployment's existing `reasoning_agent` chat workload
for at most one bounded planning call—there is no general-purpose SDK agent—and validates
the result into the closed operations `profile`, `aggregate`, `top`, and `filter`. Aggregation
and filters also use closed operator lists; execution is local and deterministic. A planner
plan may name at most 8 filters and 20 result columns; exceeding either invariant invalidates
the whole plan and falls back to a local profile, so no prefix of a user-requested operation
is executed as though it were complete. A planner timeout or malformed plan likewise falls
back to a local profile, and any lane failure fails open to
the ordinary reasoning answer.
One plan may name several tables (user ruling 2026-10-19): the planner returns a `targets` list,
one entry per sheet, at most `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_MAX_TARGETS` entries (default 3, range 1..3),
and is told to write more than one only when the question explicitly compares, contrasts or
separately analyses several tables; it is still that one planner call (its output allowance
scales to 500 tokens per entry). Each entry is validated on its own: an invalid entry drops only
itself and is never replaced by another table. One sheet may be analysed several ways (user ruling
2026-10-21, e.g. a sum and a ranking of the same table): each analysis takes a seat under the cap
and gets its own card; only an entry that computes exactly what an earlier one computes (same
sheet, same operation, same parameters and filters that operation actually reads -- a count
ignores its measure, a ranking its result columns) is dropped as a duplicate. The distinct valid
entries run in plan order up to the cap, the rest are cut in plan order and the last result card
says so ("本次规划了 X 项表格分析，超过单次最多 N 项的上限，按规划顺序只做了前 N 项；未做：工作簿 · 工作表（操作：
参数）…"). A reply with no usable entry (an empty list, not a list, all invalid) falls back
exactly as an invalid single plan did, to the local profile of the first sheet. Every executed
analysis is its own result card, in plan order, naming its workbook and sheet and, when it comes
from another library, that library; when a sheet is analysed more than once in the run, those
cards also carry `analysis_label` (a reading of the parameters, e.g. 「按 Price 降序」; a profile or
filter without parameters reads 「全部行」/「全部列」; filter values are spelled as JSON, text quoted, so
`true` and "是" never read the same), shown after
the operation name on the card and written as `plan=…;` on the synthesis block's title line, so
two cards of one sheet with the same operation can be told apart; a sheet analysed once carries
no such field. There is no merged comparison card -- the comparison is the synthesized answer's
job. When one analysis runs, the card, the trace step, the synthesis table block and its citable
map are byte-identical to before; with several, the trace summary reads "已分析 N 张表：…" (all
different sheets) or "已对 M 张表做了 N 项分析：…", and `detail.tables[]` lists the per-analysis
fields, and whenever the reply named
more than one entry `detail.targets` adds `planned`, `executed`, `invalid`, `duplicate`,
`over_limit` and `limit`.
Successful output adds a `spreadsheet` trace step, citable bounded evidence, and one
`result_sets[]` item with `kind="spreadsheet"` per table; the card discloses
scanned/result/displayed rows, formula-cache gaps, and partial preview coverage. The planner
receives a whole-field prefix projection of the selected workbook/sheet/header catalog under
one aggregate byte rail; omitted fields are never cut mid-value, and a result warning discloses
when that projection was partial. The persisted/browser result is independently bounded by
rows, cells (headers included), and serialized table bytes (per result card), while synthesis
receives a further row-and-byte-bounded preview. Several tables share that preview's one budget
(`SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_PROMPT_BYTES` and the characters the source partition leaves it); it does
not grow with the number of tables. Every table's title line goes in first, in plan order, then
every table's header line, in plan order (a table whose header does not fit shows no rows), then
preview rows round robin, one per table per round (each table shows a prefix of its own rows; the
first row that does not fit ends that table). So a wide header cannot push a later table's title
line out, a larger budget never lists fewer tables, and the first table cannot starve the others. Table evidence keys run from `k6001` in plan order; plugin-returned external evidence
shares the 6000 band and now numbers after the table keys instead of restarting at `k6001` (when
both appeared they used to collide and the merged map overwrote the table receipt); without
table results external evidence still starts at `k6001`. Two sheets of one workbook keep one
source-level citation each.
Every spreadsheet evidence line admitted under that preview byte rail is retained whole in
the citable evidence map; it is never subjected to a second hidden character slice.

The professional compiler refuses shapes it cannot analyze without guessing: unreadable,
damaged or encrypted workbooks; missing headers; dimension/sheet limits; cells over the
character rail; and a second header-like region separated by a blank row. It never silently
truncates a user cell or combines multiple likely tables. Such a failure opens a
`spreadsheet_analysis` issue while ordinary text parsing continues. A terminal source-parser
failure opens `source_parse`. The system copies an upload—not moves it—into a private
quarantine outside the notebook source tree, stores only a content-minimal safe issue
projection for administrators, and never exposes its physical path or source hash through
the API.

The same private artifact store also owns `model_output` records. Whenever any of the current
29 structured chat workloads fails the scheduler's shared JSON syntax/shape contract, the
system creates a new immutable case. The list projection contains only its model area, stable
workload id/display label, failure kind, timestamps, `support_id`, and any available actor,
notebook, and parent-work linkage. Complete messages, the schema hint, raw response, and an
explicit user question are read only when an administrator opens that one case; they are never
bulk-loaded into the list response. A model-output record copies no source file and is not
resolved by model retry or a product fallback: it stays `open` until expiry or related-notebook
deletion. Calls without Notebook context use the private `_unscoped` directory, retain the same
classification, identify the executor as `system`, and do not invent a user or notebook association.

| Spreadsheet-analysis rail | Default | Accepted range |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_ENABLED` | `true` | boolean |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_MAX_CELLS` | 200,000 | 1,000..2,000,000 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_MAX_SHEETS` | 32 | 1..256 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_MAX_CELL_CHARS` | 20,000 | 256..1,000,000 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_RESULT_ROWS` | 100 | 1..1,000 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_RESULT_CELLS` | 2,000 | 10..20,000 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_RESULT_BYTES` | 262,144 | 1,024..2,097,152 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_PROMPT_ROWS` | 20 | 1..100 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_PROMPT_BYTES` | 65,536 | 1,024..524,288 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_PLANNER_CATALOG_BYTES` | 32,768 | 1,024..262,144 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_MAX_TARGETS` | 3 | 1..3 |
| `SPREADSHEET_ANALYSIS_PLANNER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | 8.0 seconds | 1.0..60.0 |
| `ANALYSIS_FAILURE_RETENTION_DAYS` | 30 days | 1..3,650 |

Issue records have `open`/`resolved` status and a stamped expiry. For a source issue, a later
successful user-initiated reparse automatically resolves the matching record and deletes its
quarantine copy; a `model_output` case is neither retried nor auto-resolved. Expiry is a hard
read boundary and physical cleanup occurs on list and single-model-case reads. Source or
notebook deletion immediately removes the spreadsheet snapshot and quarantine copy, clears
owner/source/notebook linkage, names, ids, filenames, hashes, model messages, schema, raw
response, `support_id`, and parent-work id, and retains only
category/time and a redacted summary under a new neutral case id and identifier-free archive
path until expiry. This filesystem redaction is best-effort
after a committed notebook deletion: a cleanup I/O failure is logged without making the
already-completed DELETE appear to fail.
Model prompts may contain evidence from several sources, and the scheduler boundary owns no
trustworthy per-source identity ledger. Deleting any source therefore conservatively destroys
**all** retained model content for that notebook instead of guessing which cases cited it.

The administrator's **User usage overview** keeps its existing user-table columns and adds
two sheets next to it: **Question analysis** and **Parsing issues**. Each user row keeps separate
**View questions** and **LLM logs** links: the former opens Question analysis on that user's Ask
questions, while the latter opens the Model calls log view filtered to that user. Question analysis
switches between **问答** (Ask) and **深度报告** (Deep Report) for the selected user; a selected report
opens its read-only body and citations. Both sheets are read-only. Parsing issues can
be filtered by user, status, category, and the seven model areas. A model-output case loads its
full prompt and response only when that row is explicitly opened; list loading never bulk-reads
the content. A live source links to the original notebook and
the exact source's read-only administrator detail in User activity (rather than the ordinary
workspace, whose owner/member guard still applies), while a deleted source shows only the
redacted summary. The administrator has
no reparse, bulk retry, close, quarantine-delete, or case-purge endpoint/control and therefore
cannot mutate a user's notebook through this feature.

- `GET /api/admin/analysis-issues?owner_id=&status=&category=&model_area=&offset=&limit=` — admin-only,
  read-only list; `status` is empty/`open`/`resolved`, `category` is empty/`source_parse`/
  `spreadsheet_analysis`/`model_output`, `model_area` is empty/`ask`/`report`/`source`/
  `knowledge`/`memory`/`knowhow`/`retrieval`, `offset` is `>= 0` (default 0), and `limit` is
  `1..500` (default 200). Rows are newest-updated first; the response carries `items` plus
  `total`, the full match count under the same filters and expiry sweep, so no match beyond one
  page is silently unreachable. The Parsing issues sheet requests 50 rows per page, and changing
  any filter returns it to the first page. There is deliberately no POST/PATCH/DELETE companion.
- `GET /api/admin/analysis-issues/{issue_id}/artifact` — admin-only read of the complete
  request messages, schema hint, and raw model response for one unexpired `model_output` case.
  Source issues and missing, deleted, or expired cases return 404. It is read-only and exposes
  no physical path.
- `GET /api/admin/users/{user_id}/notebooks/{notebook_id}/sources/{source_id}` — the
  content-minimal, read-only exact-source projection used by that analysis deep link; it
  returns 404 unless the notebook belongs to the path user and the source is a live visible
  source in that notebook.

## Admin observability: user activity (`/dev/logs`)

`/dev/logs` shares one top scope bar (viewed user, date range) across two view tabs: **Activity** (default) and **Model calls** (the original per-day LLM-call viewer, unchanged byte-for-byte — `kind`/`status`/`model` facets, full-text search, per-day dropdown, and auto-refresh all behave exactly as before; its API remains `/api/debug/logs/...`, still gated by `DEBUG_LOGS_ENABLED`).

A deployment admin reading a user's full answers and reports here is audit access: a separate, admin-only read that the per-user rules of the notebook surfaces (the answer-owner rule, the report creator gate) do not govern.

The Activity tab is three columns:

- **Scope** — the viewed user's own notebooks (name plus source/ask/report counts), each expandable to that notebook's source list (display name plus a parse-status badge). Selecting a notebook filters the middle stream to it; selecting a source only opens it in the right Detail column (it does **not** filter the stream — see "not yet built" below). The notebook list is fetched whole and shown 20 per page; a selected notebook on a later page (for example one selected by a parsing-issue deep link) turns the list to that page. A source list fetches its first 50 sources, discloses `已显示 N / M 个来源` while more remain, and **加载更多来源** appends the next 50 (`offset` = rows already shown, de-duplicated by source id). The button is disabled while that page is in flight; a failed append reports beside the button and keeps the rows already listed. Changing the viewed user, or re-fetching the first page, discards a late append.
- **Activity stream** — asks, sources, and reports merged into one newest-first feed, `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` keyset-paginated ("加载更多"/Load more), 50 items per page by default (`limit`, capped at 200). The type controls switch between all activity and ask/source/report-only feeds. **Global Ask** jobs are merged into this feed too, as `type="ask"`/`scope="global"` rows attributed by submitting `user_id`, carrying a 「全局」(Global) chip; `notebook_id` is always empty, so an explicit notebook filter (`notebook_id=`) excludes them while the mixed feed and ask-only mode both include them. A self-service read of this list applies the same rule notebook asks follow: every participant notebook must still be readable by the viewed user as a set, otherwise the row is omitted (the predicate applies before each table's `LIMIT`, exactly like notebook asks, so a page is never eaten by filtered rows and `has_more`/cursor semantics match the other three types); an administrator's audit read is not filtered, matching revoked shared-notebook questions. The detail endpoint below applies the same rule. A global row's failure text is `error_detail` (administrators only); a failed row written before that column existed falls back to its fixed owner-facing sentence. Ask and report rows name their notebook under the question (「笔记本：库名」, truncated with the full name on hover): the ask-only and report-only modes include shared-notebook submissions while the Scope column lists only owned notebooks, so the row is where an administrator sees which notebook a question was asked in. A retained post-deletion row names the notebook as it was when deleted, beside the 「原笔记本已删除」 chip; a global Ask row carries only its 「全局」 chip and no notebook name, and source rows name none (the Scope column already shows their notebook). Ask-only mode is labelled **Question overview**, keeps each question whole, and is the direct destination of the admin user-usage page's **View questions** link so an administrator can scan that user's concerns across time. Its all-questions scope follows the usage total's `ask_jobs.created_by` attribution, including the user's submissions in shared notebooks; selecting a notebook narrows back to one of that user's owned notebooks, and the date filter remains available. Report-only mode is labelled **Report overview** and follows the same rule against the usage total's `reports.created_by` attribution, so it includes reports the user created in shared notebooks. The type filter is applied by the repository **before** each table's page limit, never client-side after a mixed page, so newer source/report rows cannot crowd questions out and every question remains reachable through keyset pagination. A native date picker plus "全部时间"/all-time drives a half-open `[since, until)` window. Its bounds carry the **browser's UTC offset** (`2026-08-04T00:00:00+08:00`), so "a day" means the viewer's local calendar day — the same timezone every rendered timestamp already uses; each bound computes its own offset, so a DST-transition day is not off by an hour. A malformed bound fails the request with `400` plus a user-facing message (`X-User-Message`) rather than silently widening the window or 500-ing. All three item types are normalized through the same `parse_activity_instant` helper (`app/core/activity_time.py`) on both database backends: SQLite compares on an absolute instant via `julianday()` (mixed naive/offset-aware `created_at` text — historical rows are naive, newer rows carry an offset — is unified by reading a naive value as UTC), while PostgreSQL compares natively on `timestamptz` with the same `COALESCE` fallback SQLite applies (`ask_jobs.created_at` is nullable there, and PostgreSQL's default `DESC` ordering is `NULLS FIRST`, so an unset value would otherwise pin a broken row to page 1 and break the Python merge). Both backends fold an unparseable or null value onto one shared sentinel instant that sorts last **and** round-trips through the cursor, so `next_cursor` never emits a value the next page cannot parse. The three sources are queried independently with their own keyset pages and merged in Python rather than a three-way `UNION ALL`, so a large deployment gets an honest, bounded "this page covers up to HH:MM" rather than a full sort blow-up.
  For shared-notebook submissions, caller authority is deliberate: an administrator retains the complete creator-attributed audit history even after the viewed user loses access, while a regular user viewing themselves sees only submissions whose notebook still passes the canonical live read predicate. Ask and report detail apply the same self-service read check, so a revoked row cannot be recovered by retaining its job or report id. Raw failure text is administrator-only diagnostics: the persisted `ask_jobs.error` / `reports.error` string is a caught exception's text that can name internal model gateways or server paths, so the ask entries in the activity feed and both detail endpoints return it only when the caller is an administrator (who can already read that user's raw model-call logs). A self-service read receives an empty `error` with the unchanged `status`, and the Detail column shows fixed copy for a failed ask or report instead — the same direction as the source entries' `parse_failed` boolean and the fixed failure copy the Deep Report workspace UI shows. This rule covers the activity surface only; other APIs that carry failure text (for example the notebook report detail, the ask job status and stream, and self-service model-call logs) keep their own existing contracts.
  Notebook deletion has a separate, bounded rule. In the same transaction that deletes the notebook aggregate, the service snapshots only the analysis metadata for its visible sources, asks, and reports into a table with no notebook foreign key. The default retention window is **180 days after deletion**, configurable with `USER_ACTIVITY_RETENTION_DAYS` (`1..3650`). The projection keeps attribution, notebook id/name, event timestamps, question/report prompt, the ask/report `submitted_via` entry point, source display/file metadata, status, and the deletion/expiry stamps. It never keeps answer text, citations, reasoning traces, source bodies/elements, report sections, or report references; those still disappear with the notebook. If an offline database merge has already placed an older snapshot beside a live notebook with the same id, that retained set stays hidden while the notebook is live; a later deletion discards the entire older set, projects the current aggregate, and restarts the window from the actual deletion time. During the window, admin usage totals and the unscoped admin Activity feed include the retained rows, marked `notebook_deleted_at`/`retained_until` and “原笔记本已删除”. A deleted notebook no longer appears in Scope and cannot be selected as a notebook filter. Self-service reads still require a live readable notebook, so only administrators can inspect this post-deletion projection. `expires_at` is a hard read gate; expired rows vanish immediately from totals/feed/detail, then startup recovery or the next notebook deletion physically prunes them. This is rolling time retention, not a backup or an unbounded audit log. The global Ask turns that used the deleted notebook are stamped with the same expiry in the same transaction, stay readable to their owner during the window (body kept, citations into the deleted library shown as "来源已删除") and are cleaned up by the same rule afterwards; see [After a participant notebook is deleted](#after-a-participant-notebook-is-deleted).
- **Detail** — an ask from a live notebook shows the full question, answer, citations, and reasoning trace (the existing read-only Ask-panel renderers); a retained post-deletion ask shows only the question/status metadata plus the deletion/expiry notice. A selected notebook ask or report names its notebook under the title (once the detail arrives the detail endpoint's name wins, so a rename after the list was read shows); a retained post-deletion entry names the notebook only in its retention notice, not on a second line. A selected global Ask job additionally shows **参与笔记本** (Participant notebooks) — the participant set projected as `notebook_ids`/`notebook_names` below. A failed ask or report shows its recorded raw failure reason to administrators, and a report with failed sections — whatever its status — lists each section's raw failure text under "章节失败原因" (administrators only); when no raw text is returned (every self-service read, or a row that recorded none) it shows fixed copy instead, and an ask interrupted by a service restart says so. A report from a live notebook shows its status, depth, timing, and the read-only report body with citations (the shared Deep Report Markdown renderer, without image assets or source navigation); a report with no body yet says so, and a retained post-deletion report shows only its prompt/status metadata plus the deletion/expiry notice. A source shows its display name, parse status, and derived diagnostics; a model-call row (Model calls tab only) reuses the existing prompt/response transcript viewer, unchanged.

Four endpoints (self-or-admin reads; permission mirrors `debug_logs._resolve_owner`'s owner-or-admin check — the viewed `user_id` may be the caller's own id, or the caller must have `role="admin"`, otherwise 403). They're also gated by a dedicated deploy-time switch, `USER_ACTIVITY_VIEW_ENABLED` (default **true**): Activity is the default `/dev/logs` tab, so gating it behind the default-off `DEBUG_LOGS_ENABLED` would 404 every ordinary deployment's default tab; the two switches are independent — `DEBUG_LOGS_ENABLED` continues to gate only `/api/debug/logs/...` behind the Model calls tab. Because the frontend has no other way to learn this deploy-time value, `GET /system/config`'s `SystemConfiguration` response carries it as `user_activity_view_enabled`; `/dev/logs` reads it there and, when `false`, hides the Activity tab and defaults `view` to `llm` instead (a `?view=activity` deep link is normalized away rather than opening a tab whose endpoints all 404). A missing field (older backend, newer frontend) is treated as `true`, matching the backend's own default rather than hiding an available tab. `GET /admin/users/{user_id}/notebooks` (reused by the Scope column) is likewise self-or-admin rather than admin-only, so a user viewing their own activity can read their own notebook list:

- `GET /admin/users/{user_id}/activity?activity_type=&notebook_id=&since=&until=&before_ts=&before_id=&limit=` — the feed above; optional `activity_type` is exactly `ask`, `source`, or `report`, and omission keeps the merged feed. Ask and report entries carry the same `submitted_via` value as the question overview (`web`, `mcp`, or `''` for not recorded); the stream labels recorded values 「网页」/「MCP」 and shows no label for unrecorded rows. Ask entries and the ask detail also carry `output` (`answer` or `evidence`, default `answer`); an `evidence` entry is labelled 「仅检索」 in the stream and its detail reads 「仅检索，未生成回答」 with no answer panel. Ask and report entries carry `notebook_name`: for a live notebook it is the current name at read time (looked up once by id for the notebooks the page's asks and reports touch, leaving each type's own query unchanged; a concurrent deletion can leave it empty), for a retained post-deletion snapshot it is the name at deletion, and for a global Ask job it is empty. In an administrator's audit read a shared notebook the viewed user has since lost access to is still named, matching the Question analysis page's 「笔记本」 column.
- `GET /admin/users/{user_id}/notebooks/{notebook_id}/sources?offset=&limit=` — that notebook's source list (default `limit` 50, capped 200; the Scope panel pages through it with **加载更多来源**); 404 if the notebook is not owned by `user_id`.
- `GET /admin/users/{user_id}/asks/{job_id}` — one ask's detail; a live ask includes question/answer/trace and its notebook's `notebook_name` (as the report detail does), while an unexpired retained ask includes question/status/deletion metadata with `answer=null` and an empty trace. `error` carries the raw failure text for administrators only and is empty for self-service callers. It is 404 if the job is not owned by `user_id`, if a self-service caller no longer has live notebook read access, or if the retained row has expired. `job_id` also serves a global Ask job: the response carries `scope="global"`, the participant set `notebook_ids`, and `notebook_names` for the participants the viewed user can still read (a deleted or now-unreadable participant is left out). An administrator keeps the complete audit record even after the viewed user later lost read access to a participant — the same rule as a notebook ask. A self-service read instead applies the global Ask page's own reader rule: **if any one participant is no longer readable, the whole detail is 404**, not just that one participant hidden from an otherwise-visible answer. As with the notebook branch, both reader checks and the answer projection run inside one adapter transaction that holds the job row and every participant's read-authority chain until the response is assembled, so a revocation or deletion landing mid-request cannot carry a no-longer-authorized answer across the commit boundary.
- `GET /admin/users/{user_id}/reports/{report_id}` — one report's detail; a live report includes question, depth, status, timing stamps, `error` (raw failure text for administrators only, empty for self-service callers), `section_errors` (`[{index, title, error}]` for each section whose generation failed, with its raw failure text — on a `done` report too; administrators only, the same disclosure rule as `error`, empty for self-service callers), `content_md`, and `references`, while an unexpired retained report (administrators only) includes its prompt/status/deletion metadata with an empty `content_md`, `references`, and `section_errors`. Like ask detail, the adapter holds the notebook lifecycle lock and the report row while the response is assembled. It is 404 if the report was not created by `user_id`, if a self-service caller no longer has live notebook read access, or if the retained row has expired.

Mixed activity, the source-only feed, and every explicit notebook filter are attributed **owner-only**: they break down only notebooks the viewed user created (`created_by`, excluding notebooks mid-copy), matching the existing convention that the admin usage overview's expanded per-notebook inventory stays owner-only. The unscoped ask-only Question overview and report-only Report overview are the registered exceptions above and include shared-notebook submissions by the viewed user. Hidden synthetic sources (`memory`/`knowhow`) are excluded from the source list, the activity feed, **and** the Scope column's per-notebook source count — that count now applies the same single-source-of-truth visibility predicate the list itself uses, so the header and the expanded list can no longer disagree. (Because `GET /admin/users/{user_id}/notebooks` backs both screens, the admin usage overview's per-notebook source count drops to the same visible-source figure for any user who has saved a Memory record or built a Knowhow table; it was over-counting before.) The same notebook's report count is likewise scoped to `created_by = user_id`, matching `questions`'s existing predicate and the Activity stream's own report entries: a report another writable member created in a shared notebook is no longer counted toward the notebook owner's header (it was over-counting before, and the count would silently disagree with the expanded stream, which never showed that entry). A source activity entry never carries the raw `error_message` (it can hold a server-side absolute path); it exposes a derived `parse_failed` boolean plus `extraction_warning`/`parse_quality_warning`/`paper_meta_status`, mirroring `ScopedSourceDetail`'s existing redaction. Its display name is `SourceSummary`'s new, additive `display_title` field (paper title preferred, the same single implementation citation cards already use — `source_display.py::source_display_title`); the existing `title` field is untouched, so the Sources sidebar has zero regression. `SourceSummary` also gained an additive raw `created_at` timestamp: both entry points into the Detail column (Scope list and Activity stream) render it in the **browser's** timezone, where the pre-existing `created_label` is a server-side pre-formatted calendar day and would otherwise show the same source under two different dates depending on which column was clicked. `created_label` remains for the existing Sources sidebar. A report entry's duration reuses the Deep Report rule verbatim: `generation_started_at → updated_at`, no duration shown when the start stamp is missing, unfinished reports show only their creation time.

The unscoped ask-only and report-only exceptions above are therefore caller-sensitive: administrators may include revoked shared-notebook history; self-service reads include shared submissions only while live read access remains valid. Filtering still occurs before the page limit in both cases.

Explicitly not yet built (a phased sequencing choice, not a silent gap): correlating a model call to the ask/report that triggered it — this needs a new write-side log-context propagation and cannot be backfilled onto history recorded before it ships; surfacing per-stage retrieval/parsing timings inside ask/source detail; clicking a source in the Scope column narrowing the Activity stream (today it only opens Detail).

## Current Limitations

- Retrieval on SQLite uses keyword/FTS-compatible CJK handling plus a bounded float32 matrix/scale index. PostgreSQL uses `pg_trgm`/`ILIKE` and the same byte-oriented float32 vectors behind repository ports; pgvector remains a future scale option, not a runtime prerequisite.
- Large-document ingestion is hardened: greedy-window KG extraction (cost scales linearly with document size), concurrent embedding with per-batch DB writes, and extraction-first pipeline. For very large corpora, adding `sqlite-vec` is a natural next step.
- Ask no longer performs synchronous embedding backfill or a full source-element scan; it uses available keyword/vector indexes and stays responsive while maintenance jobs run. Ask emits per-stage timing (`ask_stage` events).
- Unified KG rebuild is explicit and observable via `GET /notebooks/{id}/unified-kg/status`; ingesting a source marks the graph dirty instead of rebuilding synchronously, and opening the graph overlay no longer auto-rebuilds (refresh on demand).
- Cross-document concept merge uses deterministic alias normalization plus bounded top-k vector candidates (scales past thousands of concepts); optional LLM pre-review (`POST /notebooks/{id}/unified-kg/merges/review`) confirms/rejects high-confidence near-synonym merges in small batches.
- LLM-backed KG extraction requires the `kg_extract` workload to be bound in the system model-service TOML; offline smoke tests seed KG objects explicitly when retrieval/governance assertions are needed.
- Two-tier federation is early: marking a notebook `base`/`personal` (via `POST /notebooks/{id}/tier`), the edge-trust review queue, and promotion (personal→base) all now have dedicated front-end controls in the analysis toolbar; publishing a notebook as a public knowledge base only makes it mountable — tier-aware federation and the base-wins conflict rule activate only for notebooks that explicitly mount it as a reference library.
- Notebook sharing is link-based copy, read-only membership, or group sharing — not live collaborative editing. Group members may ask questions and write their own deep reports; content management (sources, graph, authorization edges) stays with the owner, and the group-admin write tier is P2.
- PostgreSQL is the default deployment choice for development and production; SQLite/PostgreSQL selection is direct and atomic through the repository factory. Changing `DATABASE_URL` does not synchronize existing rows; cutover and rollback therefore require stopped writers, verified backups, an external data migration when data already exists, and post-start consistency checks.
- The `off`-mode PDF fallback uses PyMuPDF4LLM page-chunked Markdown to retain headings, multi-column reading order and reconstructed tables; pypdf is only the last resort if that parser is unavailable or errors. MinerU still provides the authoritative high-fidelity formula/image/complex-scan path. A cloud URL/file parse that fails after retries uses the same local fallback and returns an extracted source with `parse_quality_warning=true`; the source detail explains the risk and offers reparse/delete actions. A later successful MinerU reparse clears the warning. See [PDF parsing with MinerU](./operations.md#pdf-parsing-with-mineru).
- User memory remains manual opt-in only; no automatic memory behavior has been added.
- A PostgreSQL query cancellation (`psycopg.errors.QueryCanceled` — statement timeout or an administrative cancel) that reaches the top of the request stack on a non-streaming response returns a structured `503` (`detail` plus a machine-readable `code: "query_timeout"`) and emits a `query_timeout` event carrying the paired `kind=http` row's request id, method/path and, when the route names one, `notebook_id` — instead of falling through to a bare, unobservable `500`. On a streaming response that has already started, no status code can be rewritten — the stream aborts, but the same `query_timeout` event (marked `streaming: true`) is still emitted from an outermost ASGI observer. The frontend still shows its existing generic 5xx "service unavailable" copy (no new user-facing text ships; `frontend/app/errors.ts` deliberately generalizes every 5xx). The pre-existing savepoint-bounded probes (e.g. the chunk lexical-recall budget in `knowledge_store.py`) are unaffected — they catch and convert their own `QueryCanceled` into a domain-specific exception before it ever reaches this handler.


## External authentication

The optional `auth.provider` deployment plugin authenticates external identities; core retains site users, sessions and resource authorization. The W3 example lives in `examples/extensions/w3-auth`, is independently packageable and is disabled by default. It is an OAuth2 code/userinfo adapter, not an assertion of OIDC support or verified connectivity to a real IDaaS.

**The switch.** External authentication is on exactly when the deployment configures an `auth.provider` plugin, that plugin is enabled (the host's provider description is non-empty) and the callback configuration is valid. There is no persisted stage or administrator-driven migration state. Disabling the plugin returns the site to local login; that is the emergency path. An invalid configuration (for example `AUTH_OPTIONAL`, a public/frontend origin mismatch, or a non-HTTPS production callback without `AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP`) is reported as a startup/capability error and never silently degrades to local login.

**Precheck before switching on (lockout guard).** Before an administrator **enables** a plugin that provides `auth.provider` through `PATCH /admin/extensions/{plugin_id}`, the deployment configuration above is checked as if that plugin were enabled (`AUTH_OPTIONAL` forbidden, `AUTH_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` required, frontend and callback origins on the same scheme and host, https in production unless `AUTH_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP`), and the site must have at least one administrator with `status='active'`, `role='admin'` who is not `user-local` (the built-in administrator cannot sign in under external authentication). Any failure returns 409 with a Chinese explanation and writes no switch row. Disabling is never restricted. The way back when actually locked out is in the [operations guide](./operations.md#external-authentication-enablement-and-rollback): disable the plugin in the deployment configuration and restart.

**Identity key.** The only key is `users.username == identity.username` (the provider's username, i.e. the employee number), compared exactly and case-sensitively. There is no `(namespace, subject)` mapping table; `subject` and namespace are written only to the session columns (`auth_sessions.external_subject` / `provider_namespace`) and to audit rows. The anonymous `user-local` account of `AUTH_OPTIONAL` can never be matched, linked or created. A provider username is validated by the same rule as an administrator rename (non-empty, no surrounding whitespace, no control characters, within the length rail); an identity that fails it is refused at the callback.

**Linked mark.** `users.sso_linked_at` records when the account first signed in through external authentication (written on a direct login when still empty, and on a successful link or a creation). An account carrying it can no longer be linked by anyone through its password; neither an administrator rename nor a password reset clears it.

**Login flow.**

1. `POST /auth/sso/start` begins the login; the callback returns to the frontend with a one-time handoff code, then `POST /auth/sso/complete {code}` decides:
   - An account with `username` equal to the provider username exists and is active: an SSO session is issued (`status: "authenticated"`) and `sso_linked_at` is written when empty. A non-active account returns `account_inactive`.
   - No such account: `status: "choice_required"` with `pending_id`, `external_username` and `display_name`. The pending choice is stored as a one-time authentication transaction (TTL `AUTH_TRANSACTION_TTL_SECONDS`) bound to the browser proof cookie.
2. The user then picks one of:
   - **Link an old account** (`POST /auth/sso/link`): enter the old account's username and password. An unknown name and a wrong password return the same `link_verification_failed` message and do not consume the pending choice, so the user may retry. The old account must be active (otherwise `account_inactive`), not `user-local` (`link_target_invalid`) and have a local password; **after** the password check passes, an old account that already carries `sso_linked_at` returns `link_target_linked` ("该账号已关联过统一认证账号，不能再关联；如有疑问请联系管理员。"), while a wrong password still returns `link_verification_failed`, so whether the account was linked never leaks. In one write transaction the service rechecks that no account named after the provider username has appeared meanwhile (otherwise `stale_transaction`), renames the old account to the provider username (keeping its user ID, data and role; the display name takes the provider value when non-empty), writes `sso_linked_at`, bumps its `auth_revision`, deletes all of its older sessions, audits `sso_linked` and issues an SSO session.
   - **Do not link, use a new account** (`POST /auth/sso/create`): after the same recheck, creates an ordinary `user` with no password (carrying `sso_linked_at`) named after the provider username, audits `sso_created`, issues a session and consumes the choice. The UI states that data of the old account will not appear in the new one.
   - When the employee number differs from another existing account only by letter case, linking a different account or creating one returns `username_case_conflict` ("本站已有只差大小写的同名账号，请选择「关联老账号」并输入该账号的密码。"); other conflicts, such as the built-in administrator's name, return `username_conflict`.
   - Status codes: when the pending choice is spent -- `invalid_transaction` (expired, used or a different browser), `stale_transaction`, `external_auth_expired` -- link and create return **410**, and the frontend locks the form and offers only "back to login"; every other link/create error is 409. The Chinese messages do not depend on the status code.
   - **Back to login** (`POST /auth/sso/cancel`, 204) discards the pending choice.
3. There is no self-service re-linking after choosing a new account; the user asks an administrator (below).

OAuth state, browser proof (a host-only HttpOnly SameSite cookie), PKCE when supported, Origin validation and the one-time handoff are core-owned. External access tokens remain within the provider call. The callback URL contains only a short-lived handoff code. SSO sessions have an absolute limit measured from verified external authentication (`AUTH_SSO_SESSION_SECONDS`); sliding access cannot extend it. Browser-authenticated NDJSON/SSE delivery rechecks sessions before every emitted frame. The `/mcp` transport retains its own per-request and per-tool Agent checks; Agent owner eligibility depends only on `users.status = 'active'`, token rows are retained, and an already committed write can still return its terminal acknowledgement after revocation while subsequent access is denied. Browser absolute expiry alone is not an IDaaS offboarding signal: operators must establish the provider's subject stability, non-reassignment and offboarding procedure.

**Local credentials while it is on.** `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/register` and a user's own password change are refused with 403 ("已启用统一认证，请使用统一认证登录"). Existing `auth_source = 'local'` sessions stop resolving, so the frontend returns to the login page. An administrator's password reset stays available: a user who forgot the old password gets a reset and can then complete the link step. With the switch off, local login behaves exactly as before.

**Frontend.** The login page uses `GET /auth/capabilities` to select its controls: when `sso_login` is true only the "log in with {provider_label}" button is shown; otherwise the local login/registration form. Only an absent endpoint (404) permits a local-login fallback. A saved bearer is restored independently of provider readiness. SSO login preserves a validated same-site return location (including invitation queries and notebook hashes) and consumes it after completion; external return locations are rejected. Sessions are synchronised across tabs through the storage listener.

**Administrator tools** (on the existing `/admin/users` list; both delete the user's sessions, bump `auth_revision` and are audited):

- `PATCH /admin/users/{id}/status {status: "active" | "disabled"}` enables or disables an account.
- `PATCH /admin/users/{id}/username {username}` renames an account: unique case-insensitively (a clash with another account is 409 "用户名已被占用"). "Case" means ASCII letters only, everywhere a name is compared (uniqueness, local login, the link step): `Ä123` and `ä123` are different names, and an account renamed to `Ä123` logs in or is linked with exactly that spelling; the name must be non-empty, without surrounding whitespace or control characters and within the length rail (otherwise 400). A rename keeps `sso_linked_at` and the account's placeholder email; registering the account's old name afterwards gets the ordinary "用户名已被占用" (400), not a constraint error.
- Neither may target **the signed-in administrator themselves** (409 "不能修改当前登录的账号") nor **change `user-local`'s status or username** (409 "内置管理员账号不可修改"); a non-administrator gets 403 and a missing target 404.

**Merging a unified-login account** (`POST /admin/users/{id}/merge-sso-account {username}`; in the UI it lives in the "管理" popover behind a two-click "合并" → "确认合并" confirmation): `{id}` is the old account to keep and `username` the unified-login account to delete (named after the employee number, looked up ASCII case-insensitively). In one write transaction the deleted account is **physically removed** together with its own sessions, profile, model-service status and clarification handles; the old account takes the deleted account's username (exact spelling) and display name, gets `sso_linked_at` set to now if it was empty (an existing value is kept), has `auth_revision` bumped and all its sessions deleted (the user signs in again, after which unified login matches the old account directly by employee number); audits `account_merged` (target: the old account) and `account_removed` (target: the deleted account's id). Returns `{id, username, status, removed_user_id}`.
- **The merge is allowed only while the deleted account owns no data at all**: nothing is migrated and nothing is cascaded. Otherwise it returns 409 with `detail` `{code: "merge_source_has_data", message, items: [{label, unit, count}]}` (e.g. "该账号名下已有数据，不能合并删除：笔记本 2 个、提问记录 3 条") and writes nothing; the UI lists each category and count beside the button. Which columns count as data is registered in `backend/app/repositories/user_references.py`; a guard test aligns every user-reference column of the migrated schema on both databases with that registry.
- Other 409s: no account has that username ("找不到用户名为该值的账号"), both sides are the same account ("不能把账号合并到它自己"), the account to delete never signed in through unified authentication (`sso_linked_at` empty, "只能合并已经用统一认证登录过的账号"), the old account is disabled ("保留的账号已停用，请先启用"); either side being the signed-in administrator or `user-local` gets the same copy as the two tools above. An invalid username is 400, a missing old account 404, a non-administrator 403.

Both situations that need an administrator's correction use this merge:
- **A mistaken "new account" choice**: the person forgot the old password at the unified login and created an empty account named after the employee number.
- **An employee-number change**: when the company changes numbers (e.g. `h00123456` → `h00234567`) the provider's `subject` usually changes too, and the system does not recognize the same person by subject; the old account already carries `sso_linked_at`, so the new number cannot link it (`link_target_linked`) and can only create a new account.

In both, the administrator merges the newly created account into the old one, leaving only the old account (all its data, the new number as username). When the account to delete already owns data, the manual fallback is: disable the new account and rename it to something else (freeing the employee number), then rename the old account to the employee number; the old account's next external login signs in directly (writing `sso_linked_at` then). Account status is rechecked for Agent authentication and each data-tool call.

All routes below are under `/api`. Public routes still enforce their transaction purpose and browser proof; ordinary extension routes remain session protected.

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /auth/capabilities` | `{sso_login, local_login, local_registration, provider_label}`; with SSO on, local login and registration are false |
| `POST /auth/sso/start` | Begin external login; returns `authorization_url` |
| `GET /auth/sso/callback` | Fixed callback; validates state/proof and exchanges the code through the provider |
| `POST /auth/sso/complete` | `{code}`; returns `authenticated` token/user or `choice_required` |
| `POST /auth/sso/link` | `{pending_id, login_name, password}`; verifies the old account, renames it to the employee number, returns token/user; 410 when the pending choice is spent, 409 for `link_verification_failed`, `link_target_linked`, `username_case_conflict` and other errors |
| `POST /auth/sso/create` | `{pending_id}`; creates a passwordless ordinary user, returns token/user; 410 when the pending choice is spent, otherwise 409 |
| `POST /auth/sso/cancel` | `{pending_id}`; 204, discards the pending choice |
| `PATCH /admin/users/{id}/status` | Administrator-only enable/disable; not on oneself, not on `user-local` (both 409) |
| `PATCH /admin/users/{id}/username` | Administrator-only rename; unique case-insensitively; not oneself, not `user-local` (both 409) |
| `POST /admin/users/{id}/merge-sso-account` | `{username}`, administrator-only; deletes the unified-login account with that username and gives old account `{id}` its name; 409 `merge_source_has_data` (with `items`) while the deleted account owns data, other refusals 409/404/400 |
| `PATCH /admin/extensions/{plugin_id}` | Enabling a plugin that provides `auth.provider` runs the lockout precheck first; failure is 409 with no row written; disabling is unrestricted |

Core authentication rails (reject over-limit input; never truncate identities):

| Setting/constant | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AUTH_TRANSACTION_TTL_SECONDS` | Default 600; 60–1800 seconds |
| `AUTH_SSO_SESSION_SECONDS` | Default 28800; 300–86400 seconds |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Default 15; greater than 0, at most 60 seconds |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_ID_MAX_CHARS` | 128 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_NAMESPACE_MAX_CHARS` | 256 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_CONFIGURATION_GENERATION_MAX_CHARS` | 128 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_PUBLIC_LABEL_MAX_CHARS` | 80 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_ENDPOINT_MAX_CHARS` | 2048 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_SUBJECT_MAX_CHARS` | 512 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_USERNAME_MAX_CHARS` | 512 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_DISPLAY_NAME_MAX_CHARS` | 512 |
| `AUTH_PROVIDER_AUTHORIZATION_URL_MAX_CHARS` | 8192 |

The host admits one provider; it bounds simultaneous provider workers and rejects late results. A timed-out trusted plugin can retain its worker slot until its call returns. Provider transport-specific limits belong to the example's README pair. Installation, enabling and rollback are owned by the deployment and operations references.
